Testing a pre-trained 3D pose estimator on a new dataset results in a major performance drop. Previous methods have mainly addressed this problem by improving the diversity of the training data. We argue that diversity alone is not sufficient and that the characteristics of the training data need to be adapted to those of the new dataset such as camera viewpoint, position, human actions, and body size. To this end, we propose AdaptPose, an end-to-end framework that generates synthetic 3D human motions from a source dataset and uses them to fine-tune a 3D pose estimator. AdaptPose follows an adversarial training scheme. From a source 3D pose the generator generates a sequence of 3D poses and a camera orientation that is used to project the generated poses to a novel view. Without any 3D labels or camera information AdaptPose successfully learns to create synthetic 3D poses from the target dataset while only being trained on 2D poses. In experiments on the Human3.6M, MPI-INF-3DHP, 3DPW, and Ski-Pose datasets our method outperforms previous work in cross-dataset evaluations by 14% and previous semi-supervised learning methods that use partial 3D annotations by 16%.

title: AdaptPose: Cross-Dataset Adaptation for 3D Human Pose Estimation by Learnable Motion Generation
text: Estimating 3D human pose from 2D images remains a challenging task, particularly when dealing with datasets captured under different conditions. This discrepancy in data distributions often leads to poor performance when models are deployed in new, unseen environments. Recent approaches have attempted to address this issue by leveraging domain adaptation techniques, but they typically rely on access to target domain data or require explicit domain labels. In this work, we propose AdaptPose, a novel framework that enables cross-dataset adaptation for 3D human pose estimation without requiring any target domain data or domain labels. Our approach leverages learnable motion generation to synthesize new poses that are likely to appear in the target domain, thereby bridging the gap between the source and target distributions. We demonstrate the effectiveness of AdaptPose on several benchmark datasets, including Human3.6M, MPI-INF-3DHP, and 3DPW, and show significant improvements over state-of-the-art methods in terms of 3D pose estimation accuracy. Notably, our approach achieves an average improvement of 14.4% in MPJPE on the 3DPW dataset when adapting from Human3.6M. We further analyze the generated motions and provide insights into the adaptation process, highlighting the potential of our approach for real-world applications where data distribution shifts are common.

title: Log severity level classification: an approach for systems in production
text: Context: Logs are often the primary source of information for system developers and operations engineers to understand and diagnose the behavior of a software system in production. In many cases, logs are the only evidence available for fault investigation. Problem: However, the inappropriate choice of log severity level can impact the amount of log data generated and, consequently, quality. This storage overhead can impact the performance of log-based monitoring systems, as excess log data comes with increased aggregate noise, making it challenging to utilize what is actually important when trying to do diagnostics. Goal: This research aims to decrease the overheads of monitoring systems by processing the severity level of log data from systems in production. Approach: To achieve this goal, we intend to deepen the knowledge about the log severity levels and develop an automated approach to log severity level classification, demonstrating that reducing log severity level "noise" improves the monitoring of systems in production. Conclusion: We hope that the set of contributions from this work can improve the monitoring activities of software systems and contribute to the creation of knowledge that improves logging practices

title: Log severity level classification: an approach for systems in production
text: The availability of logs is crucial for system developers and operations engineers to comprehend and diagnose software system behavior in production environments, often serving as the sole evidence for fault investigation. Nevertheless, the selection of log severity levels can have a profound impact on the volume of generated log data, ultimately influencing its quality. The ensuing storage overhead can compromise the performance of log-based monitoring systems, as excessive log data introduces aggregate noise, rendering it challenging to discern pertinent information during diagnostic efforts. This research endeavors to mitigate these overheads by refining the processing of log severity levels from production systems. To achieve this, we seek to advance the understanding of log severity levels and develop an automated classification approach, demonstrating that the reduction of log severity level "noise" enhances the monitoring of production systems. By doing so, we anticipate that our contributions will improve software system monitoring activities and inform logging practices.

title: EyePAD++: A Distillation-based approach for joint Eye Authentication and Presentation Attack Detection using Periocular Images
text: A practical eye authentication (EA) system targeted for edge devices needs to perform authentication and be robust to presentation attacks, all while remaining compute and latency efficient. However, existing eye-based frameworks a) perform authentication and Presentation Attack Detection (PAD) independently and b) involve significant pre-processing steps to extract the iris region. Here, we introduce a joint framework for EA and PAD using periocular images. While a deep Multitask Learning (MTL) network can perform both the tasks, MTL suffers from the forgetting effect since the training datasets for EA and PAD are disjoint. To overcome this, we propose Eye Authentication with PAD (EyePAD), a distillation-based method that trains a single network for EA and PAD while reducing the effect of forgetting. To further improve the EA performance, we introduce a novel approach called EyePAD++ that includes training an MTL network on both EA and PAD data, while distilling the `versatility' of the EyePAD network through an additional distillation step. Our proposed methods outperform the SOTA in PAD and obtain near-SOTA performance in eye-to-eye verification, without any pre-processing. We also demonstrate the efficacy of EyePAD and EyePAD++ in user-to-user verification with PAD across network backbones and image quality.

title: EyePAD++: A Distillation-based approach for joint Eye Authentication and Presentation Attack Detection using Periocular Images
text: Robust eye authentication (EA) on edge devices necessitates the concurrent achievement of authentication and presentation attack detection (PAD) while maintaining computational efficiency and low latency. Existing eye-based frameworks are limited by their independent treatment of EA and PAD, as well as the need for extensive preprocessing to extract the iris region. This work presents a unified framework for EA and PAD using periocular images, leveraging a deep multitask learning (MTL) network to perform both tasks jointly. However, MTL is susceptible to the forgetting effect due to the disjoint nature of EA and PAD training datasets. To mitigate this, we introduce Eye Authentication with PAD (EyePAD), a distillation-based approach that trains a single network for EA and PAD, minimizing the forgetting effect. Moreover, we propose EyePAD++, which further enhances EA performance by distilling the versatility of the EyePAD network through an additional step. Our methods surpass state-of-the-art PAD performance and achieve near-state-of-the-art eye-to-eye verification without preprocessing, demonstrating efficacy in user-to-user verification with PAD across various network backbones and image qualities.

title: MOSAIC: Mobile Segmentation via decoding Aggregated Information and encoded Context
text: We present a next-generation neural network architecture, MOSAIC, for efficient and accurate semantic image segmentation on mobile devices. MOSAIC is designed using commonly supported neural operations by diverse mobile hardware platforms for flexible deployment across various mobile platforms. With a simple asymmetric encoder-decoder structure which consists of an efficient multi-scale context encoder and a light-weight hybrid decoder to recover spatial details from aggregated information, MOSAIC achieves new state-of-the-art performance while balancing accuracy and computational cost. Deployed on top of a tailored feature extraction backbone based on a searched classification network, MOSAIC achieves a 5% absolute accuracy gain surpassing the current industry standard MLPerf models and state-of-the-art architectures.

title: MOSAIC: Mobile Segmentation via decoding Aggregated Information and encoded Context
text: We introduce MOSAIC, a novel neural network architecture optimized for efficient and accurate semantic image segmentation on mobile devices. By leveraging a set of neural operations widely supported across diverse mobile hardware platforms, MOSAIC ensures flexible deployment capabilities. Its asymmetric encoder-decoder design incorporates a multi-scale context encoder and a lightweight hybrid decoder, enabling the recovery of spatial details from aggregated information. This architecture achieves state-of-the-art performance, striking a balance between accuracy and computational cost. When integrated with a tailored feature extraction backbone derived from a searched classification network, MOSAIC yields a 5% absolute accuracy gain, outperforming current industry standards and state-of-the-art models.

title: Convolutional neural network based on transfer learning for breast cancer screening
text: Breast cancer is the most common cancer in the world and the most prevalent cause of death among women worldwide. Nevertheless, it is also one of the most treatable malignancies if detected early. In this paper, a deep convolutional neural network-based algorithm is proposed to aid in accurately identifying breast cancer from ultrasonic images. In this algorithm, several neural networks are fused in a parallel architecture to perform the classification process and the voting criteria are applied in the final classification decision between the candidate object classes where the output of each neural network is representing a single vote. Several experiments were conducted on the breast ultrasound dataset consisting of 537 Benign, 360 malignant, and 133 normal images. These experiments show an optimistic result and a capability of the proposed model to outperform many state-of-the-art algorithms on several measures. Using k-fold cross-validation and a bagging classifier ensemble, we achieved an accuracy of 99.5% and a sensitivity of 99.6%.

title: Convolutional neural network based on transfer learning for breast cancer screening
text: Breast cancer, the leading cause of mortality among women globally, can be effectively treated if diagnosed at an early stage. The development of accurate diagnostic tools is crucial for improving patient outcomes. This study proposes a novel deep convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture for breast cancer identification from ultrasonic images. The proposed algorithm employs a parallel fusion of multiple neural networks, where each network's output serves as a single vote in the final classification decision. Experimental evaluations on a dataset comprising 537 benign, 360 malignant, and 133 normal images demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed model, outperforming several state-of-the-art algorithms across various metrics. Notably, the model achieves an accuracy of 99.5% and a sensitivity of 99.6% when combined with k-fold cross-validation and a bagging classifier ensemble, highlighting its potential for clinical applications.

title: Breaking the Rate-Loss Bound of Quantum Key Distribution with Asynchronous Two-Photon Interference
text: Twin-field quantum key distribution can overcome the secret key capacity of repeaterless quantum key distribution via single-photon interference. However, to compensate for the channel fluctuations and lock the laser fluctuations, the techniques of phase tracking and phase locking are indispensable in experiment, which drastically increase experimental complexity and hinder free-space realization. Inspired by the duality in entanglement, we herein present an asynchronous measurement-device-independent quantum key distribution protocol that can surpass the secret key capacity even without phase tracking and phase locking. Leveraging the concept of time multiplexing, asynchronous two-photon Bell-state measurement is realized by postmatching two interference detection events. For a 1 GHz system, the new protocol reaches a transmission distance of 450 km without phase tracking. After further removing phase locking, our protocol is still capable of breaking the capacity at 270 km. Intriguingly, when using the same experimental techniques, our protocol has a higher key rate than the phase-matching-type twin-field protocol. In the presence of imperfect intensity modulation, it also has a significant advantage in terms of the transmission distance over the sending-or-not-sending type twin-field protocol. With high key rates and accessible technology, our work provides a promising candidate for practical scalable quantum communication networks.

title: Breaking the Rate-Loss Bound of Quantum Key Distribution with Asynchronous Two-Photon Interference
text: By harnessing the principles of entanglement duality, we develop a novel asynchronous measurement-device-independent quantum key distribution protocol that transcends the secret key capacity of repeaterless quantum key distribution without relying on phase tracking and phase locking. This achievement is made possible by the implementation of time multiplexing, which enables asynchronous two-photon Bell-state measurement through postmatching of interference detection events. Our protocol demonstrates a remarkable transmission distance of 450 km in a 1 GHz system, even without phase tracking. Furthermore, by eliminating the need for phase locking, our protocol still achieves a capacity-breaking distance of 270 km. Notably, our approach outperforms the phase-matching-type twin-field protocol in terms of key rate, using the same experimental techniques. Moreover, in the presence of imperfect intensity modulation, our protocol exhibits a significant advantage in transmission distance over the sending-or-not-sending type twin-field protocol. With its high key rates and accessible technology, our work presents a promising solution for practical, scalable quantum communication networks.

title: JoJoGAN: One Shot Face Stylization
text: A style mapper applies some fixed style to its input images (so, for example, taking faces to cartoons). This paper describes a simple procedure -- JoJoGAN -- to learn a style mapper from a single example of the style. JoJoGAN uses a GAN inversion procedure and StyleGAN's style-mixing property to produce a substantial paired dataset from a single example style. The paired dataset is then used to fine-tune a StyleGAN. An image can then be style mapped by GAN-inversion followed by the fine-tuned StyleGAN. JoJoGAN needs just one reference and as little as 30 seconds of training time. JoJoGAN can use extreme style references (say, animal faces) successfully. Furthermore, one can control what aspects of the style are used and how much of the style is applied. Qualitative and quantitative evaluation show that JoJoGAN produces high quality high resolution images that vastly outperform the current state-of-the-art.

title: JoJoGAN: One Shot Face Stylization
text: Face stylization, a fundamental task in computer vision, aims to transfer the style of a reference face image to a target face while preserving its identity. Existing methods either rely on explicit 3D face reconstruction or require extensive training datasets, limiting their applicability and flexibility. We propose JoJoGAN, a one-shot face stylization framework that tackles these limitations by leveraging a novel, hybrid architecture combining a style encoder, a face reconstruction module, and a generative adversarial network. Our approach enables stylization of unseen faces with a single reference image, eliminating the need for large training datasets. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate JoJoGAN's superior performance, achieving state-of-the-art results in terms of stylization quality, identity preservation, and robustness to varying pose and illumination conditions. Furthermore, our method exhibits impressive generalization capabilities, successfully stylizing faces from diverse domains and datasets.

title: Exploring Credibility Scoring Metrics of Perception Systems for Autonomous Driving
text: Autonomous and semi-autonomous vehicles' perception algorithms can encounter situations with erroneous object detection, such as misclassification of objects on the road, which can lead to safety violations and potentially fatal consequences. While there has been substantial work in the robustness of object detection algorithms and online metric learning, there is little research on benchmarking scoring metrics to determine any possible indicators of potential misclassification. An emphasis is put on exploring the potential of taking these scoring metrics online in order to allow the AV to make perception-based decisions given real-time constraints. In this work, we explore which, if any, metrics act as online indicators of when perception algorithms and object detectors are failing. Our work provides insight on better design principles and characteristics of online metrics to accurately evaluate the credibility of object detectors. Our approach employs non-adversarial and realistic perturbations to images, on which we evaluate various quantitative metrics. We found that offline metrics can be designed to account for real-world corruptions such as poor weather conditions and that the analysis of such metrics can provide a segue into designing online metrics. This is a clear next step as it can allow for error-free autonomous vehicle perception and safer time-critical and safety-critical decision-making.

title: Exploring Credibility Scoring Metrics of Perception Systems for Autonomous Driving
text: The proliferation of autonomous driving systems has heightened concerns about the reliability of perception systems, which are critical to safe and efficient navigation. A key challenge lies in quantifying the credibility of sensor data and perception outputs, as inaccuracies can have devastating consequences. This paper presents a comprehensive investigation into credibility scoring metrics for perception systems in autonomous driving, focusing on computer vision-based approaches. We formulate a novel credibility scoring framework that integrates both data-driven and model-driven metrics, capturing various aspects of perception system performance, including sensor reliability, environmental factors, and algorithmic confidence. Our methodology involves a large-scale evaluation of state-of-the-art perception models on diverse datasets, incorporating real-world and synthetic scenarios. The results show that our proposed framework outperforms existing approaches in terms of accuracy and robustness, with a mean absolute error reduction of 23.4% in credibility scoring. Furthermore, we analyze the impact of credibility scoring on downstream autonomous driving tasks, such as object detection and tracking, and demonstrate significant improvements in system performance. Our work provides a foundation for the development of more reliable and trustworthy perception systems, ultimately contributing to the widespread adoption of autonomous vehicles.

title: Out-of-distribution Detection with Boundary Aware Learning
text: There is an increasing need to determine whether inputs are out-of-distribution (\emph{OOD}) for safely deploying machine learning models in the open world scenario. Typical neural classifiers are based on the closed world assumption, where the training data and the test data are drawn \emph{i.i.d.} from the same distribution, and as a result, give over-confident predictions even faced with \emph{OOD} inputs. For tackling this problem, previous studies either use real outliers for training or generate synthetic \emph{OOD} data under strong assumptions, which are either costly or intractable to generalize. In this paper, we propose boundary aware learning (\textbf{BAL}), a novel framework that can learn the distribution of \emph{OOD} features adaptively. The key idea of BAL is to generate \emph{OOD} features from trivial to hard progressively with a generator, meanwhile, a discriminator is trained for distinguishing these synthetic \emph{OOD} features and in-distribution (\emph{ID}) features. Benefiting from the adversarial training scheme, the discriminator can well separate \emph{ID} and \emph{OOD} features, allowing more robust \emph{OOD} detection. The proposed BAL achieves \emph{state-of-the-art} performance on classification benchmarks, reducing up to 13.9\% FPR95 compared with previous methods.

title: Out-of-distribution Detection with Boundary Aware Learning
text: The proliferation of deep neural networks in real-world applications has led to a growing concern about their robustness to out-of-distribution (OOD) inputs, which can cause unpredictable behavior and even safety risks. Existing OOD detection methods often rely on ad-hoc heuristics or require additional annotations, limiting their applicability. We propose Boundary Aware Learning (BAL), a novel approach that leverages the intrinsic structure of the decision boundary to detect OOD samples. By regularizing the model to produce high-confidence predictions near the boundary, BAL encourages the learning of a more informative and separable representation. Our method is simple to implement, requiring only minor modifications to the standard training protocol. On a range of benchmark datasets, including CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and SVHN, BAL consistently outperforms state-of-the-art OOD detection methods, achieving an average improvement of 12.5% in AUROC. Furthermore, we demonstrate the robustness of BAL to various types of distribution shifts and its applicability to real-world scenarios, such as medical image analysis. Our results suggest that BAL is a promising solution for reliable OOD detection in deep learning systems.

title: AED: An black-box NLP classifier model attacker
text: Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) have been successful in solving real-world tasks in domains such as connected and automated vehicles, disease, and job hiring. However, their implications are far-reaching in critical application areas. Hence, there is a growing concern regarding the potential bias and robustness of these DNN models. A transparency and robust model is always demanded in high-stakes domains where reliability and safety are enforced, such as healthcare and finance. While most studies have focused on adversarial image attack scenarios, fewer studies have investigated the robustness of DNN models in natural language processing (NLP) due to their adversarial samples are difficult to generate. To address this gap, we propose a word-level NLP classifier attack model called "AED," which stands for Attention mechanism enabled post-model Explanation with Density peaks clustering algorithm for synonyms search and substitution. AED aims to test the robustness of NLP DNN models by interpretability their weaknesses and exploring alternative ways to optimize them. By identifying vulnerabilities and providing explanations, AED can help improve the reliability and safety of DNN models in critical application areas such as healthcare and automated transportation. Our experiment results demonstrate that compared with other existing models, AED can effectively generate adversarial examples that can fool the victim model while maintaining the original meaning of the input.

title: AED: An black-box NLP classifier model attacker
text: The proliferation of Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) in high-stakes domains, such as healthcare and finance, has raised concerns about their potential biases and robustness. The demand for transparent and robust models is paramount in these areas, where reliability and safety are paramount. While research has primarily focused on adversarial image attacks, the robustness of DNN models in natural language processing (NLP) has received relatively little attention, likely due to the challenges of generating adversarial samples. To bridge this gap, we introduce AED, a word-level NLP classifier attack model that leverages attention mechanisms, post-model explanation, and density peaks clustering for synonym search and substitution. By identifying vulnerabilities and providing explanations, AED aims to test the robustness of NLP DNN models and explore opportunities for optimization. Our experimental results show that AED can effectively generate adversarial examples that deceive victim models while preserving the original input meaning, outperforming existing models. By doing so, AED can contribute to improving the reliability and safety of DNN models in critical application areas, such as healthcare and automated transportation.

title: Ghost-dil-NetVLAD: A Lightweight Neural Network for Visual Place Recognition
text: Visual place recognition (VPR) is a challenging task with the unbalance between enormous computational cost and high recognition performance. Thanks to the practical feature extraction ability of the lightweight convolution neural networks (CNNs) and the train-ability of the vector of locally aggregated descriptors (VLAD) layer, we propose a lightweight weakly supervised end-to-end neural network consisting of a front-ended perception model called GhostCNN and a learnable VLAD layer as a back-end. GhostCNN is based on Ghost modules that are lightweight CNN-based architectures. They can generate redundant feature maps using linear operations instead of the traditional convolution process, making a good trade-off between computation resources and recognition accuracy. To enhance our proposed lightweight model further, we add dilated convolutions to the Ghost module to get features containing more spatial semantic information, improving accuracy. Finally, rich experiments conducted on a commonly used public benchmark and our private dataset validate that the proposed neural network reduces the FLOPs and parameters of VGG16-NetVLAD by 99.04% and 80.16%, respectively. Besides, both models achieve similar accuracy.

title: Ghost-dil-NetVLAD: A Lightweight Neural Network for Visual Place Recognition
text: Visual Place Recognition (VPR) remains a crucial component in various robotics and computer vision applications, including autonomous navigation and simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM). Despite significant advancements, existing VPR methods struggle to balance accuracy and computational efficiency, particularly in resource-constrained scenarios. This paper introduces Ghost-dil-NetVLAD, a lightweight neural network designed to tackle this challenge. By leveraging a novel ghost module, which adaptively aggregates features from different scales, and a dilated convolutional layer, which captures long-range dependencies, our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance on popular VPR benchmarks. Notably, Ghost-dil-NetVLAD reduces the number of parameters by 75% compared to the current best method, NetVLAD, while maintaining a competitive accuracy. Our extensive experiments demonstrate the efficacy of our method in various environments, including daytime, nighttime, and seasonal changes. Furthermore, we provide an in-depth analysis of the ghost module's contribution to feature learning, shedding light on its role in improving VPR robustness.

title: Cost Aggregation Is All You Need for Few-Shot Segmentation
text: We introduce a novel cost aggregation network, dubbed Volumetric Aggregation with Transformers (VAT), to tackle the few-shot segmentation task by using both convolutions and transformers to efficiently handle high dimensional correlation maps between query and support. In specific, we propose our encoder consisting of volume embedding module to not only transform the correlation maps into more tractable size but also inject some convolutional inductive bias and volumetric transformer module for the cost aggregation. Our encoder has a pyramidal structure to let the coarser level aggregation to guide the finer level and enforce to learn complementary matching scores. We then feed the output into our affinity-aware decoder along with the projected feature maps for guiding the segmentation process. Combining these components, we conduct experiments to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, and our method sets a new state-of-the-art for all the standard benchmarks in few-shot segmentation task. Furthermore, we find that the proposed method attains state-of-the-art performance even for the standard benchmarks in semantic correspondence task although not specifically designed for this task. We also provide an extensive ablation study to validate our architectural choices. The trained weights and codes are available at:

title: Cost Aggregation Is All You Need for Few-Shot Segmentation
text: This paper presents Volumetric Aggregation with Transformers (VAT), a novel cost aggregation network designed to tackle few-shot segmentation tasks by leveraging the strengths of both convolutional and transformer-based architectures to efficiently process high-dimensional correlation maps between query and support sets. Our proposed encoder features a pyramidal structure, comprising a volume embedding module that transforms correlation maps into a more tractable size while injecting convolutional inductive bias, and a volumetric transformer module for cost aggregation. This design enables coarser-level aggregations to guide finer-level processing, promoting the learning of complementary matching scores. The output is fed into an affinity-aware decoder, along with projected feature maps, to guide the segmentation process. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of VAT, setting a new state-of-the-art on all standard benchmarks for few-shot segmentation tasks. Notably, VAT also achieves state-of-the-art performance on standard benchmarks for semantic correspondence tasks, despite not being specifically designed for this task. An extensive ablation study validates our architectural choices, providing insights into the network's design.

title: Multi-Centroid Representation Network for Domain Adaptive Person Re-ID
text: Recently, many approaches tackle the Unsupervised Domain Adaptive person re-identification (UDA re-ID) problem through pseudo-label-based contrastive learning. During training, a uni-centroid representation is obtained by simply averaging all the instance features from a cluster with the same pseudo label. However, a cluster may contain images with different identities (label noises) due to the imperfect clustering results, which makes the uni-centroid representation inappropriate. In this paper, we present a novel Multi-Centroid Memory (MCM) to adaptively capture different identity information within the cluster. MCM can effectively alleviate the issue of label noises by selecting proper positive/negative centroids for the query image. Moreover, we further propose two strategies to improve the contrastive learning process. First, we present a Domain-Specific Contrastive Learning (DSCL) mechanism to fully explore intradomain information by comparing samples only from the same domain. Second, we propose Second-Order Nearest Interpolation (SONI) to obtain abundant and informative negative samples. We integrate MCM, DSCL, and SONI into a unified framework named Multi-Centroid Representation Network (MCRN). Extensive experiments demonstrate the superiority of MCRN over state-of-the-art approaches on multiple UDA re-ID tasks and fully unsupervised re-ID tasks.

title: Multi-Centroid Representation Network for Domain Adaptive Person Re-ID
text: Unsupervised domain adaptation for person re-identification (Re-ID) remains a challenging task due to the lack of labeled data in the target domain. Existing methods often rely on a single centroid representation, which may not capture the complex distribution of the target domain. To address this limitation, we propose a novel Multi-Centroid Representation Network (MCRN) that learns to adapt to the target domain by discovering multiple centroids. Our approach leverages a clustering-based strategy to identify distinct clusters in the target domain, and each cluster is represented by a centroid. The MCRN model is trained to minimize the discrepancy between the source and target domains, while simultaneously encouraging the centroids to capture diverse aspects of the target domain. Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, achieving state-of-the-art performance on Market-1501, DukeMTMC-reID, and MSMT17 datasets. Specifically, our method yields an improvement of 4.3%, 3.5%, and 2.9% in terms of mAP, compared to the current state-of-the-art methods. The proposed MCRN provides a new perspective for domain adaptive person Re-ID and has the potential to be applied to other computer vision tasks.

title: Comprehensive Visual Question Answering on Point Clouds through Compositional Scene Manipulation
text: Visual Question Answering on 3D Point Cloud (VQA-3D) is an emerging yet challenging field that aims at answering various types of textual questions given an entire point cloud scene. To tackle this problem, we propose the CLEVR3D, a large-scale VQA-3D dataset consisting of 171K questions from 8,771 3D scenes. Specifically, we develop a question engine leveraging 3D scene graph structures to generate diverse reasoning questions, covering the questions of objects' attributes (i.e., size, color, and material) and their spatial relationships. Through such a manner, we initially generated 44K questions from 1,333 real-world scenes. Moreover, a more challenging setup is proposed to remove the confounding bias and adjust the context from a common-sense layout. Such a setup requires the network to achieve comprehensive visual understanding when the 3D scene is different from the general co-occurrence context (e.g., chairs always exist with tables). To this end, we further introduce the compositional scene manipulation strategy and generate 127K questions from 7,438 augmented 3D scenes, which can improve VQA-3D models for real-world comprehension. Built upon the proposed dataset, we baseline several VQA-3D models, where experimental results verify that the CLEVR3D can significantly boost other 3D scene understanding tasks. Our code and dataset will be made publicly available at

title: Comprehensive Visual Question Answering on Point Clouds through Compositional Scene Manipulation
text: The proliferation of 3D sensors has led to an exponential growth in point cloud data, necessitating the development of novel methods to facilitate intelligent scene understanding. Visual question answering (VQA) on point clouds is a burgeoning area of research, where the goal is to answer complex, open-ended questions about a scene using only the point cloud as input. However, existing methods struggle to generalize across diverse scenes and question types, often relying on simplistic, hand-crafted features that fail to capture the compositional structure of real-world environments. This work presents a comprehensive approach to VQA on point clouds, leveraging compositional scene manipulation to reason about complex scenes. Our methodology involves decomposing scenes into constituent objects and relationships, which are then manipulated to generate a rich, symbolic representation of the scene. This representation is used to answer a wide range of questions, from object detection and counting to spatial reasoning and event prediction. Our approach achieves state-of-the-art results on multiple benchmarks, including ScanQA and PointCloudQA, outperforming existing methods by up to 15% on certain question types. A thorough ablation study and human subject evaluation demonstrate the effectiveness of our compositional scene manipulation strategy in facilitating robust, generalizable VQA performance.

title: Few-Shot Object Detection: A Comprehensive Survey
text: Humans are able to learn to recognize new objects even from a few examples. In contrast, training deep-learning-based object detectors requires huge amounts of annotated data. To avoid the need to acquire and annotate these huge amounts of data, few-shot object detection aims to learn from few object instances of new categories in the target domain. In this survey, we provide an overview of the state of the art in few-shot object detection. We categorize approaches according to their training scheme and architectural layout. For each type of approaches, we describe the general realization as well as concepts to improve the performance on novel categories. Whenever appropriate, we give short takeaways regarding these concepts in order to highlight the best ideas. Eventually, we introduce commonly used datasets and their evaluation protocols and analyze reported benchmark results. As a result, we emphasize common challenges in evaluation and identify the most promising current trends in this emerging field of few-shot object detection.

title: Few-Shot Object Detection: A Comprehensive Survey
text: Object detection, a fundamental task in computer vision, has achieved remarkable progress with the advent of deep learning. However, most state-of-the-art detectors rely on large datasets and extensive training, limiting their applicability to real-world scenarios where data scarcity is prevalent. Few-shot object detection, which aims to detect objects with only a few annotated examples, has emerged as a promising solution. Despite its significance, the field lacks a comprehensive survey to consolidate existing knowledge and guide future research. This paper presents a thorough review of few-shot object detection, encompassing 120+ papers and covering key aspects such as problem formulations, benchmark datasets, and evaluation metrics. We categorize existing approaches into four paradigms: transfer learning, meta-learning, few-shot adaptation, and hybrid methods. Our analysis reveals that while meta-learning has shown impressive results, it often suffers from overfitting and high computational costs. We also identify key challenges and open issues, including the need for more realistic evaluation protocols and better handling of class imbalance.

title: Adaptive Contrast for Image Regression in Computer-Aided Disease Assessment
text: Image regression tasks for medical applications, such as bone mineral density (BMD) estimation and left-ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) prediction, play an important role in computer-aided disease assessment. Most deep regression methods train the neural network with a single regression loss function like MSE or L1 loss. In this paper, we propose the first contrastive learning framework for deep image regression, namely AdaCon, which consists of a feature learning branch via a novel adaptive-margin contrastive loss and a regression prediction branch. Our method incorporates label distance relationships as part of the learned feature representations, which allows for better performance in downstream regression tasks. Moreover, it can be used as a plug-and-play module to improve performance of existing regression methods. We demonstrate the effectiveness of AdaCon on two medical image regression tasks, ie, bone mineral density estimation from X-ray images and left-ventricular ejection fraction prediction from echocardiogram videos. AdaCon leads to relative improvements of 3.3% and 5.9% in MAE over state-of-the-art BMD estimation and LVEF prediction methods, respectively.

title: Adaptive Contrast for Image Regression in Computer-Aided Disease Assessment
text: Medical image regression tasks, such as estimating bone mineral density and predicting left-ventricular ejection fraction, are crucial for computer-aided disease diagnosis and assessment. Conventional deep regression methods rely on a single loss function, typically mean squared error or L1 loss, to train neural networks. We depart from this paradigm by introducing AdaCon, a novel contrastive learning framework for deep image regression. This framework comprises two branches: a feature learning branch, which leverages an adaptive-margin contrastive loss to capture label distance relationships, and a regression prediction branch. By incorporating these relationships into the learned feature representations, AdaCon enhances performance on downstream regression tasks. Furthermore, it can be seamlessly integrated into existing regression methods as a plug-and-play module to boost their performance. Experimental results on two medical image regression tasks demonstrate the efficacy of AdaCon, yielding relative improvements of 3.3% and 5.9% in mean absolute error over state-of-the-art methods for bone mineral density estimation and left-ventricular ejection fraction prediction, respectively.

title: Entropy Regularized Iterative Weighted Shrinkage-Thresholding Algorithm (ERIWSTA): An Application to CT Image Restoration
text: The iterative weighted shrinkage-thresholding algorithm (IWSTA) has shown superiority to the classic unweighted iterative shrinkage-thresholding algorithm (ISTA) for solving linear inverse problems, which address the attributes differently. This paper proposes a new entropy regularized IWSTA (ERIWSTA) that adds an entropy regularizer to the cost function to measure the uncertainty of the weights to stimulate attributes to participate in problem solving. Then, the weights are solved with a Lagrange multiplier method to obtain a simple iterative update. The weights can be explained as the probability of the contribution of an attribute to the problem solution. Experimental results on CT image restoration show that the proposed method has better performance in terms of convergence speed and restoration accuracy than the existing methods.

title: Entropy Regularized Iterative Weighted Shrinkage-Thresholding Algorithm (ERIWSTA): An Application to CT Image Restoration
text: Computed Tomography (CT) image restoration is a crucial task in medical imaging, as it enhances diagnostic accuracy and reduces radiation exposure. However, the presence of noise and artifacts in CT scans hinders image quality. To address this, we propose the Entropy Regularized Iterative Weighted Shrinkage-Thresholding Algorithm (ERIWSTA), a novel optimization framework that leverages the sparse nature of CT images. ERIWSTA integrates an entropy-based regularization term into the iterative weighted shrinkage-thresholding algorithm, promoting sparse solutions while adaptively adjusting the regularization strength. Experimental results on simulated and real CT datasets demonstrate that ERIWSTA outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of peak signal-to-noise ratio, structural similarity index, and visual information fidelity. Notably, ERIWSTA achieves a 2.5 dB improvement in PSNR compared to the current best approach, making it a promising tool for clinical CT image restoration.

title: Fusion of medical imaging and electronic health records with attention and multi-head machanisms
text: Doctors often make diagonostic decisions based on patient's image scans, such as magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and patient's electronic health records (EHR) such as age, gender, blood pressure and so on. Despite a lot of automatic methods have been proposed for either image or text analysis in computer vision or natural language research areas, much fewer studies have been developed for the fusion of medical image and EHR data for medical problems. Among existing early or intermediate fusion methods, concatenation of features from both modalities is still a mainstream. For a better exploiting of image and EHR data, we propose a multi-modal attention module which use EHR data to help the selection of important regions during image feature extraction process conducted by traditional CNN. Moreover, we propose to incorporate multi-head machnism to gated multimodal unit (GMU) to make it able to parallelly fuse image and EHR features in different subspaces. With the help of the two modules, existing CNN architecture can be enhanced using both modalities. Experiments on predicting Glasgow outcome scale (GOS) of intracerebral hemorrhage patients and classifying Alzheimer's Disease showed the proposed method can automatically focus on task-related areas and achieve better results by making better use of image and EHR features.

title: Fusion of medical imaging and electronic health records with attention and multi-head machanisms
text: The integration of medical imaging and electronic health records (EHRs) has the potential to revolutionize disease diagnosis and treatment by providing a more comprehensive understanding of patient health. However, existing approaches often rely on simple concatenation or early fusion of imaging and EHR data, neglecting the complex relationships between these modalities. To address this limitation, we propose a novel framework that leverages attention and multi-head mechanisms to fuse medical imaging and EHR data. Our approach, termed FusionNet, employs a multi-head self-attention module to model interactions between imaging and EHR features, allowing the model to selectively focus on relevant regions of interest and identify salient patterns. We evaluate FusionNet on a large-scale dataset of chest X-rays and corresponding EHRs, annotated with pneumonia diagnosis labels. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art fusion methods, achieving an absolute improvement of 4.2% in area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC) and 3.5% in area under the precision-recall curve (AUC-PR). Furthermore, visualization of attention weights reveals that FusionNet learns to attend to clinically relevant regions of the imaging data and EHR features, providing insights into the decision-making process. Our findings suggest that the proposed framework has the potential to improve disease diagnosis and patient outcomes by harnessing the complementary information contained in medical imaging and EHRs.

title: High-Accuracy RGB-D Face Recognition via Segmentation-Aware Face Depth Estimation and Mask-Guided Attention Network
text: Deep learning approaches have achieved highly accurate face recognition by training the models with very large face image datasets. Unlike the availability of large 2D face image datasets, there is a lack of large 3D face datasets available to the public. Existing public 3D face datasets were usually collected with few subjects, leading to the over-fitting problem. This paper proposes two CNN models to improve the RGB-D face recognition task. The first is a segmentation-aware depth estimation network, called DepthNet, which estimates depth maps from RGB face images by including semantic segmentation information for more accurate face region localization. The other is a novel mask-guided RGB-D face recognition model that contains an RGB recognition branch, a depth map recognition branch, and an auxiliary segmentation mask branch with a spatial attention module. Our DepthNet is used to augment a large 2D face image dataset to a large RGB-D face dataset, which is used for training an accurate RGB-D face recognition model. Furthermore, the proposed mask-guided RGB-D face recognition model can fully exploit the depth map and segmentation mask information and is more robust against pose variation than previous methods. Our experimental results show that DepthNet can produce more reliable depth maps from face images with the segmentation mask. Our mask-guided face recognition model outperforms state-of-the-art methods on several public 3D face datasets.

title: High-Accuracy RGB-D Face Recognition via Segmentation-Aware Face Depth Estimation and Mask-Guided Attention Network
text: Despite significant progress in RGB-D face recognition, existing methods often struggle to accurately estimate face depth and effectively leverage depth cues, resulting in subpar performance. To address these limitations, we propose a novel framework that integrates segmentation-aware face depth estimation and mask-guided attention networks to enhance RGB-D face recognition accuracy. Our approach first employs a segmentation-aware depth estimation module to generate a refined depth map, which is then utilized to guide a mask-guided attention network. This attention mechanism adaptively focuses on the most discriminative regions of the face, suppressing noisy or irrelevant features. We extensively evaluate our method on three benchmark datasets, including BUAA-VisNIR, CASIA-SURF, and NJU-3D, and demonstrate significant improvements over state-of-the-art methods. Specifically, our approach achieves an average recognition rate of 98.5% on BUAA-VisNIR, outperforming the best existing method by 2.1%. Furthermore, we conduct ablation studies to validate the effectiveness of our segmentation-aware depth estimation and mask-guided attention mechanisms, showing that each component contributes substantially to the overall performance gain. Our findings suggest that the proposed framework can effectively harness the rich information contained in RGB-D data to achieve high-accuracy face recognition, with potential applications in various fields, including security, healthcare, and human-computer interaction.

title: Comparing radiologists' gaze and saliency maps generated by interpretability methods for chest x-rays
text: The interpretability of medical image analysis models is considered a key research field. We use a dataset of eye-tracking data from five radiologists to compare the outputs of interpretability methods and the heatmaps representing where radiologists looked. We conduct a class-independent analysis of the saliency maps generated by two methods selected from the literature: Grad-CAM and attention maps from an attention-gated model. For the comparison, we use shuffled metrics, which avoid biases from fixation locations. We achieve scores comparable to an interobserver baseline in one shuffled metric, highlighting the potential of saliency maps from Grad-CAM to mimic a radiologist's attention over an image. We also divide the dataset into subsets to evaluate in which cases similarities are higher.

title: Comparing radiologists' gaze and saliency maps generated by interpretability methods for chest x-rays
text: Chest X-ray diagnosis relies heavily on visual inspection by radiologists, but the interpretation process remains poorly understood. Recent advances in interpretability methods have enabled the generation of saliency maps, which highlight regions contributing most to model predictions. We investigate the relationship between radiologists' gaze patterns and saliency maps generated by three popular interpretability methods: gradient-based saliency, attention-based saliency, and SHAP values. We collect gaze data from 10 radiologists interpreting 150 chest X-rays and compare it to saliency maps generated by each method. Our results show that gaze patterns are significantly correlated with attention-based saliency maps (r=0.64, p<0.01), but not with gradient-based saliency or SHAP values. These findings suggest that attention-based saliency maps may provide a more accurate representation of radiologists' visual attention and decision-making processes.

title: Towards Malicious address identification in Bitcoin
text: The temporal aspect of blockchain transactions enables us to study the address's behavior and detect if it is involved in any illicit activity. However, due to the concept of change addresses (used to thwart replay attacks), temporal aspects are not directly applicable in the Bitcoin blockchain. Several pre-processing steps should be performed before such temporal aspects are utilized. We are motivated to study the Bitcoin transaction network and use the temporal features such as burst, attractiveness, and inter-event time along with several graph-based properties such as the degree of node and clustering coefficient to validate the applicability of already existing approaches known for other cryptocurrency blockchains on the Bitcoin blockchain. We generate the temporal and non-temporal feature set and train the Machine Learning (ML) algorithm over different temporal granularities to validate the state-of-the-art methods. We study the behavior of the addresses over different time granularities of the dataset. We identify that after applying change-address clustering, in Bitcoin, existing temporal features can be extracted and ML approaches can be applied. A comparative analysis of results show that the behavior of addresses in Ethereum and Bitcoin is similar with respect to in-degree, out-degree and inter-event time. Further, we identify 3 suspects that showed malicious behavior across different temporal granularities. These suspects are not marked as malicious in Bitcoin.

title: Towards Malicious address identification in Bitcoin
text: The temporal dimension of blockchain transactions offers a valuable lens through which to examine address behavior and identify potential illicit activity. However, the use of change addresses in the Bitcoin blockchain, aimed at preventing replay attacks, complicates the direct application of temporal analysis. To overcome this limitation, we undertake a comprehensive study of the Bitcoin transaction network, combining temporal features such as burst, attractiveness, and inter-event time with graph-based properties like node degree and clustering coefficient. We generate a rich feature set, encompassing both temporal and non-temporal attributes, and train machine learning algorithms across diverse temporal granularities to assess the viability of approaches established in other cryptocurrency blockchains. Our analysis reveals that, following change-address clustering, existing temporal features can be successfully extracted from Bitcoin transactions, enabling the application of machine learning methods. A comparative examination of results underscores the similarity in address behavior between Ethereum and Bitcoin, with respect to in-degree, out-degree, and inter-event time. Notably, our study identifies three suspects exhibiting malicious behavior across multiple temporal granularities, which were not previously flagged as malicious in the Bitcoin ecosystem.

title: Generalized Local Optimality for Video Steganalysis in Motion Vector Domain
text: The local optimality of motion vectors (MVs) is an intrinsic property in video coding, and any modifications to the MVs will inevitably destroy this optimality, making it a sensitive indicator of steganography in the MV domain. Thus the local optimality is commonly used to design steganalytic features, and the estimation for local optimality has become a top priority in video steganalysis. However, the local optimality in existing works is often estimated inaccurately or using an unreasonable assumption, limiting its capability in steganalysis. In this paper, we propose to estimate the local optimality in a more reasonable and comprehensive fashion, and generalize the concept of local optimality in two aspects. First, the local optimality measured in a rate-distortion sense is jointly determined by MV and predicted motion vector (PMV), and the variability of PMV will affect the estimation for local optimality. Hence we generalize the local optimality from a static estimation to a dynamic one. Second, the PMV is a special case of MV, and can also reflect the embedding traces in MVs. So we generalize the local optimality from the MV domain to the PMV domain. Based on the two generalizations of local optimality, we construct new types of steganalytic features and also propose feature symmetrization rules to reduce feature dimension. Extensive experiments performed on three databases demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed features, which achieve state-of-the-art in both accuracy and robustness in various conditions, including cover source mismatch, video prediction methods, video codecs, and video resolutions.

title: Generalized Local Optimality for Video Steganalysis in Motion Vector Domain
text: Video steganalysis, the process of detecting hidden messages in videos, has gained significant attention in recent years due to the increasing threat of multimedia-based cyber attacks. While existing methods have shown promising results in the spatial and frequency domains, the motion vector domain remains relatively unexplored. This domain, however, offers a unique opportunity to leverage the temporal correlations inherent in video sequences. In this context, we propose a novel framework for video steganalysis in the motion vector domain, grounded in the concept of generalized local optimality. Our approach revolves around the observation that steganographic algorithms often introduce subtle perturbations in the motion vector field, which can be captured by a carefully designed local optimization strategy. We formulate the steganalysis problem as a binary classification task, where a deep neural network is trained to distinguish between stego and cover videos based on the optimized motion vector features. The proposed framework is extensively evaluated on several benchmark datasets, including the popular VideoSteg dataset, and demonstrates significant improvements over state-of-the-art methods in terms of detection accuracy and robustness. Notably, our approach achieves an average detection accuracy of 93.5% on the VideoSteg dataset, outperforming the current best method by 7.2%. Furthermore, we conduct an in-depth analysis of the learned features and provide insights into the underlying mechanisms that contribute to the superior performance of our approach. The proposed method has far-reaching implications for the development of robust video steganalysis systems and can be potentially extended to other multimedia forensic applications.

title: Simple and Effective Balance of Contrastive Losses
text: Contrastive losses have long been a key ingredient of deep metric learning and are now becoming more popular due to the success of self-supervised learning. Recent research has shown the benefit of decomposing such losses into two sub-losses which act in a complementary way when learning the representation network: a positive term and an entropy term. Although the overall loss is thus defined as a combination of two terms, the balance of these two terms is often hidden behind implementation details and is largely ignored and sub-optimal in practice. In this work, we approach the balance of contrastive losses as a hyper-parameter optimization problem, and propose a coordinate descent-based search method that efficiently find the hyper-parameters that optimize evaluation performance. In the process, we extend existing balance analyses to the contrastive margin loss, include batch size in the balance, and explain how to aggregate loss elements from the batch to maintain near-optimal performance over a larger range of batch sizes. Extensive experiments with benchmarks from deep metric learning and self-supervised learning show that optimal hyper-parameters are found faster with our method than with other common search methods.

title: Simple and Effective Balance of Contrastive Losses
text: The efficacy of contrastive losses in deep metric learning has been well-established, and their popularity has surged with the advent of self-supervised learning. Decomposing these losses into complementary positive and entropy terms has been shown to enhance representation learning. However, the balance between these terms, crucial for optimal performance, is often obscured by implementation details and suboptimal in practice. We reformulate the balance of contrastive losses as a hyperparameter optimization problem and propose a coordinate descent-based search method to efficiently identify the optimal hyperparameters that maximize evaluation performance. Our approach extends existing balance analyses to the contrastive margin loss and incorporates batch size as a critical factor, enabling near-optimal performance across a broad range of batch sizes. Through extensive experimentation on benchmarks from deep metric learning and self-supervised learning, we demonstrate that our method discovers optimal hyperparameters more rapidly than common search methods, thereby improving the overall efficiency of the learning process.

title: Security Risks of Porting C Programs to WebAssembly
text: WebAssembly is a compilation target for cross-platform applications that is increasingly being used. In this paper, we investigate whether one can transparently cross-compile C programs to WebAssembly, and if not, what impact porting can have on their security. We compile 17,802 programs that exhibit common vulnerabilities to 64-bit x86 and to WebAssembly binaries, and we observe that the execution of 4,911 binaries produces different results across these platforms. Through manual inspection, we identify three classes of root causes for such differences: the use of a different standard library implementation, the lack of security measures in WebAssembly, and the different semantics of the execution environments. We describe our observations and discuss the ones that are critical from a security point of view and need most attention from developers. We conclude that compiling an existing C program to WebAssembly for cross-platform distribution may require source code adaptations; otherwise, the security of the WebAssembly application may be at risk.

title: Security Risks of Porting C Programs to WebAssembly
text: The adoption of WebAssembly as a compilation target for cross-platform applications is gaining momentum. This raises crucial questions regarding the transparent cross-compilation of C programs to WebAssembly and the potential security implications of porting. To investigate this, we compiled 17,802 programs exhibiting common vulnerabilities to both 64-bit x86 and WebAssembly binaries, revealing that 4,911 binaries produce disparate results across these platforms. A manual analysis of these discrepancies identified three primary root causes: differences in standard library implementation, inadequate security measures in WebAssembly, and disparate execution environment semantics. Our findings highlight critical security concerns that warrant attention from developers, suggesting that source code adaptations may be necessary when compiling existing C programs to WebAssembly for cross-platform distribution, lest the security of the resulting WebAssembly application be compromised.

title: Class-aware Sounding Objects Localization via Audiovisual Correspondence
text: Audiovisual scenes are pervasive in our daily life. It is commonplace for humans to discriminatively localize different sounding objects but quite challenging for machines to achieve class-aware sounding objects localization without category annotations, i.e., localizing the sounding object and recognizing its category. To address this problem, we propose a two-stage step-by-step learning framework to localize and recognize sounding objects in complex audiovisual scenarios using only the correspondence between audio and vision. First, we propose to determine the sounding area via coarse-grained audiovisual correspondence in the single source cases. Then visual features in the sounding area are leveraged as candidate object representations to establish a category-representation object dictionary for expressive visual character extraction. We generate class-aware object localization maps in cocktail-party scenarios and use audiovisual correspondence to suppress silent areas by referring to this dictionary. Finally, we employ category-level audiovisual consistency as the supervision to achieve fine-grained audio and sounding object distribution alignment. Experiments on both realistic and synthesized videos show that our model is superior in localizing and recognizing objects as well as filtering out silent ones. We also transfer the learned audiovisual network into the unsupervised object detection task, obtaining reasonable performance.

title: Class-aware Sounding Objects Localization via Audiovisual Correspondence
text: The ubiquity of audiovisual scenes in daily life underscores the importance of developing machines capable of localizing and recognizing sounding objects without reliance on category annotations. While humans effortlessly distinguish between diverse sounding objects, machines struggle to achieve class-aware localization. To bridge this gap, we introduce a two-stage learning framework that leverages the audio-visual correspondence to localize and recognize sounding objects in complex scenarios. Initially, we identify the sounding area through coarse-grained audiovisual correspondence in single-source cases. Subsequently, visual features from the sounding area are utilized to construct a category-representation object dictionary, facilitating expressive visual character extraction. By generating class-aware object localization maps in cocktail-party scenarios and suppressing silent areas via audiovisual correspondence, we achieve fine-grained alignment between audio and sounding object distributions. Experimental results on realistic and synthesized videos demonstrate the superiority of our model in localizing and recognizing objects, as well as filtering out silent ones. Furthermore, we successfully transfer the learned audiovisual network to unsupervised object detection tasks, achieving reasonable performance.

title: Exploring Inter-frequency Guidance of Image for Lightweight Gaussian Denoising
text: Image denoising is of vital importance in many imaging or computer vision related areas. With the convolutional neural networks showing strong capability in computer vision tasks, the performance of image denoising has also been brought up by CNN based methods. Though CNN based image denoisers show promising results on this task, most of the current CNN based methods try to learn the mapping from noisy image to clean image directly, which lacks the explicit exploration of prior knowledge of images and noises. Natural images are observed to obey the reciprocal power law, implying the low-frequency band of image tend to occupy most of the energy. Thus in the condition of AGWN (additive gaussian white noise) deterioration, low-frequency band tend to preserve a higher PSNR than high-frequency band. Considering the spatial morphological consistency of different frequency bands, low-frequency band with more fidelity can be used as a guidance to refine the more contaminated high-frequency bands. Based on this thought, we proposed a novel network architecture denoted as IGNet, in order to refine the frequency bands from low to high in a progressive manner. Firstly, it decomposes the feature maps into high- and low-frequency subbands using DWT (discrete wavelet transform) iteratively, and then each low band features are used to refine the high band features. Finally, the refined feature maps are processed by a decoder to recover the clean result. With this design, more inter-frequency prior and information are utilized, thus the model size can be lightened while still perserves competitive results. Experiments on several public datasets show that our model obtains competitive performance comparing with other state-of-the-art methods yet with a lightweight structure.

title: Exploring Inter-frequency Guidance of Image for Lightweight Gaussian Denoising
text: Image denoising is a fundamental problem in computer vision, where the goal is to recover a clean image from a noisy observation. While Gaussian denoising is a well-studied topic, existing methods often suffer from high computational complexity, limiting their applicability in real-time scenarios. Recently, lightweight denoising models have gained popularity due to their efficiency and competitive performance. However, these models typically rely on intra-frequency guidance, which may not fully exploit the frequency-domain information of the image. In this work, we propose a novel approach to Gaussian denoising, exploring inter-frequency guidance of image (IFGI) to leverage the frequency-domain relationships between different frequency bands. Our method, dubbed IFGI-Net, consists of a lightweight neural network that takes the noisy image as input and produces a denoised output. The core innovation lies in the introduction of inter-frequency guidance modules, which facilitate the exchange of information across frequency bands, enabling the network to capture more robust and diverse frequency-domain patterns. Through extensive experiments on benchmark datasets, including BSD500 and Urban100, we demonstrate that IFGI-Net outperforms state-of-the-art lightweight denoising models, achieving a 1.2 dB improvement in PSNR on average. Furthermore, our model exhibits a 30% reduction in computational complexity compared to existing methods, making it more suitable for real-time applications. Ablation studies and visual results confirm the effectiveness of inter-frequency guidance in improving denoising performance. Our work has implications for various computer vision tasks, including image compression, deblurring, and segmentation, where efficient and accurate denoising is essential.

title: BEVDet: High-performance Multi-camera 3D Object Detection in Bird-Eye-View
text: Autonomous driving perceives its surroundings for decision making, which is one of the most complex scenarios in visual perception. The success of paradigm innovation in solving the 2D object detection task inspires us to seek an elegant, feasible, and scalable paradigm for fundamentally pushing the performance boundary in this area. To this end, we contribute the BEVDet paradigm in this paper. BEVDet performs 3D object detection in Bird-Eye-View (BEV), where most target values are defined and route planning can be handily performed. We merely reuse existing modules to build its framework but substantially develop its performance by constructing an exclusive data augmentation strategy and upgrading the Non-Maximum Suppression strategy. In the experiment, BEVDet offers an excellent trade-off between accuracy and time-efficiency. As a fast version, BEVDet-Tiny scores 31.2% mAP and 39.2% NDS on the nuScenes val set. It is comparable with FCOS3D, but requires just 11% computational budget of 215.3 GFLOPs and runs 9.2 times faster at 15.6 FPS. Another high-precision version dubbed BEVDet-Base scores 39.3% mAP and 47.2% NDS, significantly exceeding all published results. With a comparable inference speed, it surpasses FCOS3D by a large margin of +9.8% mAP and +10.0% NDS. The source code is publicly available for further research at .

title: BEVDet: High-performance Multi-camera 3D Object Detection in Bird-Eye-View
text: The quest for robust autonomous driving hinges on the ability to perceptually understand complex surroundings, rendering it a paramount challenge in computer vision. Inspired by the paradigmatic breakthroughs in 2D object detection, we seek to devise an innovative, efficient, and scalable framework to push the performance envelope in 3D object detection. This paper introduces BEVDet, a novel paradigm that tackles 3D object detection in Bird-Eye-View (BEV), where target values are predominantly defined and route planning can be conveniently performed. By reutilizing existing modules and developing a bespoke data augmentation strategy, as well as an upgraded Non-Maximum Suppression strategy, BEVDet achieves substantial performance enhancements. Experimental results demonstrate an excellent trade-off between accuracy and time-efficiency. The fast BEVDet-Tiny variant attains 31.2% mAP and 39.2% NDS on the nuScenes validation set, rivaling FCOS3D while requiring only 11% of its computational budget (215.3 GFLOPs) and operating 9.2 times faster at 15.6 FPS. The high-precision BEVDet-Base variant scores 39.3% mAP and 47.2% NDS, outperforming all published results, and surpassing FCOS3D by a significant margin of +9.8% mAP and +10.0% NDS, with comparable inference speed.

title: Shape Fragments
text: In constraint languages for RDF graphs, such as ShEx and SHACL, constraints on nodes and their properties in RDF graphs are known as "shapes". Schemas in these languages list the various shapes that certain targeted nodes must satisfy for the graph to conform to the schema. Using SHACL, we propose in this paper a novel use of shapes, by which a set of shapes is used to extract a subgraph from an RDF graph, the so-called shape fragment. Our proposed mechanism fits in the framework of Linked Data Fragments. In this paper, (i) we define our extraction mechanism formally, building on recently proposed SHACL formalizations; (ii) we establish correctness properties, which relate shape fragments to notions of provenance for database queries; (iii) we compare shape fragments with SPARQL queries; (iv) we discuss implementation options; and (v) we present initial experiments demonstrating that shape fragments are a feasible new idea.

title: Shape Fragments
text: The proliferation of shape-based data in various domains, including computer-aided design, geographic information systems, and multimedia databases, has necessitated the development of efficient indexing and querying techniques. Existing approaches, however, are often limited by their reliance on holistic shape representations, which can be computationally expensive and inflexible. We propose Shape Fragments, a novel framework that decomposes shapes into smaller, meaningful fragments, enabling the creation of a robust and scalable indexing structure. Our approach leverages a combination of geometric and topological features to extract fragments, which are then organized into a hierarchical index. Experimental evaluations on diverse shape datasets demonstrate that Shape Fragments significantly outperform state-of-the-art methods in terms of query processing time and accuracy. Furthermore, our framework facilitates the support of advanced queries, such as partial shape matching and shape similarity search, which are crucial in many real-world applications.

title: YOLO-Z: Improving small object detection in YOLOv5 for autonomous vehicles
text: As autonomous vehicles and autonomous racing rise in popularity, so does the need for faster and more accurate detectors. While our naked eyes are able to extract contextual information almost instantly, even from far away, image resolution and computational resources limitations make detecting smaller objects (that is, objects that occupy a small pixel area in the input image) a genuinely challenging task for machines and a wide-open research field. This study explores how the popular YOLOv5 object detector can be modified to improve its performance in detecting smaller objects, with a particular application in autonomous racing. To achieve this, we investigate how replacing certain structural elements of the model (as well as their connections and other parameters) can affect performance and inference time. In doing so, we propose a series of models at different scales, which we name `YOLO-Z', and which display an improvement of up to 6.9% in mAP when detecting smaller objects at 50% IOU, at the cost of just a 3ms increase in inference time compared to the original YOLOv5. Our objective is to inform future research on the potential of adjusting a popular detector such as YOLOv5 to address specific tasks and provide insights on how specific changes can impact small object detection. Such findings, applied to the broader context of autonomous vehicles, could increase the amount of contextual information available to such systems.

title: YOLO-Z: Improving small object detection in YOLOv5 for autonomous vehicles
text: Small object detection in images is a crucial task for various computer vision applications, particularly in autonomous vehicles where it directly impacts safety and reliability. While YOLOv5 has demonstrated state-of-the-art performance in object detection, its performance degrades significantly when dealing with small objects. This limitation arises from the inherent trade-off between spatial resolution and receptive field size in convolutional neural networks (CNNs). To address this issue, we propose YOLO-Z, a novel architecture that improves small object detection in YOLOv5. Our approach leverages a combination of spatial attention mechanisms and feature fusion techniques to enhance the feature representation of small objects. Specifically, we introduce a spatial attention module that adaptively weights feature maps based on object size, and a feature fusion module that combines features from different scales to improve robustness. We evaluate YOLO-Z on the KITTI object detection benchmark, which is a widely used dataset for autonomous vehicle applications. Experimental results demonstrate that YOLO-Z significantly outperforms YOLOv5 in detecting small objects, achieving an average precision improvement of 11.2% and 7.5% for pedestrian and cyclist classes, respectively. Furthermore, we show that YOLO-Z maintains a competitive performance on larger objects, making it a robust and efficient object detector for autonomous vehicle applications.

title: Binary Image Skeletonization Using 2-Stage U-Net
text: Object Skeletonization is the process of extracting skeletal, line-like representations of shapes. It provides a very useful tool for geometric shape understanding and minimal shape representation. It also has a wide variety of applications, most notably in anatomical research and activity detection. Several mathematical algorithmic approaches have been developed to solve this problem, and some of them have been proven quite robust. However, a lesser amount of attention has been invested into deep learning solutions for it. In this paper, we use a 2-stage variant of the famous U-Net architecture to split the problem space into two sub-problems: shape minimization and corrective skeleton thinning. Our model produces results that are visually much better than the baseline SkelNetOn model. We propose a new metric, M-CCORR, based on normalized correlation coefficients as an alternative to F1 for this challenge as it solves the problem of class imbalance, managing to recognize skeleton similarity without suffering from F1's over-sensitivity to pixel-shifts.

title: Binary Image Skeletonization Using 2-Stage U-Net
text: Binary image skeletonization is a fundamental task in computer vision, with applications in object recognition, feature extraction, and image analysis. Despite its importance, existing methods often suffer from limitations, including computational inefficiency, sensitivity to noise, and inability to handle complex topologies.
