In this work, we propose a novel 2-Stage U-Net architecture for binary image skeletonization, which leverages the strengths of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) in image feature extraction and shape analysis. Our approach consists of two stages: a coarse skeleton extraction stage, which generates an initial skeleton from the input binary image, and a refinement stage, which iteratively refines the skeleton to produce a more accurate and detailed representation. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate the superior performance of our method, achieving a mean structural similarity index (SSIM) of 0.953 and a mean intersection over union (IoU) of 0.921, outperforming state-of-the-art methods by a significant margin. Our approach also exhibits improved robustness to noise and ability to handle complex topologies, making it a promising solution for various computer vision applications.

title: Deep learning for brain metastasis detection and segmentation in longitudinal MRI data
text: Brain metastases occur frequently in patients with metastatic cancer. Early and accurate detection of brain metastases is very essential for treatment planning and prognosis in radiation therapy. To improve brain metastasis detection performance with deep learning, a custom detection loss called volume-level sensitivity-specificity (VSS) is proposed, which rates individual metastasis detection sensitivity and specificity in (sub-)volume levels. As sensitivity and precision are always a trade-off in a metastasis level, either a high sensitivity or a high precision can be achieved by adjusting the weights in the VSS loss without decline in dice score coefficient for segmented metastases. To reduce metastasis-like structures being detected as false positive metastases, a temporal prior volume is proposed as an additional input of DeepMedic. The modified network is called DeepMedic+ for distinction. Our proposed VSS loss improves the sensitivity of brain metastasis detection for DeepMedic, increasing the sensitivity from 85.3% to 97.5%. Alternatively, it improves the precision from 69.1% to 98.7%. Comparing DeepMedic+ with DeepMedic with the same VSS loss, 44.4% of the false positive metastases are reduced in the high sensitivity model and the precision reaches 99.6% for the high specificity model. The mean dice coefficient for all metastases is about 0.81. With the ensemble of the high sensitivity and high specificity models, on average only 1.5 false positive metastases per patient needs further check, while the majority of true positive metastases are confirmed. The ensemble learning is able to distinguish high confidence true positive metastases from metastases candidates that require special expert review or further follow-up, being particularly well-fit to the requirements of expert support in real clinical practice.

title: Deep learning for brain metastasis detection and segmentation in longitudinal MRI data
text: Brain metastases are a common and devastating complication of cancer, with timely detection and accurate segmentation being crucial for effective treatment. Longitudinal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) data offers a unique opportunity for monitoring disease progression, but manual analysis is time-consuming and prone to variability. Deep learning-based approaches have shown promise in automating this task, but existing methods are limited by small datasets, simplistic architectures, and inadequate handling of longitudinal data. We propose a novel deep learning framework for brain metastasis detection and segmentation in longitudinal MRI data, leveraging a large dataset of 150 patients with 450 MRI scans. Our approach combines a 3D U-Net with a recurrent neural network (RNN) to model spatial and temporal dependencies, respectively. The U-Net is designed to detect and segment metastases in individual scans, while the RNN integrates information across time points to capture disease progression. We evaluate our framework using a longitudinal segmentation task, where the goal is to segment metastases in a new scan given the previous scan(s). Our approach achieves a dice similarity coefficient (DSC) of 0.83, outperforming state-of-the-art methods by 10%. We also demonstrate improved detection performance, with a sensitivity of 0.92 and specificity of 0.95. Furthermore, we show that our framework can automatically identify disease progression patterns, enabling personalized treatment planning. Our contributions include a large-scale longitudinal MRI dataset, a novel deep learning architecture for brain metastasis detection and segmentation, and a comprehensive evaluation framework. Our approach has the potential to revolutionize the clinical workflow, enabling timely and accurate diagnosis, and improving patient outcomes.

title: Bottom-up approaches for multi-person pose estimation and it's applications: A brief review
text: Human Pose Estimation (HPE) is one of the fundamental problems in computer vision. It has applications ranging from virtual reality, human behavior analysis, video surveillance, anomaly detection, self-driving to medical assistance. The main objective of HPE is to obtain the person's posture from the given input. Among different paradigms for HPE, one paradigm is called bottom-up multi-person pose estimation. In the bottom-up approach, initially, all the key points of the targets are detected, and later in the optimization stage, the detected key points are associated with the corresponding targets. This review paper discussed the recent advancements in bottom-up approaches for the HPE and listed the possible high-quality datasets used to train the models. Additionally, a discussion of the prominent bottom-up approaches and their quantitative results on the standard performance matrices are given. Finally, the limitations of the existing methods are highlighted, and guidelines of the future research directions are given.

title: Bottom-up approaches for multi-person pose estimation and it's applications: A brief review
text: Human pose estimation has garnered significant attention in the computer vision community, driven by its potential to transform various applications such as healthcare, sports analysis, and human-computer interaction. Multi-person pose estimation, in particular, is a challenging problem due to the complexity of modeling interactions between individuals. Bottom-up approaches have emerged as a promising direction, where the focus is on detecting keypoints and grouping them to form poses, rather than directly predicting poses. This review provides an in-depth analysis of recent advancements in bottom-up multi-person pose estimation, covering key methodologies, datasets, and evaluation metrics. We examine the strengths and limitations of various techniques, including graph-based, clustering-based, and part-based methods. Our analysis reveals that bottom-up approaches have achieved state-of-the-art performance on benchmarks such as MSCOCO and PoseTrack, with notable improvements in handling occlusions and varied poses. We also discuss the potential applications of multi-person pose estimation in areas such as autonomous systems, virtual reality, and surveillance.

title: A Discriminative Single-Shot Segmentation Network for Visual Object Tracking
text: Template-based discriminative trackers are currently the dominant tracking paradigm due to their robustness, but are restricted to bounding box tracking and a limited range of transformation models, which reduces their localization accuracy. We propose a discriminative single-shot segmentation tracker -- D3S2, which narrows the gap between visual object tracking and video object segmentation. A single-shot network applies two target models with complementary geometric properties, one invariant to a broad range of transformations, including non-rigid deformations, the other assuming a rigid object to simultaneously achieve robust online target segmentation. The overall tracking reliability is further increased by decoupling the object and feature scale estimation. Without per-dataset finetuning, and trained only for segmentation as the primary output, D3S2 outperforms all published trackers on the recent short-term tracking benchmark VOT2020 and performs very close to the state-of-the-art trackers on the GOT-10k, TrackingNet, OTB100 and LaSoT. D3S2 outperforms the leading segmentation tracker SiamMask on video object segmentation benchmarks and performs on par with top video object segmentation algorithms.

title: A Discriminative Single-Shot Segmentation Network for Visual Object Tracking
text: Discriminative trackers, while robust, have limitations in bounding box tracking and transformation models, compromising their localization accuracy. This paper bridges the gap between visual object tracking and video object segmentation by introducing D3S2, a discriminative single-shot segmentation tracker. Our approach employs a single-shot network that leverages two target models with complementary geometric properties: one invariant to a broad range of transformations, including non-rigid deformations, and another that assumes a rigid object. This enables robust online target segmentation while decoupling object and feature scale estimation, thereby increasing tracking reliability. Notably, without per-dataset fine-tuning and trained solely for segmentation, D3S2 outperforms all published trackers on VOT2020 and rivals state-of-the-art trackers on GOT-10k, TrackingNet, OTB100, and LaSoT. Furthermore, D3S2 surpasses the leading segmentation tracker SiamMask on video object segmentation benchmarks and performs competitively with top video object segmentation algorithms.

title: Multimodal Analysis of memes for sentiment extraction
text: Memes are one of the most ubiquitous forms of social media communication. The study and processing of memes, which are intrinsically multimedia, is a popular topic right now. The study presented in this research is based on the Memotion dataset, which involves categorising memes based on irony, comedy, motivation, and overall-sentiment. Three separate innovative transformer-based techniques have been developed, and their outcomes have been thoroughly reviewed.The best algorithm achieved a macro F1 score of 0.633 for humour classification, 0.55 for motivation classification, 0.61 for sarcasm classification, and 0.575 for overall sentiment of the meme out of all our techniques.

title: Multimodal Analysis of memes for sentiment extraction
text: The proliferation of internet memes has created a vast, uncharted territory for sentiment analysis, as they often convey complex emotions and opinions through multimodal content. We propose a novel framework for sentiment extraction from memes, integrating computer vision and natural language processing techniques. Our approach leverages a convolutional neural network for visual feature extraction and a transformer-based architecture for textual analysis. Experimental results on a large-scale dataset of memes demonstrate the effectiveness of our method, achieving a sentiment classification accuracy of 83.2% and outperforming state-of-the-art unimodal approaches.

title: Geodesic squared exponential kernel for non-rigid shape registration
text: This work addresses the problem of non-rigid registration of 3D scans, which is at the core of shape modeling techniques. Firstly, we propose a new kernel based on geodesic distances for the Gaussian Process Morphable Models (GPMMs) framework. The use of geodesic distances into the kernel makes it more adapted to the topological and geometric characteristics of the surface and leads to more realistic deformations around holes and curved areas. Since the kernel possesses hyperparameters we have optimized them for the task of face registration on the FaceWarehouse dataset. We show that the Geodesic squared exponential kernel performs significantly better than state of the art kernels for the task of face registration on all the 20 expressions of the FaceWarehouse dataset. Secondly, we propose a modification of the loss function used in the non-rigid ICP registration algorithm, that allows to weight the correspondences according to the confidence given to them. As a use case, we show that we can make the registration more robust to outliers in the 3D scans, such as non-skin parts.

title: Geodesic squared exponential kernel for non-rigid shape registration
text: Non-rigid shape registration is a fundamental task in computer vision, with numerous applications in image and video analysis, object recognition, and tracking. The key challenge lies in designing a robust and efficient kernel function that can effectively capture the complex, non-linear relationships between shapes. This paper presents a novel geodesic squared exponential kernel (GSEK) that leverages the Riemannian geometry of the shape space to achieve accurate and efficient non-rigid shape registration. Unlike traditional kernel methods, GSEK incorporates the intrinsic geometry of the shape space, enabling it to better handle complex deformations and topological changes. We derive the GSEK kernel function and develop an efficient optimization algorithm to compute the registration. Experimental results on various benchmark datasets demonstrate the superiority of GSEK over state-of-the-art kernel methods, achieving higher registration accuracy and faster computational times. Moreover, we show that GSEK can be seamlessly integrated with existing registration frameworks, making it a versatile and practical tool for real-world applications. Our approach opens up new avenues for exploring the geometric structure of shape spaces, with far-reaching implications for computer vision and machine learning research.

title: End to End Software Engineering Research
text: End to end learning is machine learning starting in raw data and predicting a desired concept, with all steps done automatically. In software engineering context, we see it as starting from the source code and predicting process metrics. This framework can be used for predicting defects, code quality, productivity and more. End-to-end improves over features based machine learning by not requiring domain experts and being able to extract new knowledge. We describe a dataset of 5M files from 15k projects constructed for this goal. The dataset is constructed in a way that enables not only predicting concepts but also investigating their causes.

title: End to End Software Engineering Research
text: Machine learning paradigm shifts towards end-to-end learning, where raw data is directly utilized to predict desired concepts, eliminating manual intervention. In software engineering, this translates to automatically predicting process metrics from source code. This framework has far-reaching potential, encompassing defect prediction, code quality assessment, and productivity evaluation, among others. Unlike feature-based machine learning, end-to-end learning dispenses with the need for domain experts and has the capacity to uncover novel insights. We present a comprehensive dataset comprising 5 million files from 15,000 projects, carefully constructed to facilitate both concept prediction and causal investigation.

title: Few-shot Font Generation with Weakly Supervised Localized Representations
text: Automatic few-shot font generation aims to solve a well-defined, real-world problem because manual font designs are expensive and sensitive to the expertise of designers. Existing methods learn to disentangle style and content elements by developing a universal style representation for each font style. However, this approach limits the model in representing diverse local styles, because it is unsuitable for complicated letter systems, for example, Chinese, whose characters consist of a varying number of components (often called "radical") -- with a highly complex structure. In this paper, we propose a novel font generation method that learns localized styles, namely component-wise style representations, instead of universal styles. The proposed style representations enable the synthesis of complex local details in text designs. However, learning component-wise styles solely from a few reference glyphs is infeasible when a target script has a large number of components, for example, over 200 for Chinese. To reduce the number of required reference glyphs, we represent component-wise styles by a product of component and style factors, inspired by low-rank matrix factorization. Owing to the combination of strong representation and a compact factorization strategy, our method shows remarkably better few-shot font generation results (with only eight reference glyphs) than other state-of-the-art methods. Moreover, strong locality supervision, for example, location of each component, skeleton, or strokes, was not utilized. The source code is available at and

title: Few-shot Font Generation with Weakly Supervised Localized Representations
text: The proliferation of digital content has led to an unprecedented demand for diverse and high-quality fonts, yet the traditional font design process remains labor-intensive and time-consuming. Recent advances in deep learning-based font generation have shown promise, but existing methods often require large amounts of labeled data, limiting their applicability to rare or niche font styles. To address this challenge, we propose a novel few-shot font generation framework that leverages weakly supervised localized representations. Our approach exploits the inherent structure of font glyphs, learning to represent characters as a composition of localized parts. By enforcing consistency across characters and fonts, our model is able to generalize effectively from limited data. We introduce a new weak supervision signal, termed "glyph co-occurrence," which captures the frequency of character pairs in a given language. This signal enables our model to learn meaningful localized representations without explicit part labels. Experimental results on a range of benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, achieving state-of-the-art performance in few-shot font generation tasks. Notably, our model is able to generate high-quality fonts from as few as 5 example characters, outperforming existing methods that require orders of magnitude more data. Our work has significant implications for the automation of font design and the democratization of typography.

title: Meta-Learning and Self-Supervised Pretraining for Real World Image Translation
text: Recent advances in deep learning, in particular enabled by hardware advances and big data, have provided impressive results across a wide range of computational problems such as computer vision, natural language, or reinforcement learning. Many of these improvements are however constrained to problems with large-scale curated data-sets which require a lot of human labor to gather. Additionally, these models tend to generalize poorly under both slight distributional shifts and low-data regimes. In recent years, emerging fields such as meta-learning or self-supervised learning have been closing the gap between proof-of-concept results and real-life applications of machine learning by extending deep-learning to the semi-supervised and few-shot domains. We follow this line of work and explore spatio-temporal structure in a recently introduced image-to-image translation problem in order to: i) formulate a novel multi-task few-shot image generation benchmark and ii) explore data augmentations in contrastive pre-training for image translation downstream tasks. We present several baselines for the few-shot problem and discuss trade-offs between different approaches. Our code is available at

title: Meta-Learning and Self-Supervised Pretraining for Real World Image Translation
text: Image-to-image translation tasks, such as translating daytime to nighttime scenes, remain challenging due to the scarcity of paired training data. Recent advances in self-supervised learning and meta-learning have shown promising results in related domains. This paper explores the synergy between these two paradigms for real-world image translation. We propose a novel framework that leverages self-supervised pretraining to learn domain-invariant representations and meta-learning to adapt to target domains with limited supervision. Our approach, dubbed MetaSSL, iteratively refines the pretraining process using meta-learning objectives, enabling the model to generalize to unseen domains. Experimental results on three real-world image translation benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness of MetaSSL, achieving state-of-the-art performance in most settings. Notably, our method outperforms existing approaches by 3.5% in terms of peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) on the challenging Day-Night translation task. Ablation studies further validate the importance of self-supervised pretraining and meta-learning components in our framework.

title: BBM92 quantum key distribution over a free space dusty channel of 200 meters
text: Free space quantum communication assumes importance as it is a precursor for satellite-based quantum communication needed for secure key distribution over longer distances. Prepare and measure protocols like BB84 consider the satellite as a trusted device, which is fraught with security threat looking at the current trend for satellite-based optical communication. Therefore, entanglement-based protocols must be preferred, so that one can consider the satellite as an untrusted device too. The current work reports the implementation of BBM92 protocol, an entanglement-based QKD protocol over 200 m distance using an indigenous facility developed at Physical Research Laboratory (PRL), Ahmedabad, India. Our results show the effect of atmospheric aerosols on sift key rate, and eventually, secure key rate. Such experiments are important to validate the models to account for the atmospheric effects on the key rates achieved through satellite-based QKD.

title: BBM92 quantum key distribution over a free space dusty channel of 200 meters
text: The establishment of secure key distribution over extended distances relies on the development of free space quantum communication, a precursor to satellite-based quantum communication. However, traditional prepare and measure protocols, such as BB84, rely on the satellite as a trusted device, rendering them vulnerable to security threats in the context of current satellite-based optical communication trends. In contrast, entanglement-based protocols offer the advantage of considering the satellite as an untrusted device, thereby enhancing security. This study reports the successful implementation of the BBM92 protocol, an entanglement-based quantum key distribution protocol, over a 200 m distance using a novel facility developed at the Physical Research Laboratory, Ahmedabad, India. Our findings demonstrate the impact of atmospheric aerosols on sift key rates and secure key rates, underscoring the importance of such experiments in validating models that account for atmospheric effects on satellite-based QKD key rates.

title: Compromised ACC vehicles can degrade current mixed-autonomy traffic performance while remaining stealthy against detection
text: We demonstrate that a supply-chain level compromise of the adaptive cruise control (ACC) capability on equipped vehicles can be used to significantly degrade system level performance of current day mixed-autonomy freeway networks. Via a simple threat model which causes random deceleration attacks (RDAs), compromised vehicles create congestion waves in the traffic that decrease average speed and network throughput. We use a detailed and realistic traffic simulation environment to quantify the impacts of the attack on a model of a real high-volume freeway in the United States. We find that the effect of the attack depends both on the level of underlying traffic congestion, and what percentage of ACC vehicles can be compromised. In moderate congestion regimes the attack can degrade mean commuter speed by over 7%. In high density regimes overall network throughput can be reduced by up to 3%. And, in moderate to high congestion regimes, it can cost commuters on the network over 300 USD/km hr. All of these results motivate that the proposed attack is able to significantly degrade performance of the traffic network. We also develop an anomaly detection technique that uses GPS traces on vehicles to identify malicious/compromised vehicles. We employ this technique on data from the simulation experiments and find that it is unable to identify compromised ACCs compared to benign/normal drivers. That is, these attacks are stealthy to detection. Stronger attacks can be accurately labeled as malicious, motivating that there is a limit to how impactful attacks can be before they are no longer stealthy. Finally, we experimentally execute the attack on a real and commercially available ACC vehicle, demonstrating the possible real world feasibility of an RDA.

title: Compromised ACC vehicles can degrade current mixed-autonomy traffic performance while remaining stealthy against detection
text: The compromising of adaptive cruise control (ACC) systems at the supply-chain level can have a profound impact on the performance of mixed-autonomy freeway networks. We develop a threat model that induces random deceleration attacks (RDAs) in compromised vehicles, which in turn generate congestion waves that decrease average speed and network throughput. Utilizing a realistic traffic simulation environment, we quantify the effects of the attack on a model of a high-volume freeway in the United States. Our results indicate that the attack's efficacy is dependent on both the underlying traffic congestion and the proportion of compromised ACC vehicles. Notably, in moderate congestion regimes, the attack can reduce mean commuter speed by over 7%, while in high-density regimes, overall network throughput can be decreased by up to 3%. Moreover, the attack can incur significant costs for commuters, exceeding 300 USD/km hr in moderate to high congestion regimes. We also design an anomaly detection technique that leverages GPS traces to identify malicious vehicles. However, when applied to our simulation data, this technique fails to distinguish compromised ACCs from benign drivers, highlighting the stealthy nature of these attacks. Conversely, more aggressive attacks can be accurately labeled as malicious, suggesting a threshold beyond which attacks become detectable. Finally, we demonstrate the feasibility of RDAs in the real world by experimentally executing the attack on a commercially available ACC vehicle.

title: Automatic Estimation of Anthropometric Human Body Measurements
text: Research tasks related to human body analysis have been drawing a lot of attention in computer vision area over the last few decades, considering its potential benefits on our day-to-day life. Anthropometry is a field defining physical measures of a human body size, form, and functional capacities. Specifically, the accurate estimation of anthropometric body measurements from visual human body data is one of the challenging problems, where the solution would ease many different areas of applications, including ergonomics, garment manufacturing, etc. This paper formulates a research in the field of deep learning and neural networks, to tackle the challenge of body measurements estimation from various types of visual input data (such as 2D images or 3D point clouds). Also, we deal with the lack of real human data annotated with ground truth body measurements required for training and evaluation, by generating a synthetic dataset of various human body shapes and performing a skeleton-driven annotation.

title: Automatic Estimation of Anthropometric Human Body Measurements
text: The analysis of the human body has garnered significant attention in computer vision over the past few decades, driven by its potential to transform various aspects of daily life. Anthropometry, the study of human body size, shape, and functional capabilities, is a crucial field that stands to benefit from accurate estimation of body measurements from visual data. However, achieving this goal poses significant challenges, with applications in ergonomics, garment manufacturing, and beyond. This research leverages deep learning and neural networks to tackle the problem of estimating anthropometric measurements from diverse visual inputs, including 2D images and 3D point clouds. A notable obstacle in this pursuit is the scarcity of annotated real-world data, which we address by generating a synthetic dataset of varied human body shapes and implementing skeleton-driven annotation, thereby facilitating the training and evaluation of our approach.

title: DA-FDFtNet: Dual Attention Fake Detection Fine-tuning Network to Detect Various AI-Generated Fake Images
text: Due to the advancement of Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN), Autoencoders, and other AI technologies, it has been much easier to create fake images such as "Deepfakes". More recent research has introduced few-shot learning, which uses a small amount of training data to produce fake images and videos more effectively. Therefore, the ease of generating manipulated images and the difficulty of distinguishing those images can cause a serious threat to our society, such as propagating fake information. However, detecting realistic fake images generated by the latest AI technology is challenging due to the reasons mentioned above. In this work, we propose Dual Attention Fake Detection Fine-tuning Network (DA-FDFtNet) to detect the manipulated fake face images from the real face data. Our DA-FDFtNet integrates the pre-trained model with Fine-Tune Transformer, MBblockV3, and a channel attention module to improve the performance and robustness across different types of fake images. In particular, Fine-Tune Transformer consists of multiple numbers of an image-based self-attention module and a down-sampling layer. The channel attention module is also connected with the pre-trained model to capture the fake images feature space. We experiment with our DA-FDFtNet with the FaceForensics++ dataset and various GAN-generated datasets, and we show that our approach outperforms the previous baseline models.

title: DA-FDFtNet: Dual Attention Fake Detection Fine-tuning Network to Detect Various AI-Generated Fake Images
text: The proliferation of generative models, such as Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN) and Autoencoders, has facilitated the creation of sophisticated fake images, including "Deepfakes". The recent advent of few-shot learning has further exacerbated this issue, enabling the production of convincing fake images and videos with limited training data. This ease of image manipulation poses a significant threat to the dissemination of truthful information, as distinguishing authentic from manipulated images has become increasingly challenging. To address this concern, we propose the Dual Attention Fake Detection Fine-tuning Network (DA-FDFtNet), a novel approach for detecting manipulated face images amidst real face data. Our framework integrates a pre-trained model with a Fine-Tune Transformer, comprising multiple image-based self-attention modules and down-sampling layers, as well as an MBblockV3 component and a channel attention module. This architecture enables the capture of fake image feature spaces and enhances performance and robustness across diverse types of manipulated images. Experimental results on the FaceForensics++ dataset and various GAN-generated datasets demonstrate the superiority of our DA-FDFtNet over existing baseline models.

title: Looking Beyond Corners: Contrastive Learning of Visual Representations for Keypoint Detection and Description Extraction
text: Learnable keypoint detectors and descriptors are beginning to outperform classical hand-crafted feature extraction methods. Recent studies on self-supervised learning of visual representations have driven the increasing performance of learnable models based on deep networks. By leveraging traditional data augmentations and homography transformations, these networks learn to detect corners under adverse conditions such as extreme illumination changes. However, their generalization capabilities are limited to corner-like features detected a priori by classical methods or synthetically generated data. In this paper, we propose the Correspondence Network (CorrNet) that learns to detect repeatable keypoints and to extract discriminative descriptions via unsupervised contrastive learning under spatial constraints. Our experiments show that CorrNet is not only able to detect low-level features such as corners, but also high-level features that represent similar objects present in a pair of input images through our proposed joint guided backpropagation of their latent space. Our approach obtains competitive results under viewpoint changes and achieves state-of-the-art performance under illumination changes.

title: Looking Beyond Corners: Contrastive Learning of Visual Representations for Keypoint Detection and Description Extraction
text: The task of detecting and describing keypoints in images is a fundamental problem in computer vision, with applications in various areas such as object recognition, tracking, and 3D reconstruction. While recent advances in deep learning have led to significant improvements in keypoint detection, the extraction of informative and robust descriptors remains a challenging task. Existing methods often rely on hand-crafted features or supervision from annotated data, which can be limited and biased. In this work, we propose a novel contrastive learning framework that learns visual representations for keypoint detection and description extraction without relying on explicit supervision. Our approach, dubbed CornerBeyond, leverages self-supervised learning to learn robust and informative descriptors by contrasting positive and negative keypoint pairs. Experimental results on popular benchmarks, including HPatches and Aachen Day-Night, demonstrate that CornerBeyond outperforms state-of-the-art methods in keypoint detection and description tasks, achieving significant improvements in terms of repeatability, distinctiveness, and matching accuracy.

title: Barely-Supervised Learning: Semi-Supervised Learning with very few labeled images
text: This paper tackles the problem of semi-supervised learning when the set of labeled samples is limited to a small number of images per class, typically less than 10, problem that we refer to as barely-supervised learning. We analyze in depth the behavior of a state-of-the-art semi-supervised method, FixMatch, which relies on a weakly-augmented version of an image to obtain supervision signal for a more strongly-augmented version. We show that it frequently fails in barely-supervised scenarios, due to a lack of training signal when no pseudo-label can be predicted with high confidence. We propose a method to leverage self-supervised methods that provides training signal in the absence of confident pseudo-labels. We then propose two methods to refine the pseudo-label selection process which lead to further improvements. The first one relies on a per-sample history of the model predictions, akin to a voting scheme. The second iteratively updates class-dependent confidence thresholds to better explore classes that are under-represented in the pseudo-labels. Our experiments show that our approach performs significantly better on STL-10 in the barely-supervised regime, e.g. with 4 or 8 labeled images per class.

title: Barely-Supervised Learning: Semi-Supervised Learning with very few labeled images
text: The scarcity of labeled data hinders the widespread adoption of deep learning in computer vision, as collecting and annotating large datasets is a labor-intensive and time-consuming task. Semi-supervised learning (SSL) offers a promising solution by leveraging both labeled and unlabeled data to improve model performance. However, existing SSL methods often require a substantial number of labeled examples, which may not be feasible in many real-world scenarios. In this work, we explore the challenging problem of SSL with very few labeled images, which we term "barely-supervised learning." We propose a novel approach that combines a robust pseudo-labeling strategy with a confidence-based sampling technique to effectively utilize the limited labeled data and a large pool of unlabeled images. Our method, dubbed Barely-Supervised Learning (BSL), achieves state-of-the-art performance on several benchmark datasets, including CIFAR-10 and SVHN, with as few as 10 labeled examples per class. We demonstrate that BSL can learn effective representations and generalize well to unseen data, even with extremely limited supervision. Our findings have significant implications for real-world applications where labeled data is scarce, and we believe that BSL can pave the way for more widespread adoption of deep learning in computer vision.

title: Catch Me If You GAN: Using Artificial Intelligence for Fake Log Generation
text: With artificial intelligence (AI) becoming relevant in various parts of everyday life, other technologies are already widely influenced by the new way of handling large amounts of data. Although widespread already, AI has had only punctual influences on the cybersecurity field specifically. Many techniques and technologies used by cybersecurity experts function through manual labor and barely draw on automation, e.g., logs are often reviewed manually by system admins for potentially malicious keywords. This work evaluates the use of a special type of AI called generative adversarial networks (GANs) for log generation. More precisely, three different generative adversarial networks, SeqGAN, MaliGAN, and CoT, are reviewed in this research regarding their performance, focusing on generating new logs as a means of deceiving system admins for red teams. Although static generators for fake logs have been around for a while, their produces are usually easy to reveal as such. Using AI as an approach to this problem has not been widely researched. Identified challenges consist of formatting, dates and times, and overall consistency. Summing up the results, GANs seem not to be a good fit for generating fake logs. Their capability to detect fake logs, however, might be of use in practical scenarios.

title: Catch Me If You GAN: Using Artificial Intelligence for Fake Log Generation
text: The proliferation of sophisticated cyber threats has led to an urgent need for effective log analysis and incident response strategies. However, the scarcity of realistic and diverse log data hinders the development of robust log analysis techniques. To address this challenge, we propose a novel approach that leverages Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) to generate synthetic logs that mimic real-world attack patterns. Our framework, dubbed "FakeLogGen," utilizes a combination of supervised and unsupervised learning techniques to generate logs that are indistinguishable from genuine logs. We evaluate FakeLogGen using a dataset of real-world logs from a large-scale enterprise network and demonstrate its ability to generate high-fidelity logs that can effectively evade detection by state-of-the-art log analysis tools. Our experiments show that FakeLogGen can increase the false negative rate of log analysis tools by up to 35%, highlighting the potential risks of relying solely on machine learning-based log analysis techniques. Furthermore, we demonstrate the utility of FakeLogGen in generating logs that can be used to augment existing log datasets, improving the robustness of log analysis models by up to 25%. Our findings have significant implications for the development of more effective log analysis and incident response strategies.

title: Community Detection in Medical Image Datasets: Using Wavelets and Spectral Methods
text: Medical image datasets can have large number of images representing patients with different health conditions and various disease severity. When dealing with raw unlabeled image datasets, the large number of samples often makes it hard for experts and non-experts to understand the variety of images present in a dataset. Supervised learning methods rely on labeled images which requires a considerable effort by medical experts to first understand the communities of images present in the data and then labeling the images. Here, we propose an algorithm to facilitate the automatic identification of communities in medical image datasets. We further demonstrate that such analysis can be insightful in a supervised setting when the images are already labeled. Such insights are useful because, health and disease severity can be considered a continuous spectrum, and within each class, there usually are finer communities worthy of investigation, especially when they have similarities to communities in other classes. In our approach, we use wavelet decomposition of images in tandem with spectral methods. We show that the eigenvalues of a graph Laplacian can reveal the number of notable communities in an image dataset. Moreover, analyzing the similarities may be used to infer a spectrum representing the severity of the disease. In our experiments, we use a dataset of images labeled with different conditions for COVID patients. We detect 25 communities in the dataset and then observe that only 6 of those communities contain patients with pneumonia. We also investigate the contents of a colorectal cancer histology dataset.

title: Community Detection in Medical Image Datasets: Using Wavelets and Spectral Methods
text: Medical image datasets often comprise a large number of images representing diverse patient populations with varying disease severity, rendering it challenging for experts and non-experts to comprehend the inherent image variability. The reliance on supervised learning methods necessitates labor-intensive labeling efforts by medical experts, who must first identify and understand the underlying image communities. This paper proposes an algorithm to automate the identification of communities in medical image datasets, demonstrating its utility in both unlabeled and labeled settings. By acknowledging that health and disease severity exist on a continuous spectrum, our approach uncovers finer communities within each class, which can exhibit similarities to those in other classes. We employ wavelet decomposition of images in conjunction with spectral methods, leveraging the eigenvalues of a graph Laplacian to reveal the number of prominent communities in an image dataset. Furthermore, analyzing similarities enables the inference of a disease severity spectrum. Experimental results on a COVID-19 image dataset labeled with different conditions reveal 25 distinct communities, with only 6 containing patients with pneumonia. Additionally, we investigate a colorectal cancer histology dataset, showcasing the algorithm's versatility in uncovering meaningful patterns in medical image datasets.

title: Learning and Crafting for the Wide Multiple Baseline Stereo
text: This thesis introduces the wide multiple baseline stereo (WxBS) problem. WxBS, a generalization of the standard wide baseline stereo problem, considers the matching of images that simultaneously differ in more than one image acquisition factor such as viewpoint, illumination, sensor type, or where object appearance changes significantly, e.g., over time. A new dataset with the ground truth, evaluation metric and baselines has been introduced. The thesis presents the following improvements of the WxBS pipeline. (i) A loss function, called HardNeg, for learning a local image descriptor that relies on hard negative mining within a mini-batch and on the maximization of the distance between the closest positive and the closest negative patches. (ii) The descriptor trained with the HardNeg loss, called HardNet, is compact and shows state-of-the-art performance in standard matching, patch verification and retrieval benchmarks. (iii) A method for learning the affine shape, orientation, and potentially other parameters related to geometric and appearance properties of local features. (iv) A tentative correspondences generation strategy which generalizes the standard first to second closest distance ratio is presented. The selection strategy, which shows performance superior to the standard method, is applicable to either hard-engineered descriptors like SIFT, LIOP, and MROGH or deeply learned like HardNet. (v) A feedback loop is introduced for the two-view matching problem, resulting in MODS -- matching with on-demand view synthesis -- algorithm. MODS is an algorithm that handles a viewing angle difference even larger than the previous state-of-the-art ASIFT algorithm, without a significant increase of computational cost over "standard" wide and narrow baseline approaches. Last, but not least, a comprehensive benchmark for local features and robust estimation algorithms is introduced.

title: Learning and Crafting for the Wide Multiple Baseline Stereo
text: The wide multiple baseline stereo (WxBS) problem, a generalized variant of the standard wide baseline stereo problem, is introduced, where images differ in multiple acquisition factors, including viewpoint, illumination, sensor type, or exhibit significant object appearance changes over time. To facilitate research in this domain, a novel dataset with ground truth, evaluation metrics, and baselines is presented. This work proposes several key improvements to the WxBS pipeline. Firstly, a novel loss function, HardNeg, is developed for learning local image descriptors, which leverages hard negative mining within mini-batches and maximizes the distance between the closest positive and negative patches. The resulting descriptor, HardNet, is compact and achieves state-of-the-art performance in standard matching, patch verification, and retrieval benchmarks. Furthermore, a method for learning affine shape, orientation, and other geometric and appearance properties of local features is presented. A generalized tentative correspondences generation strategy is also introduced, which outperforms the standard first to second closest distance ratio and is applicable to both handcrafted and learned descriptors. Additionally, a feedback loop is incorporated into the two-view matching problem, yielding the MODS algorithm, which can handle large viewing angle differences without significantly increasing computational cost. Finally, a comprehensive benchmark for local features and robust estimation algorithms is established, providing a unified framework for evaluating WxBS methods.

title: Physical ZKP for Makaro Using a Standard Deck of Cards
text: Makaro is a logic puzzle with an objective to fill numbers into a rectangular grid to satisfy certain conditions. In 2018, Bultel et al. developed a physical zero-knowledge proof (ZKP) protocol for Makaro using a deck of cards, which allows a prover to physically convince a verifier that he/she knows a solution of the puzzle without revealing it. However, their protocol requires several identical copies of some cards, making it impractical as a deck of playing cards found in everyday life typically consists of all different cards. In this paper, we propose a new ZKP protocol for Makaro that can be implemented using a standard deck (a deck consisting of all different cards). Our protocol also uses asymptotically less cards than the protocol of Bultel et al. Most importantly, we develop a general method to encode a number with a sequence of all different cards. This allows us to securely compute several numerical functions using a standard deck, such as verifying that two given numbers are different and verifying that a number is the largest one among the given numbers.

title: Physical ZKP for Makaro Using a Standard Deck of Cards
text: The logic puzzle Makaro involves filling a rectangular grid with numbers subject to specific constraints. Recently, Bultel et al. (2018) developed a physical zero-knowledge proof (ZKP) protocol for Makaro, leveraging a deck of cards to enable a prover to demonstrate puzzle solvability without disclosure. However, this protocol relies on identical card copies, rendering it impractical for standard decks comprised of distinct cards. This paper presents a novel ZKP protocol for Makaro amenable to implementation with a standard deck, overcoming the limitations of prior work. Notably, our protocol requires asymptotically fewer cards than its predecessor. Furthermore, we introduce a general method for encoding numerical values using sequences of distinct cards, facilitating secure computation of various numerical functions, including verifying numerical distinctness and identifying the maximum value among a set of given numbers.

title: DevOps and Microservices in Scientific System development
text: There is a gap in scientific information systems development concerning modern software engineering and scientific computing. Historically, software engineering methodologies have been perceived as an unwanted accidental complexity to computational scientists in their scientific systems development. More recent trends, like the end of Moore's law and the subsequent diversification of hardware platforms, combined with the increasing multidisciplinarity of science itself have exacerbated the problem because self-taught "end user developers" are not familiar with the disciplines needed to tackle this increased complexity. On a more positive note, agile programming methods have approached software development practices to the way scientific software is produced. In this work, we present the experience of a multi-year industry research project where agile methods, microservices and DevOps were applied. Our goal is to validate the hypothesis that the use of microservices would allow computational scientists to work in the more minimalistic prototype-oriented way that they prefer while the software engineering team would handle the integration. Hence, scientific multidisciplinary systems would gain in a twofold way: (i) Subject Matter Experts(SME) use their preferable tools to develop the specific scientific part of the system; (ii) software engineers provide the high quality software code for the system delivery.

title: DevOps and Microservices in Scientific System development
text: The adoption of DevOps practices and microservices architecture has transformed the software development landscape in recent years, promising increased agility, scalability, and maintainability. However, the scientific system development community has been slow to capitalize on these advances, hindered by the complexity of integrating heterogeneous tools and workflows. To address this gap, we conducted a mixed-methods study, combining a systematic literature review, a survey of 150 scientific system developers, and three in-depth case studies of scientific system development projects adopting DevOps and microservices. Our results show that the adoption of DevOps practices, such as continuous integration and delivery, and microservices architecture can significantly reduce integration time, improve system reliability, and enhance collaboration among development teams. However, we also identify key challenges, including the need for cultural shifts, additional infrastructure investments, and the development of new skills. Our analysis reveals that a tailored approach, incorporating domain-specific tools and workflows, is essential for successful adoption in scientific system development. We present a reference model for DevOps and microservices adoption in scientific system development, providing a roadmap for practitioners and researchers seeking to harness the benefits of these approaches in their own projects.

title: Multi-View Partial (MVP) Point Cloud Challenge 2021 on Completion and Registration: Methods and Results
text: As real-scanned point clouds are mostly partial due to occlusions and viewpoints, reconstructing complete 3D shapes based on incomplete observations becomes a fundamental problem for computer vision. With a single incomplete point cloud, it becomes the partial point cloud completion problem. Given multiple different observations, 3D reconstruction can be addressed by performing partial-to-partial point cloud registration. Recently, a large-scale Multi-View Partial (MVP) point cloud dataset has been released, which consists of over 100,000 high-quality virtual-scanned partial point clouds. Based on the MVP dataset, this paper reports methods and results in the Multi-View Partial Point Cloud Challenge 2021 on Completion and Registration. In total, 128 participants registered for the competition, and 31 teams made valid submissions. The top-ranked solutions will be analyzed, and then we will discuss future research directions.

title: Multi-View Partial (MVP) Point Cloud Challenge 2021 on Completion and Registration: Methods and Results
text: The proliferation of 3D point cloud data has spurred significant interest in developing robust methods for completion and registration. To foster innovation in this realm, we organized the Multi-View Partial (MVP) Point Cloud Challenge 2021, a comprehensive benchmarking initiative focusing on these two tasks. The challenge attracted 15 participating teams, who submitted their methods for evaluation on a diverse dataset comprising 145 scenes with varying levels of occlusion and complexity. We employed a rigorous evaluation protocol, incorporating metrics such as Chamfer distance, Earth Mover's distance, and registration accuracy. The results reveal that the top-performing methods leverage advanced neural network architectures, incorporating features like attention mechanisms and graph convolutions. Notably, the winning approach achieved a 23.1% reduction in Chamfer distance for completion and a 34.5% improvement in registration accuracy compared to the baseline. This challenge provides valuable insights into the current state-of-the-art and outlines future research directions in point cloud processing.

title: A Case Study on Optimization of Warehouses
text: In warehouses, order picking is known to be the most labor-intensive and costly task in which the employees account for a large part of the warehouse performance. Hence, many approaches exist, that optimize the order picking process based on diverse economic criteria. However, most of these approaches focus on a single economic objective at once and disregard ergonomic criteria in their optimization. Further, the influence of the placement of the items to be picked is underestimated and accordingly, too little attention is paid to the interdependence of these two problems. In this work, we aim at optimizing the storage assignment and the order picking problem within mezzanine warehouse with regards to their reciprocal influence. We propose a customized version of the Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II) for optimizing the storage assignment problem as well as an Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) algorithm for optimizing the order picking problem. Both algorithms incorporate multiple economic and ergonomic constraints simultaneously. Furthermore, the algorithms incorporate knowledge about the interdependence between both problems, aiming to improve the overall warehouse performance. Our evaluation results show that our proposed algorithms return better storage assignments and order pick routes compared to commonly used techniques for the following quality indicators for comparing Pareto fronts: Coverage, Generational Distance, Euclidian Distance, Pareto Front Size, and Inverted Generational Distance. Additionally, the evaluation regarding the interaction of both algorithms shows a better performance when combining both proposed algorithms.

title: A Case Study on Optimization of Warehouses
text: The rise of e-commerce has led to an unprecedented increase in warehouse demand, rendering traditional warehouse management systems inefficient. Warehouses are crucial to the global supply chain, and their optimization is vital to reduce costs, enhance customer satisfaction, and minimize environmental impact. This case study focuses on optimizing warehouse operations for a mid-sized e-commerce company, handling approximately 50,000 daily orders. We propose a novel, data-driven approach that leverages machine learning and constraint programming to optimize warehouse layout, inventory allocation, and order picking routes. Our methodology involves collecting and processing large-scale datasets on order patterns, inventory levels, and warehouse layouts. We develop a mixed-integer programming model that integrates these factors to generate optimal solutions. Using real-world data, we demonstrate a 23.4% reduction in order fulfillment time, a 17.6% decrease in labor costs, and a 12.9% increase in inventory turnover rate. Our approach also yields a 9.2% decrease in carbon emissions, primarily due to reduced transportation distances. We conduct a thorough sensitivity analysis to evaluate the robustness of our approach under varying demand patterns, inventory levels, and warehouse configurations. Our results show that the proposed approach outperforms traditional rule-based systems and heuristic methods, even in the presence of uncertainties and disruptions. This study contributes to the development of more efficient and sustainable warehouse management systems, providing insights for practitioners and researchers in the field of logistics and supply chain management.

title: Input-Specific Robustness Certification for Randomized Smoothing
text: Although randomized smoothing has demonstrated high certified robustness and superior scalability to other certified defenses, the high computational overhead of the robustness certification bottlenecks the practical applicability, as it depends heavily on the large sample approximation for estimating the confidence interval. In existing works, the sample size for the confidence interval is universally set and agnostic to the input for prediction. This Input-Agnostic Sampling (IAS) scheme may yield a poor Average Certified Radius (ACR)-runtime trade-off which calls for improvement. In this paper, we propose Input-Specific Sampling (ISS) acceleration to achieve the cost-effectiveness for robustness certification, in an adaptive way of reducing the sampling size based on the input characteristic. Furthermore, our method universally controls the certified radius decline from the ISS sample size reduction. The empirical results on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet show that ISS can speed up the certification by more than three times at a limited cost of 0.05 certified radius. Meanwhile, ISS surpasses IAS on the average certified radius across the extensive hyperparameter settings.
