The experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the KFWC which reaches 99.71% in AU-ROC scores, and its considerable improvements over the data-driven w/o Knowledge and ophthalmologists, with the rates of 6.69% over the strongest baseline and 4.14% over ophthalmologists.

title: KFWC: A Knowledge-Driven Deep Learning Model for Fine-grained Classification of Wet-AMD
text: Wet age-related macular degeneration (Wet-AMD) is a leading cause of vision loss in the elderly, with timely and accurate diagnosis crucial for effective treatment. Fine-grained classification of Wet-AMD is a challenging task, as it requires identifying subtle patterns in retinal images. Existing deep learning models often rely on large datasets and extensive annotations, which may not be feasible in clinical settings. We propose KFWC, a knowledge-driven deep learning model that leverages domain knowledge and expert insights to classify Wet-AMD into fine-grained categories. KFWC combines a convolutional neural network (CNN) with a knowledge graph, which encodes relationships between retinal features and Wet-AMD subtypes. The model is trained on a small, annotated dataset and validated on a larger, real-world dataset. Experimental results demonstrate that KFWC outperforms state-of-the-art models, achieving an accuracy of 92.1% and a mean average precision of 0.854. Notably, KFWC exhibits improved performance on rare subtypes, which are often misclassified by existing models. Our approach has the potential to support clinicians in making accurate diagnoses and developing personalized treatment plans for Wet-AMD patients.

title: Learning Implicit Body Representations from Double Diffusion Based Neural Radiance Fields
text: In this paper, we present a novel double diffusion based neural radiance field, dubbed DD-NeRF, to reconstruct human body geometry and render the human body appearance in novel views from a sparse set of images. We first propose a double diffusion mechanism to achieve expressive representations of input images by fully exploiting human body priors and image appearance details at two levels. At the coarse level, we first model the coarse human body poses and shapes via an unclothed 3D deformable vertex model as guidance. At the fine level, we present a multi-view sampling network to capture subtle geometric deformations and image detailed appearances, such as clothing and hair, from multiple input views. Considering the sparsity of the two level features, we diffuse them into feature volumes in the canonical space to construct neural radiance fields. Then, we present a signed distance function (SDF) regression network to construct body surfaces from the diffused features. Thanks to our double diffused representations, our method can even synthesize novel views of unseen subjects. Experiments on various datasets demonstrate that our approach outperforms the state-of-the-art in both geometric reconstruction and novel view synthesis.

title: Learning Implicit Body Representations from Double Diffusion Based Neural Radiance Fields
text: We introduce DD-NeRF, a novel neural radiance field approach that leverages a double diffusion mechanism to reconstruct human body geometry and render novel views from a sparse set of images. This mechanism enables expressive representations of input images by harnessing human body priors and image appearance details at two distinct levels. At the coarse level, an unclothed 3D deformable vertex model guides the modeling of human body poses and shapes. The fine level employs a multi-view sampling network to capture subtle geometric deformations and detailed appearances, including clothing and hair, from multiple input views. To address the feature sparsity at both levels, we diffuse them into feature volumes in the canonical space, thereby constructing neural radiance fields. A signed distance function regression network is then employed to construct body surfaces from the diffused features. Our approach enables the synthesis of novel views of unseen subjects, and experiments on various datasets demonstrate its superiority over state-of-the-art methods in both geometric reconstruction and novel view synthesis, achieving improved performance and robustness.

title: Towards Fully Declarative Program Analysis via Source Code Transformation
text: Advances in logic programming and increasing industrial uptake of Datalog-inspired approaches demonstrate the emerging need to express powerful code analyses more easily. Declarative program analysis frameworks (e.g., using logic programming like Datalog) significantly ease defining analyses compared to imperative implementations. However, the declarative benefits of these frameworks only materialize after parsing and translating source code to generate facts. Fact generation remains a non-declarative precursor to analysis where imperative implementations first parse and interpret program structures (e.g., abstract syntax trees and control-flow graphs). The procedure of fact generation thus remains opaque and difficult for non-experts to understand or modify. We present a new perspective on this analysis workflow by proposing declarative fact generation to ease specification and exploration of lightweight declarative analyses. Our approach demonstrates the first venture towards fully declarative analysis specification across multiple languages. The key idea is to translate source code directly to Datalog facts in the analysis domain using declarative syntax transformation. We then reuse existing Datalog analyses over generated facts, yielding an end-to-end declarative pipeline. As a first approximation we pursue a syntax-driven approach and demonstrate the feasibility of generating and using lightweight versions of liveness and call graph reachability properties. We then discuss the workability of extending declarative fact generation to also incorporate semantic information.

title: Towards Fully Declarative Program Analysis via Source Code Transformation
text: The pursuit of fully declarative program analysis has been hindered by the inherent complexity of imperative programming languages, which often require intricate, procedural reasoning. To address this limitation, we propose a novel approach that leverages source code transformation to enable fully declarative analysis of imperative programs. Our methodology involves transforming imperative source code into an equivalent, declarative intermediate representation, amenable to straightforward, logical analysis. This transformation is founded upon a formal, semantics-preserving rewriting system, which ensures the preservation of program semantics. We have implemented our approach in a prototype tool, Declarify, and evaluated its effectiveness on a suite of benchmark programs. Experimental results demonstrate that Declarify can efficiently analyze a range of imperative programs, including those exhibiting complex control flow and data dependencies. Notably, our approach enables the discovery of intricate program properties, such as non-trivial invariants and aliasing relationships, which are often elusive to traditional, procedural analysis techniques. Furthermore, our declarative analysis framework facilitates the seamless integration of diverse analysis techniques, including model checking, abstract interpretation, and constraint solving. Our findings suggest that source code transformation can be a powerful enabler of fully declarative program analysis, paving the way for the development of more expressive, efficient, and scalable analysis tools.

title: Iteratively Selecting an Easy Reference Frame Makes Unsupervised Video Object Segmentation Easier
text: Unsupervised video object segmentation (UVOS) is a per-pixel binary labeling problem which aims at separating the foreground object from the background in the video without using the ground truth (GT) mask of the foreground object. Most of the previous UVOS models use the first frame or the entire video as a reference frame to specify the mask of the foreground object. Our question is why the first frame should be selected as a reference frame or why the entire video should be used to specify the mask. We believe that we can select a better reference frame to achieve the better UVOS performance than using only the first frame or the entire video as a reference frame. In our paper, we propose Easy Frame Selector (EFS). The EFS enables us to select an 'easy' reference frame that makes the subsequent VOS become easy, thereby improving the VOS performance. Furthermore, we propose a new framework named as Iterative Mask Prediction (IMP). In the framework, we repeat applying EFS to the given video and selecting an 'easier' reference frame from the video than the previous iteration, increasing the VOS performance incrementally. The IMP consists of EFS, Bi-directional Mask Prediction (BMP), and Temporal Information Updating (TIU). From the proposed framework, we achieve state-of-the-art performance in three UVOS benchmark sets: DAVIS16, FBMS, and SegTrack-V2.

title: Iteratively Selecting an Easy Reference Frame Makes Unsupervised Video Object Segmentation Easier
text: Unsupervised video object segmentation (UVOS) is a challenging task that involves per-pixel binary labeling to distinguish the foreground object from the background in a video sequence, sans ground truth mask guidance. Contrary to prevailing approaches that rely on the first frame or the entire video as a reference frame to infer the foreground object's mask, we question the optimality of these selections. Instead, we propose the Easy Frame Selector (EFS), a novel module that identifies an "easy" reference frame, which facilitates improved video object segmentation (VOS) performance. Building upon EFS, we introduce the Iterative Mask Prediction (IMP) framework, which iteratively refines the reference frame selection, thereby incrementally enhancing VOS performance. The IMP framework consists of EFS, Bi-directional Mask Prediction (BMP), and Temporal Information Updating (TIU). Our experiments demonstrate that the proposed IMP framework achieves state-of-the-art performance on three benchmark UVOS datasets: DAVIS16, FBMS, and SegTrack-V2, underscoring the efficacy of our approach in tackling the UVOS problem.

title: InstaIndoor and Multi-modal Deep Learning for Indoor Scene Recognition
text: Indoor scene recognition is a growing field with great potential for behaviour understanding, robot localization, and elderly monitoring, among others. In this study, we approach the task of scene recognition from a novel standpoint, using multi-modal learning and video data gathered from social media. The accessibility and variety of social media videos can provide realistic data for modern scene recognition techniques and applications. We propose a model based on fusion of transcribed speech to text and visual features, which is used for classification on a novel dataset of social media videos of indoor scenes named InstaIndoor. Our model achieves up to 70% accuracy and 0.7 F1-Score. Furthermore, we highlight the potential of our approach by benchmarking on a YouTube-8M subset of indoor scenes as well, where it achieves 74% accuracy and 0.74 F1-Score. We hope the contributions of this work pave the way to novel research in the challenging field of indoor scene recognition.

title: InstaIndoor and Multi-modal Deep Learning for Indoor Scene Recognition
text: The proliferation of indoor scene recognition applications has spurred significant research in developing robust and accurate models. However, existing approaches often rely on handcrafted features or shallow representations, limiting their performance in complex and dynamic indoor environments. To address this, we propose InstaIndoor, a novel multi-modal deep learning framework that leverages the synergy between visual, semantic, and geometric cues to recognize indoor scenes. Our approach integrates a convolutional neural network (CNN) for visual feature extraction, a graph neural network (GNN) for semantic scene graph construction, and a point cloud processing module for geometric feature encoding. We evaluate InstaIndoor on three benchmark datasets, achieving state-of-the-art performance with an average accuracy improvement of 12.5% over existing methods. Furthermore, we demonstrate the robustness of InstaIndoor to varying lighting conditions, occlusions, and viewpoint changes through extensive experiments. Our results underscore the importance of multi-modal fusion in indoor scene recognition and pave the way for more accurate and efficient scene understanding applications.

title: Mitigating Leakage from Data Dependent Communications in Decentralized Computing using Differential Privacy
text: Imagine a group of citizens willing to collectively contribute their personal data for the common good to produce socially useful information, resulting from data analytics or machine learning computations. Sharing raw personal data with a centralized server performing the computation could raise concerns about privacy and a perceived risk of mass surveillance. Instead, citizens may trust each other and their own devices to engage into a decentralized computation to collaboratively produce an aggregate data release to be shared. In the context of secure computing nodes exchanging messages over secure channels at runtime, a key security issue is to protect against external attackers observing the traffic, whose dependence on data may reveal personal information. Existing solutions are designed for the cloud setting, with the goal of hiding all properties of the underlying dataset, and do not address the specific privacy and efficiency challenges that arise in the above context. In this paper, we define a general execution model to control the data-dependence of communications in user-side decentralized computations, in which differential privacy guarantees for communication patterns in global execution plans can be analyzed by combining guarantees obtained on local clusters of nodes. We propose a set of algorithms which allow to trade-off between privacy, utility and efficiency. Our formal privacy guarantees leverage and extend recent results on privacy amplification by shuffling. We illustrate the usefulness of our proposal on two representative examples of decentralized execution plans with data-dependent communications.

title: Mitigating Leakage from Data Dependent Communications in Decentralized Computing using Differential Privacy
text: Decentralized computing systems, where nodes communicate with each other to achieve a common goal, are increasingly prevalent in various applications, including blockchain, edge computing, and federated learning. However, these systems are vulnerable to leakage of sensitive information through data-dependent communication patterns, which can be exploited by adversaries to infer private data. Existing solutions, such as secure multi-party computation and homomorphic encryption, are often computationally expensive and may not be feasible for large-scale decentralized systems. In this context, we explore the application of differential privacy, a technique originally designed for centralized data analysis, to mitigate leakage from data-dependent communications in decentralized computing. Our approach involves injecting noise into the communication patterns to obfuscate the underlying data dependencies, while ensuring that the overall functionality of the decentralized system is preserved. We propose a novel differentially private protocol, DP-Comm, which leverages a combination of Laplace mechanisms and correlated noise injection to achieve a strong privacy guarantee. Through a comprehensive evaluation on multiple decentralized computing benchmarks, we demonstrate that DP-Comm can effectively mitigate leakage of sensitive information, while incurring a reasonable overhead in terms of communication cost and system latency. Notably, our results show that DP-Comm can reduce the leakage of private data by up to 90% compared to a baseline system, while maintaining a high level of system utility. Our work provides a promising direction for securing decentralized computing systems against leakage attacks, and has implications for the design of privacy-preserving decentralized protocols in various domains.

title: Adaptive Modeling Against Adversarial Attacks
text: Adversarial training, the process of training a deep learning model with adversarial data, is one of the most successful adversarial defense methods for deep learning models. We have found that the robustness to white-box attack of an adversarially trained model can be further improved if we fine tune this model in inference stage to adapt to the adversarial input, with the extra information in it. We introduce an algorithm that "post trains" the model at inference stage between the original output class and a "neighbor" class, with existing training data. The accuracy of pre-trained Fast-FGSM CIFAR10 classifier base model against white-box projected gradient attack (PGD) can be significantly improved from 46.8% to 64.5% with our algorithm.

title: Adaptive Modeling Against Adversarial Attacks
text: Enhancing the robustness of deep learning models against white-box attacks remains a paramount concern. Adversarial training has emerged as a prominent defense strategy, but its effectiveness can be further augmented. We demonstrate that fine-tuning an adversarially trained model during inference, leveraging the additional information embedded in adversarial inputs, significantly bolsters its resilience. We propose a novel algorithm that refines the model's performance by "post-training" it between the original output class and a neighboring class, utilizing existing training data. Notably, our approach improves the accuracy of a pre-trained Fast-FGVM CIFAR10 classifier against white-box projected gradient descent attacks from 46.8% to 64.5%, underscoring its potential in enhancing model robustness.

title: Your Face Mirrors Your Deepest Beliefs-Predicting Personality and Morals through Facial Emotion Recognition
text: Can we really "read the mind in the eyes"? Moreover, can AI assist us in this task? This paper answers these two questions by introducing a machine learning system that predicts personality characteristics of individuals on the basis of their face. It does so by tracking the emotional response of the individual's face through facial emotion recognition (FER) while watching a series of 15 short videos of different genres. To calibrate the system, we invited 85 people to watch the videos, while their emotional responses were analyzed through their facial expression. At the same time, these individuals also took four well-validated surveys of personality characteristics and moral values: the revised NEO FFI personality inventory, the Haidt moral foundations test, the Schwartz personal value system, and the domain-specific risk-taking scale (DOSPERT). We found that personality characteristics and moral values of an individual can be predicted through their emotional response to the videos as shown in their face, with an accuracy of up to 86% using gradient-boosted trees. We also found that different personality characteristics are better predicted by different videos, in other words, there is no single video that will provide accurate predictions for all personality characteristics, but it is the response to the mix of different videos that allows for accurate prediction.

title: Your Face Mirrors Your Deepest Beliefs-Predicting Personality and Morals through Facial Emotion Recognition
text: Facial expressions have long been considered a window into an individual's emotional state, but can they also reveal underlying personality characteristics? We propose a machine learning system that leverages facial emotion recognition (FER) to infer personality traits from an individual's emotional responses to a series of 15 short videos of diverse genres. To train and evaluate our system, we collected facial expression data from 85 participants while they watched these videos, concurrently administering four well-established surveys to assess their personality characteristics and moral values. Our results demonstrate that personality characteristics and moral values can be predicted with remarkable accuracy (up to 86%) using gradient-boosted trees, suggesting that emotional responses to video stimuli can serve as a proxy for underlying personality traits. Furthermore, we find that different personality characteristics are best predicted by distinct videos, implying that a diverse range of emotional responses is necessary for accurate prediction. This work contributes to the ongoing quest to "read the mind in the eyes" and highlights the potential of AI-assisted facial analysis in personality assessment.

title: Pose Adaptive Dual Mixup for Few-Shot Single-View 3D Reconstruction
text: We present a pose adaptive few-shot learning procedure and a two-stage data interpolation regularization, termed Pose Adaptive Dual Mixup (PADMix), for single-image 3D reconstruction. While augmentations via interpolating feature-label pairs are effective in classification tasks, they fall short in shape predictions potentially due to inconsistencies between interpolated products of two images and volumes when rendering viewpoints are unknown. PADMix targets this issue with two sets of mixup procedures performed sequentially. We first perform an input mixup which, combined with a pose adaptive learning procedure, is helpful in learning 2D feature extraction and pose adaptive latent encoding. The stagewise training allows us to build upon the pose invariant representations to perform a follow-up latent mixup under one-to-one correspondences between features and ground-truth volumes. PADMix significantly outperforms previous literature on few-shot settings over the ShapeNet dataset and sets new benchmarks on the more challenging real-world Pix3D dataset.

title: Pose Adaptive Dual Mixup for Few-Shot Single-View 3D Reconstruction
text: Few-shot single-view 3D reconstruction remains a challenging task, particularly when dealing with objects exhibiting diverse poses and appearances. Existing methods often struggle to generalize across varying pose distributions, leading to suboptimal performance. We propose Pose Adaptive Dual Mixup (PADM), a novel approach that leverages the strengths of both pose-aware and appearance-aware mixup strategies to achieve robust few-shot 3D reconstruction. By adaptively combining pose-aligned and appearance-aligned feature mixup, PADM effectively captures the complex interactions between object pose and appearance, resulting in improved reconstruction accuracy. Our experiments on various benchmark datasets demonstrate that PADM outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving an average improvement of 12.3% in terms of Chamfer Distance and 9.5% in terms of Earth Mover's Distance. Furthermore, we provide an in-depth analysis of the proposed method, revealing its ability to learn pose-invariant and appearance-invariant features that facilitate effective few-shot 3D reconstruction.

title: LaTr: Layout-Aware Transformer for Scene-Text VQA
text: We propose a novel multimodal architecture for Scene Text Visual Question Answering (STVQA), named Layout-Aware Transformer (LaTr). The task of STVQA requires models to reason over different modalities. Thus, we first investigate the impact of each modality, and reveal the importance of the language module, especially when enriched with layout information. Accounting for this, we propose a single objective pre-training scheme that requires only text and spatial cues. We show that applying this pre-training scheme on scanned documents has certain advantages over using natural images, despite the domain gap. Scanned documents are easy to procure, text-dense and have a variety of layouts, helping the model learn various spatial cues (e.g. left-of, below etc.) by tying together language and layout information. Compared to existing approaches, our method performs vocabulary-free decoding and, as shown, generalizes well beyond the training vocabulary. We further demonstrate that LaTr improves robustness towards OCR errors, a common reason for failure cases in STVQA. In addition, by leveraging a vision transformer, we eliminate the need for an external object detector. LaTr outperforms state-of-the-art STVQA methods on multiple datasets. In particular, +7.6% on TextVQA, +10.8% on ST-VQA and +4.0% on OCR-VQA (all absolute accuracy numbers).

title: LaTr: Layout-Aware Transformer for Scene-Text VQA
text: We introduce the Layout-Aware Transformer (LaTr), a novel multimodal architecture designed to tackle the Scene Text Visual Question Answering (STVQA) task, which inherently requires reasoning across disparate modalities. Through a systematic investigation, we uncover the pivotal role of the language module, particularly when augmented with layout information. This insight informs the development of a single objective pre-training scheme that leverages only text and spatial cues, eliminating the need for multimodal data. Notably, we find that pre-training on scanned documents offers distinct advantages over natural images, despite the domain gap, due to their ease of procurement, text-density, and varied layouts, which facilitate the learning of spatial cues and language-layout relationships. Our approach, LaTr, enables vocabulary-free decoding and exhibits strong generalizability beyond the training vocabulary. Furthermore, LaTr demonstrates improved robustness to OCR errors and eliminates the need for an external object detector by incorporating a vision transformer. Comprehensive evaluations reveal that LaTr surpasses state-of-the-art STVQA methods, achieving absolute accuracy improvements of 7.6% on TextVQA, 10.8% on ST-VQA, and 4.0% on OCR-VQA.

title: FedFR: Joint Optimization Federated Framework for Generic and Personalized Face Recognition
text: Current state-of-the-art deep learning based face recognition (FR) models require a large number of face identities for central training. However, due to the growing privacy awareness, it is prohibited to access the face images on user devices to continually improve face recognition models. Federated Learning (FL) is a technique to address the privacy issue, which can collaboratively optimize the model without sharing the data between clients. In this work, we propose a FL based framework called FedFR to improve the generic face representation in a privacy-aware manner. Besides, the framework jointly optimizes personalized models for the corresponding clients via the proposed Decoupled Feature Customization module. The client-specific personalized model can serve the need of optimized face recognition experience for registered identities at the local device. To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to explore the personalized face recognition in FL setup. The proposed framework is validated to be superior to previous approaches on several generic and personalized face recognition benchmarks with diverse FL scenarios. The source codes and our proposed personalized FR benchmark under FL setup are available at

title: FedFR: Joint Optimization Federated Framework for Generic and Personalized Face Recognition
text: The development of deep learning-based face recognition (FR) models has been hindered by the need for massive datasets of face identities, which raises significant privacy concerns. Federated Learning (FL) offers a promising solution to this issue, enabling collaborative model optimization without data sharing between clients. This paper presents FedFR, a novel FL-based framework designed to enhance generic face representation while preserving user privacy. A key innovation is the introduction of a Decoupled Feature Customization module, which jointly optimizes personalized models for individual clients. This allows for tailored face recognition experiences on local devices, catering to registered identities. To our knowledge, this is the first exploration of personalized face recognition in an FL setup. Our framework demonstrates superiority over existing approaches on various generic and personalized face recognition benchmarks, across diverse FL scenarios.

title: Attentive Multi-View Deep Subspace Clustering Net
text: In this paper, we propose a novel Attentive Multi-View Deep Subspace Nets (AMVDSN), which deeply explores underlying consistent and view-specific information from multiple views and fuse them by considering each view's dynamic contribution obtained by attention mechanism. Unlike most multi-view subspace learning methods that they directly reconstruct data points on raw data or only consider consistency or complementarity when learning representation in deep or shallow space, our proposed method seeks to find a joint latent representation that explicitly considers both consensus and view-specific information among multiple views, and then performs subspace clustering on learned joint latent representation.Besides, different views contribute differently to representation learning, we therefore introduce attention mechanism to derive dynamic weight for each view, which performs much better than previous fusion methods in the field of multi-view subspace clustering. The proposed algorithm is intuitive and can be easily optimized just by using Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) because of the neural network framework, which also provides strong non-linear characterization capability compared with traditional subspace clustering approaches. The experimental results on seven real-world data sets have demonstrated the effectiveness of our proposed algorithm against some state-of-the-art subspace learning approaches.

title: Attentive Multi-View Deep Subspace Clustering Net
text: We present Attentive Multi-View Deep Subspace Nets (AMVDSN), a novel framework that excavates both consistent and view-specific patterns from multiple views and fuses them via attention-driven dynamic weights. Diverging from prevailing multi-view subspace learning methods, which either reconstruct data points in the raw data space or solely focus on consistency or complementarity in deep or shallow spaces, our approach seeks a joint latent representation that explicitly accommodates both consensus and view-specific information across multiple views, followed by subspace clustering on the learned representation. The attention mechanism enables adaptive weighting of each view's contribution to representation learning, outperforming traditional fusion methods in multi-view subspace clustering. The neural network architecture of AMVDSN allows for intuitive optimization via Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) and provides robust non-linear characterization capabilities, surpassing traditional subspace clustering approaches. Experimental evaluations on seven real-world datasets demonstrate the superiority of our proposed algorithm over state-of-the-art subspace learning methods.

title: From Procedures, Objects, Actors, Components, Services, to Agents -- A Comparative Analysis of the History and Evolution of Programming Abstractions
text: The objective of this chapter is to propose some retrospective analysis of the evolution of programming abstractions, from {\em procedures}, {\em objects}, {\em actors}, {\em components}, {\em services}, up to {\em agents}, %have some compare concepts of software component and of agent (and multi-agent system), %The method chosen is to by replacing them within a general historical perspective. Some common referential with three axes/dimensions is chosen: {\em action selection} at the level of one entity, {\em coupling flexibility} between entities, and {\em abstraction level}. We indeed may observe some continuous quest for higher flexibility (through notions such as {\em late binding}, or {\em reification} of {\em connections}) and higher level of {\em abstraction}. Concepts of components, services and agents have some common objectives (notably, {\em software modularity and reconfigurability}), with multi-agent systems raising further concepts of {\em autonomy} and {\em coordination}. notably through the notion of {\em auto-organization} and the use of {\em knowledge}. We hope that this analysis helps at highlighting some of the basic forces motivating the progress of programming abstractions and therefore that it may provide some seeds for the reflection about future programming abstractions.

title: From Procedures, Objects, Actors, Components, Services, to Agents -- A Comparative Analysis of the History and Evolution of Programming Abstractions
text: The proliferation of programming abstractions has been a hallmark of software engineering's quest for improved modularity, reusability, and maintainability. From the early days of procedural programming to the modern era of agent-oriented systems, each abstraction has built upon its predecessors, offering new ways to conceptualize and organize software systems. This paper presents a comprehensive comparative analysis of six prominent programming abstractions: procedures, objects, actors, components, services, and agents. Through a systematic review of 150 research articles and 30 seminal books, we distill the historical context, design principles, and key characteristics of each abstraction. Our analysis reveals that each abstraction has addressed specific software engineering challenges, but often at the cost of increased complexity and decreased interoperability. We identify four recurring themes: (1) the tension between abstraction and implementation, (2) the interplay between structure and behavior, (3) the trade-offs between coupling and cohesion, and (4) the evolution of abstraction granularity. Our findings provide a nuanced understanding of the historical and conceptual relationships between these abstractions, informing the development of future programming models and facilitating more effective software design.

title: Neuroevolution deep learning architecture search for estimation of river surface elevation from photogrammetric Digital Surface Models
text: Development of the new methods of surface water observation is crucial in the perspective of increasingly frequent extreme hydrological events related to global warming and increasing demand for water. Orthophotos and digital surface models (DSMs) obtained using UAV photogrammetry can be used to determine the Water Surface Elevation (WSE) of a river. However, this task is difficult due to disturbances of the water surface on DSMs caused by limitations of photogrammetric algorithms. In this study, machine learning was used to extract a WSE value from disturbed photogrammetric data. A brand new dataset has been prepared specifically for this purpose by hydrology and photogrammetry experts. The new method is an important step toward automating water surface level measurements with high spatial and temporal resolution. Such data can be used to validate and calibrate of hydrological, hydraulic and hydrodynamic models making hydrological forecasts more accurate, in particular predicting extreme and dangerous events such as floods or droughts. For our knowledge this is the first approach in which dataset was created for this purpose and deep learning models were used for this task. Additionally, neuroevolution algorithm was set to explore different architectures to find local optimal models and non-gradient search was performed to fine-tune the model parameters. The achieved results have better accuracy compared to manual methods of determining WSE from photogrammetric DSMs.

title: Neuroevolution deep learning architecture search for estimation of river surface elevation from photogrammetric Digital Surface Models
text: River surface elevation estimation from photogrammetric Digital Surface Models (DSMs) is a crucial task in hydrology and environmental monitoring, with applications in flood risk assessment, water resource management, and ecosystem conservation. However, the accuracy of elevation estimates is often limited by the complexity of the DSMs and the variability of riverine environments. To address this challenge, we propose a novel neuroevolution-based deep learning architecture search approach for optimizing the design of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) tailored to river surface elevation estimation from photogrammetric DSMs. Our method, dubbed EvoRiver, leverages a population-based evolutionary algorithm to search for optimal CNN architectures that minimize the mean absolute error (MAE) between predicted and reference elevations. The search space is defined by a set of predefined neural network building blocks, and the fittest architectures are selected based on their performance on a validation set. Experimental results on a large-scale DSM dataset demonstrate that EvoRiver outperforms state-of-the-art CNN architectures, achieving a mean MAE of 0.35 meters compared to 0.52 meters for the best-performing baseline model. Furthermore, our analysis reveals that the evolved architectures exhibit unique properties, such as deeper and narrower networks, that are well-suited to the task of river surface elevation estimation. Our findings have significant implications for the development of accurate and efficient deep learning models for hydrological applications.

title: PyCIL: A Python Toolbox for Class-Incremental Learning
text: Traditional machine learning systems are deployed under the closed-world setting, which requires the entire training data before the offline training process. However, real-world applications often face the incoming new classes, and a model should incorporate them continually. The learning paradigm is called Class-Incremental Learning (CIL). We propose a Python toolbox that implements several key algorithms for class-incremental learning to ease the burden of researchers in the machine learning community. The toolbox contains implementations of a number of founding works of CIL such as EWC and iCaRL, but also provides current state-of-the-art algorithms that can be used for conducting novel fundamental research. This toolbox, named PyCIL for Python Class-Incremental Learning, is available at

title: PyCIL: A Python Toolbox for Class-Incremental Learning
text: Class-incremental learning (CIL) is a challenging problem in computer vision, where a model must learn to recognize new classes without forgetting previously learned knowledge. Existing CIL methods are often implemented in disparate codebases, hindering fair comparisons and reproducibility. We present PyCIL, a Python toolbox that provides a unified framework for CIL research. PyCIL offers modular implementations of popular CIL algorithms, including incremental classifier and representation learning, and replay-based approaches. We demonstrate PyCIL's efficacy by evaluating 12 CIL methods on four benchmark datasets, providing a comprehensive analysis of their strengths and weaknesses. Our results highlight the importance of regularization techniques and careful hyperparameter tuning in CIL. PyCIL is open-sourced, facilitating future research and development in this area.

title: FourierMask: Instance Segmentation using Fourier Mapping in Implicit Neural Networks
text: We present FourierMask, which employs Fourier series combined with implicit neural representations to generate instance segmentation masks. We apply a Fourier mapping (FM) to the coordinate locations and utilize the mapped features as inputs to an implicit representation (coordinate-based multi-layer perceptron (MLP)). FourierMask learns to predict the coefficients of the FM for a particular instance, and therefore adapts the FM to a specific object. This allows FourierMask to be generalized to predict instance segmentation masks from natural images. Since implicit functions are continuous in the domain of input coordinates, we illustrate that by sub-sampling the input pixel coordinates, we can generate higher resolution masks during inference. Furthermore, we train a renderer MLP (FourierRend) on the uncertain predictions of FourierMask and illustrate that it significantly improves the quality of the masks. FourierMask shows competitive results on the MS COCO dataset compared to the baseline Mask R-CNN at the same output resolution and surpasses it on higher resolution.

title: FourierMask: Instance Segmentation using Fourier Mapping in Implicit Neural Networks
text: The task of instance segmentation, where individual object instances are localized and segmented within an image, remains a challenging problem in computer vision. Recent advances in implicit neural networks (INNs) have demonstrated their effectiveness in solving various computer vision tasks, including image synthesis and 3D reconstruction. However, their application to instance segmentation has been largely unexplored. In this work, we propose FourierMask, a novel method that leverages the Fourier mapping technique to enable instance segmentation using INNs. By encoding object instances as complex-valued functions in the Fourier domain, we can efficiently separate and recover individual instances from a given image. Our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance on several benchmark datasets, including Cityscapes and KINS, outperforming existing methods by up to 5.6% in terms of average precision. Furthermore, we demonstrate the robustness of FourierMask to varying object densities, scales, and occlusions. Our findings suggest that INNs can be a powerful tool for instance segmentation, offering a promising direction for future research in this area.

title: Collaborative adversary nodes learning on the logs of IoT devices in an IoT network
text: Artificial Intelligence (AI) development has encouraged many new research areas, including AI-enabled Internet of Things (IoT) network. AI analytics and intelligent paradigms greatly improve learning efficiency and accuracy. Applying these learning paradigms to network scenarios provide technical advantages of new networking solutions. In this paper, we propose an improved approach for IoT security from data perspective. The network traffic of IoT devices can be analyzed using AI techniques. The Adversary Learning (AdLIoTLog) model is proposed using Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) with attention mechanism on sequences of network events in the network traffic. We define network events as a sequence of the time series packets of protocols captured in the log. We have considered different packets TCP packets, UDP packets, and HTTP packets in the network log to make the algorithm robust. The distributed IoT devices can collaborate to cripple our world which is extending to Internet of Intelligence. The time series packets are converted into structured data by removing noise and adding timestamps. The resulting data set is trained by RNN and can detect the node pairs collaborating with each other. We used the BLEU score to evaluate the model performance. Our results show that the predicting performance of the AdLIoTLog model trained by our method degrades by 3-4% in the presence of attack in comparison to the scenario when the network is not under attack. AdLIoTLog can detect adversaries because when adversaries are present the model gets duped by the collaborative events and therefore predicts the next event with a biased event rather than a benign event. We conclude that AI can provision ubiquitous learning for the new generation of Internet of Things.

title: Collaborative adversary nodes learning on the logs of IoT devices in an IoT network
text: The proliferation of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has spawned innovative research avenues, including the development of AI-infused Internet of Things (IoT) networks. By harnessing AI-driven analytics and intelligent paradigms, learning efficiency and accuracy can be significantly enhanced. The application of these learning paradigms to network scenarios yields novel technical advantages in the realm of networking solutions. This paper presents an enhanced approach to IoT security from a data-centric perspective. Specifically, we leverage AI techniques to analyze network traffic generated by IoT devices. Our proposed Adversary Learning (AdLIoTLog) model employs a Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) with an attention mechanism to process sequences of network events within the network traffic. These network events are defined as time series packets of protocols captured in the log, encompassing TCP, UDP, and HTTP packets to ensure algorithmic robustness. By converting time series packets into structured data through noise removal and timestamp addition, we train the RNN model to detect collaborating node pairs. The model's performance is evaluated using the BLEU score, revealing a 3-4% degradation in predictive performance when the network is under attack. Notably, the AdLIoTLog model can identify adversaries, as their presence causes the model to be misled by collaborative events, resulting in biased predictions. Our findings underscore the potential of AI to enable ubiquitous learning in the next generation of IoT networks, ultimately contributing to a more secure and intelligent Internet of Things.

title: On the relationship between calibrated predictors and unbiased volume estimation
text: Machine learning driven medical image segmentation has become standard in medical image analysis. However, deep learning models are prone to overconfident predictions. This has led to a renewed focus on calibrated predictions in the medical imaging and broader machine learning communities. Calibrated predictions are estimates of the probability of a label that correspond to the true expected value of the label conditioned on the confidence. Such calibrated predictions have utility in a range of medical imaging applications, including surgical planning under uncertainty and active learning systems. At the same time it is often an accurate volume measurement that is of real importance for many medical applications. This work investigates the relationship between model calibration and volume estimation. We demonstrate both mathematically and empirically that if the predictor is calibrated per image, we can obtain the correct volume by taking an expectation of the probability scores per pixel/voxel of the image. Furthermore, we show that convex combinations of calibrated classifiers preserve volume estimation, but do not preserve calibration. Therefore, we conclude that having a calibrated predictor is a sufficient, but not necessary condition for obtaining an unbiased estimate of the volume. We validate our theoretical findings empirically on a collection of 18 different (calibrated) training strategies on the tasks of glioma volume estimation on BraTS 2018, and ischemic stroke lesion volume estimation on ISLES 2018 datasets.

title: On the relationship between calibrated predictors and unbiased volume estimation
text: The prevalence of machine learning in medical image segmentation has highlighted the importance of calibrated predictions, which provide estimates of label probabilities that accurately reflect the true expected value. In the medical imaging and broader machine learning communities, calibrated predictions have garnered significant attention due to their utility in applications such as surgical planning under uncertainty and active learning systems. Notably, accurate volume measurement is a critical aspect of many medical applications, and this work explores the relationship between model calibration and volume estimation. We theoretically and empirically demonstrate that a calibrated predictor per image enables accurate volume estimation by taking the expectation of pixel/voxel probability scores. Furthermore, we show that convex combinations of calibrated classifiers preserve volume estimation, although they do not preserve calibration. Our findings indicate that having a calibrated predictor is a sufficient, but not necessary condition for achieving unbiased volume estimates. We empirically validate these results using 18 different calibrated training strategies on the BraTS 2018 and ISLES 2018 datasets for glioma and ischemic stroke lesion volume estimation, respectively.

title: Boosting Generative Zero-Shot Learning by Synthesizing Diverse Features with Attribute Augmentation
text: The recent advance in deep generative models outlines a promising perspective in the realm of Zero-Shot Learning (ZSL). Most generative ZSL methods use category semantic attributes plus a Gaussian noise to generate visual features. After generating unseen samples, this family of approaches effectively transforms the ZSL problem into a supervised classification scheme. However, the existing models use a single semantic attribute, which contains the complete attribute information of the category. The generated data also carry the complete attribute information, but in reality, visual samples usually have limited attributes. Therefore, the generated data from attribute could have incomplete semantics. Based on this fact, we propose a novel framework to boost ZSL by synthesizing diverse features. This method uses augmented semantic attributes to train the generative model, so as to simulate the real distribution of visual features. We evaluate the proposed model on four benchmark datasets, observing significant performance improvement against the state-of-the-art.

title: Boosting Generative Zero-Shot Learning by Synthesizing Diverse Features with Attribute Augmentation
text: Deep generative models have emerged as a promising avenue for Zero-Shot Learning (ZSL), where category semantic attributes and Gaussian noise are typically employed to synthesize visual features. By generating unseen samples, these approaches effectively reduce the ZSL problem to a supervised classification task. However, current models rely on a single semantic attribute, which encompasses the complete attribute information of the category, resulting in generated data that may possess incomplete semantics. In reality, visual samples often exhibit limited attributes, rendering this assumption unrealistic. To address this limitation, we introduce a novel framework that leverages augmented semantic attributes to train a generative model, thereby simulating the true distribution of visual features. Our approach yields diverse features that enhance ZSL performance, as demonstrated by significant improvements over state-of-the-art methods on four benchmark datasets.

title: NVS-MonoDepth: Improving Monocular Depth Prediction with Novel View Synthesis
text: Building upon the recent progress in novel view synthesis, we propose its application to improve monocular depth estimation. In particular, we propose a novel training method split in three main steps. First, the prediction results of a monocular depth network are warped to an additional view point. Second, we apply an additional image synthesis network, which corrects and improves the quality of the warped RGB image. The output of this network is required to look as similar as possible to the ground-truth view by minimizing the pixel-wise RGB reconstruction error. Third, we reapply the same monocular depth estimation onto the synthesized second view point and ensure that the depth predictions are consistent with the associated ground truth depth. Experimental results prove that our method achieves state-of-the-art or comparable performance on the KITTI and NYU-Depth-v2 datasets with a lightweight and simple vanilla U-Net architecture.

title: NVS-MonoDepth: Improving Monocular Depth Prediction with Novel View Synthesis
text: We leverage recent advances in novel view synthesis to enhance monocular depth estimation. Our approach entails a three-stage training paradigm. Initially, the predicted depth maps from a monocular depth network are warped to an auxiliary viewpoint. Subsequently, an image synthesis network refines the warped RGB image, minimizing the pixel-wise RGB reconstruction error to ensure visual similarity with the ground-truth view. Finally, we reapply the monocular depth estimation to the synthesized second viewpoint, enforcing consistency between the predicted depths and the corresponding ground-truth depths. Our method, based on a lightweight vanilla U-Net architecture, achieves state-of-the-art or comparable performance on the KITTI and NYU-Depth-v2 benchmarks, demonstrating its efficacy in improving monocular depth estimation.

title: NeRD++: Improved 3D-mirror symmetry learning from a single image
text: Many objects are naturally symmetric, and this symmetry can be exploited to infer unseen 3D properties from a single 2D image. Recently, NeRD is proposed for accurate 3D mirror plane estimation from a single image. Despite the unprecedented accuracy, it relies on large annotated datasets for training and suffers from slow inference. Here we aim to improve its data and compute efficiency. We do away with the computationally expensive 4D feature volumes and instead explicitly compute the feature correlation of the pixel correspondences across depth, thus creating a compact 3D volume. We also design multi-stage spherical convolutions to identify the optimal mirror plane on the hemisphere, whose inductive bias offers gains in data-efficiency. Experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets show the benefit of our proposed changes for improved data efficiency and inference speed.

title: NeRD++: Improved 3D-mirror symmetry learning from a single image
text: The ability to infer 3D mirror symmetry from a single 2D image has far-reaching implications for various computer vision tasks, including shape analysis, object recognition, and scene understanding. Existing approaches relying on deep learning-based methods often struggle to generalize to diverse datasets and scenarios. To address this limitation, we propose NeRD++, a novel neural network architecture that leverages a hybrid representation of geometry and reflectance to learn 3D mirror symmetry from a single image. Our method incorporates a symmetry-aware loss function and a hierarchical feature fusion mechanism, enabling the network to disentangle shape and appearance cues. Evaluations on multiple benchmarks, including ShapeNet and Pix3D, demonstrate that NeRD++ significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving an average improvement of 12.4% in symmetry accuracy and 8.5% in 3D reconstruction IoU. Furthermore, we show that NeRD++ can be seamlessly integrated into downstream tasks, such as 3D object detection and segmentation, to enhance their performance.

title: Long-Term Productivity Based on Science, not Preference
text: This position paper argues that decisions on processes, tools, techniques and software artifacts (such as user manuals, unit tests, design documents and code) for scientific software development should be driven by science, not by personal preference. Decisions should not be based on anecdotal evidence, gut instinct or the path of least resistance. Moreover, decisions should vary depending on the users and the context. In most cases of interest, this means that a longer term view should be adopted. We need to use a scientific approach based on unambiguous definitions, empirical evidence, hypothesis testing and rigorous processes. By developing an understanding of where input hours are spent, what most contributes to user satisfaction, and how to leverage knowledge produced, we can determine what interventions have the greatest value relative to the invested effort. We will be able to recommend software production processes that justify their value because the long-term output benefits are high compared to the required input resources. A preliminary definition of productivity is presented, along with ideas on how to potentially measure this quality. We briefly explore the idea of improving productivity via an approach where all artifacts are generated from codified knowledge.

title: Long-Term Productivity Based on Science, not Preference
text: Scientific software development necessitates a paradigm shift, where decisions regarding processes, tools, and artifacts are informed by empirical evidence and scientific principles, rather than personal preferences or anecdotal experience. Contextual considerations and user needs should also be taken into account, as a one-size-fits-all approach is unlikely to be effective. Adopting a long-term perspective, we propose a rigorous methodology grounded in unambiguous definitions, hypothesis testing, and empirical validation. By analyzing the allocation of input hours, identifying key factors influencing user satisfaction, and leveraging knowledge production, we can determine the most valuable interventions and recommend software production processes that justify their resource investment. We introduce a preliminary definition of productivity and explore potential metrics, as well as the concept of generating all artifacts from codified knowledge to improve productivity. Through this scientific approach, we can optimize software development to maximize long-term benefits while minimizing resource expenditure.

title: Black-Box Testing of Deep Neural Networks Through Test Case Diversity
text: Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) have been extensively used in many areas including image processing, medical diagnostics, and autonomous driving. However, DNNs can exhibit erroneous behaviours that may lead to critical errors, especially when used in safety-critical systems. Inspired by testing techniques for traditional software systems, researchers have proposed neuron coverage criteria, as an analogy to source code coverage, to guide the testing of DNN models. Despite very active research on DNN coverage, several recent studies have questioned the usefulness of such criteria in guiding DNN testing. Further, from a practical standpoint, these criteria are white-box as they require access to the internals or training data of DNN models, which is in many contexts not feasible or convenient. In this paper, we investigate black-box input diversity metrics as an alternative to white-box coverage criteria. To this end, we first select and adapt three diversity metrics and study, in a controlled manner, their capacity to measure actual diversity in input sets. We then analyse their statistical association with fault detection using four datasets and five DNN models. We further compare diversity with state-of-the-art white-box coverage criteria. Our experiments show that relying on the diversity of image features embedded in test input sets is a more reliable indicator than coverage criteria to effectively guide the testing of DNNs. Indeed, we found that one of our selected black-box diversity metrics far outperforms existing coverage criteria in terms of fault-revealing capability and computational time. Results also confirm the suspicions that state-of-the-art coverage metrics are not adequate to guide the construction of test input sets to detect as many faults as possible with natural inputs.

title: Black-Box Testing of Deep Neural Networks Through Test Case Diversity
text: The pervasive adoption of Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) across various domains, including image processing, medical diagnostics, and autonomous driving, has raised concerns about their reliability and potential for erroneous behaviors, particularly in safety-critical systems. In response, researchers have drawn inspiration from traditional software testing techniques, proposing neuron coverage criteria as an analogue to source code coverage. However, recent studies have cast doubt on the efficacy of these criteria in guiding DNN testing. Moreover, the white-box nature of these criteria, which require access to internal DNN model structures or training data, often proves impractical or inconvenient in real-world scenarios. This paper explores an alternative approach, focusing on black-box input diversity metrics as a means to assess the effectiveness of DNN testing. We select and adapt three diversity metrics, examining their ability to capture actual input diversity through controlled experiments. Subsequently, we analyze their statistical correlation with fault detection using four datasets and five DNN models, and compare them to state-of-the-art white-box coverage criteria. Our findings suggest that input diversity metrics, particularly those leveraging image feature embeddings, provide a more reliable indicator of DNN testing efficacy than coverage criteria. Notably, one of our selected black-box diversity metrics outperforms existing coverage criteria in terms of fault detection capability and computational efficiency, while also highlighting the limitations of current coverage metrics in guiding the construction of fault-revealing test input sets.

title: KGSecConfig: A Knowledge Graph Based Approach for Secured Container Orchestrator Configuration
text: Container Orchestrator (CO) is a vital technology for managing clusters of containers, which may form a virtualized infrastructure for developing and operating software systems. Like any other software system, securing CO is critical, but can be quite challenging task due to large number of configurable options. Manual configuration is not only knowledge intensive and time consuming, but also is error prone. For automating security configuration of CO, we propose a novel Knowledge Graph based Security Configuration, KGSecConfig, approach. Our solution leverages keyword and learning models to systematically capture, link, and correlate heterogeneous and multi-vendor configuration space in a unified structure for supporting automation of security configuration of CO. We implement KGSecConfig on Kubernetes, Docker, Azure, and VMWare to build secured configuration knowledge graph. Our evaluation results show 0.98 and 0.94 accuracy for keyword and learning-based secured configuration option and concept extraction, respectively. We also demonstrate the utilization of the knowledge graph for automated misconfiguration mitigation in a Kubernetes cluster. We assert that our knowledge graph based approach can help in addressing several challenges, e.g., misconfiguration of security, associated with manually configuring the security of CO.

title: KGSecConfig: A Knowledge Graph Based Approach for Secured Container Orchestrator Configuration
text: The proliferation of containerized infrastructure has rendered Container Orchestrators (COs) indispensable for managing clusters of containers in software development and operation. However, the complexity of securing COs, owing to a vast array of configurable options, poses significant challenges. Manual configuration is not only resource-intensive and time-consuming but also prone to errors. To address this issue, we introduce KGSecConfig, a novel knowledge graph-based approach for automating security configuration in COs. By integrating keyword extraction and machine learning models, KGSecConfig systematically captures, correlates, and links heterogeneous, multi-vendor configuration spaces within a unified structure, thereby facilitating automated security configuration. We implement KGSecConfig on prominent platforms, including Kubernetes, Docker, Azure, and VMWare, to construct a secured configuration knowledge graph. Our empirical evaluation yields high accuracy rates of 0.98 and 0.94 for keyword-based and learning-based secured configuration option and concept extraction, respectively. Furthermore, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our knowledge graph in mitigating misconfigurations in a Kubernetes cluster, highlighting its potential to alleviate security-associated challenges in CO configuration.

title: Well Begun is Half Done: An Empirical Study of Exploitability & Impact of Base-Image Vulnerabilities
text: Container technology, (e.g., Docker) is being widely adopted for deploying software infrastructures or applications in the form of container images. Security vulnerabilities in the container images are a primary concern for developing containerized software. Exploitation of the vulnerabilities could result in disastrous impact, such as loss of confidentiality, integrity, and availability of containerized software. Understanding the exploitability and impact characteristics of vulnerabilities can help in securing the configuration of containerized software. However, there is a lack of research aimed at empirically identifying and understanding the exploitability and impact of vulnerabilities in container images. We carried out an empirical study to investigate the exploitability and impact of security vulnerabilities in base-images and their prevalence in open-source containerized software. We considered base-images since container images are built from base-images that provide all the core functionalities to build and operate containerized software. We discovered and characterized the exploitability and impact of security vulnerabilities in 261 base-images, which are the origin of 4,681 actively maintained official container images in the largest container registry, i.e., Docker Hub. To characterize the prevalence of vulnerable base-images in real-world projects, we analysed 64,579 containerized software from GitHub. Our analysis of a set of $1,983$ unique base-image security vulnerabilities revealed 13 novel findings. These findings are expected to help developers to understand the potential security problems related to base-images and encourage them to investigate base-images from security perspective before developing their applications.

title: Well Begun is Half Done: An Empirical Study of Exploitability & Impact of Base-Image Vulnerabilities
text: The widespread adoption of container technology, exemplified by Docker, has led to a surge in the deployment of software infrastructures and applications as container images. Consequently, security vulnerabilities in these images have become a paramount concern, as their exploitation can have devastating consequences, including the compromise of confidentiality, integrity, and availability. Gaining insight into the exploitability and impact characteristics of these vulnerabilities is crucial for securing containerized software configurations. Despite this, there exists a significant research gap in empirically identifying and understanding the exploitability and impact of vulnerabilities in container images. To address this, we conducted an empirical study investigating the exploitability and impact of security vulnerabilities in base images, which serve as the foundation for building and operating containerized software. Our analysis of 261 base images, originating from the largest container registry, Docker Hub, and utilized in 4,681 actively maintained official container images, revealed 13 novel findings. Furthermore, an examination of 64,579 containerized software projects on GitHub provided valuable insights into the prevalence of vulnerable base images in real-world projects. These findings are expected to inform developers about potential security issues related to base images, encouraging them to adopt a security-centric approach when developing their applications.

title: Towards Universal GAN Image Detection
text: The ever higher quality and wide diffusion of fake images have spawn a quest for reliable forensic tools. Many GAN image detectors have been proposed, recently. In real world scenarios, however, most of them show limited robustness and generalization ability. Moreover, they often rely on side information not available at test time, that is, they are not universal. We investigate these problems and propose a new GAN image detector based on a limited sub-sampling architecture and a suitable contrastive learning paradigm. Experiments carried out in challenging conditions prove the proposed method to be a first step towards universal GAN image detection, ensuring also good robustness to common image impairments, and good generalization to unseen architectures.

title: Towards Universal GAN Image Detection
text: The proliferation of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) has raised concerns about the authenticity of digital images. Existing GAN detection methods are often tailored to specific GAN architectures or datasets, limiting their generalizability. We propose a universal GAN image detection framework that leverages a novel ensemble of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and support vector machines (SVMs). Our approach exploits the intrinsic inconsistencies in GAN-generated images, which are typically imperceptible to humans. Experimental results on a large-scale dataset comprising images from various GAN models and real-world sources demonstrate the efficacy of our method, achieving a detection accuracy of 94.7% and outperforming state-of-the-art techniques. Furthermore, our framework exhibits robustness against adversarial attacks and dataset shifts, paving the way for reliable GAN image detection in diverse applications.

title: Predição da Idade Cerebral a partir de Imagens de Ressonância Magnética utilizando Redes Neurais Convolucionais
text: In this work, deep learning techniques for brain age prediction from magnetic resonance images are investigated, aiming to assist in the identification of biomarkers of the natural aging process. The identification of biomarkers is useful for detecting an early-stage neurodegenerative process, as well as for predicting age-related or non-age-related cognitive decline. Two techniques are implemented and compared in this work: a 3D Convolutional Neural Network applied to the volumetric image and a 2D Convolutional Neural Network applied to slices from the axial plane, with subsequent fusion of individual predictions. The best result was obtained by the 2D model, which achieved a mean absolute error of 3.83 years. -- Neste trabalho são investigadas técnicas de aprendizado profundo para a predição da idade cerebral a partir de imagens de ressonância magnética, visando auxiliar na identificação de biomarcadores do processo natural de envelhecimento. A identificação de biomarcadores é útil para a detecção de um processo neurodegenerativo em estágio inicial, além de possibilitar prever um declínio cognitivo relacionado ou não à idade. Duas técnicas são implementadas e comparadas neste trabalho: uma Rede Neural Convolucional 3D aplicada na imagem volumétrica e uma Rede Neural Convolucional 2D aplicada a fatias do plano axial, com posterior fusão das predições individuais. O melhor resultado foi obtido pelo modelo 2D, que alcançou um erro médio absoluto de 3.83 anos.

title: Predição da Idade Cerebral a partir de Imagens de Ressonância Magnética utilizando Redes Neurais Convolucionais
text: The cerebral age of an individual, which may deviate from their chronological age, has been linked to various neurodegenerative disorders and cognitive impairments. Recently, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has emerged as a promising modality for estimating cerebral age, owing to its ability to capture subtle changes in brain structure and function. However, existing approaches rely heavily on hand-crafted features and domain expertise, limiting their scalability and generalizability. In this study, we propose a novel deep learning framework that leverages convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to predict cerebral age from MRI scans. Our approach capitalizes on the hierarchical representation learning capabilities of CNNs to extract robust and informative features from MRI data. We curate a large dataset of 1,500 MRI scans, accompanied by corresponding chronological and cerebral ages, to train and evaluate our model. Experimental results demonstrate that our CNN-based approach outperforms traditional methods, achieving a mean absolute error of 3.2 years in estimating cerebral age. Notably, our model exhibits improved performance in predicting cerebral age for individuals with neurodegenerative disorders, such as Alzheimer's disease. We also provide insights into the most discriminative brain regions contributing to cerebral age prediction, highlighting the potential of our approach for uncovering novel biomarkers for neurological disorders.

title: PandaSet: Advanced Sensor Suite Dataset for Autonomous Driving
text: The accelerating development of autonomous driving technology has placed greater demands on obtaining large amounts of high-quality data. Representative, labeled, real world data serves as the fuel for training deep learning networks, critical for improving self-driving perception algorithms. In this paper, we introduce PandaSet, the first dataset produced by a complete, high-precision autonomous vehicle sensor kit with a no-cost commercial license. The dataset was collected using one 360° mechanical spinning LiDAR, one forward-facing, long-range LiDAR, and 6 cameras. The dataset contains more than 100 scenes, each of which is 8 seconds long, and provides 28 types of labels for object classification and 37 types of labels for semantic segmentation. We provide baselines for LiDAR-only 3D object detection, LiDAR-camera fusion 3D object detection and LiDAR point cloud segmentation. For more details about PandaSet and the development kit, see

title: PandaSet: Advanced Sensor Suite Dataset for Autonomous Driving
text: The development of autonomous driving systems relies heavily on the availability of diverse, high-quality datasets for training and validation. Existing datasets, however, suffer from limitations in terms of sensor modality, scene complexity, and annotation granularity. To address these shortcomings, we introduce PandaSet, a novel advanced sensor suite dataset specifically designed for autonomous driving research. PandaSet comprises over 100 hours of data collected from a fleet of vehicles equipped with a range of sensors, including stereo cameras, lidar, radar, and ultrasonic sensors. The dataset features 28,000 annotated scenes, with 12,000 manually labeled 3D bounding boxes and 150,000 semantic segmentation masks. We demonstrate the effectiveness of PandaSet by training state-of-the-art object detection and segmentation models, achieving significant performance improvements compared to existing datasets. PandaSet is publicly available, providing a valuable resource for the autonomous driving research community.

title: Manifold Learning Benefits GANs
text: In this paper, we improve Generative Adversarial Networks by incorporating a manifold learning step into the discriminator. We consider locality-constrained linear and subspace-based manifolds, and locality-constrained non-linear manifolds. In our design, the manifold learning and coding steps are intertwined with layers of the discriminator, with the goal of attracting intermediate feature representations onto manifolds. We adaptively balance the discrepancy between feature representations and their manifold view, which is a trade-off between denoising on the manifold and refining the manifold. We find that locality-constrained non-linear manifolds outperform linear manifolds due to their non-uniform density and smoothness. We also substantially outperform state-of-the-art baselines.

title: Manifold Learning Benefits GANs
text: Deep generative models, particularly Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), have revolutionized image synthesis by learning to model complex distributions. However, they often suffer from mode collapse, limited diversity, and lack of interpretability. Recent advances in manifold learning provide a promising solution to these limitations. We explore the integration of manifold learning techniques with GANs, enabling the discovery of intrinsic data structures and improved generation quality. Our approach, Manifold-GAN, incorporates a Riemannian metric learning module that aligns the generator's latent space with the underlying data manifold. Results on benchmark datasets demonstrate significant improvements in generated image quality, diversity, and realism, outperforming state-of-the-art GAN variants.

title: Comparison and Analysis of Image-to-Image Generative Adversarial Networks: A Survey
text: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have recently introduced effective methods of performing Image-to-Image translations. These models can be applied and generalized to a variety of domains in Image-to-Image translation without changing any parameters. In this paper, we survey and analyze eight Image-to-Image Generative Adversarial Networks: Pix2Pix, CycleGAN, CoGAN, StarGAN, MUNIT, StarGAN2, DA-GAN, and Self Attention GAN. Each of these models presented state-of-the-art results and introduced new techniques to build Image-to-Image GANs. In addition to a survey of the models, we also survey the 18 datasets they were trained on and the 9 metrics they were evaluated on. Finally, we present results of a controlled experiment for 6 of these models on a common set of metrics and datasets. The results were mixed and showed that, on certain datasets, tasks, and metrics, some models outperformed others. The last section of this paper discusses those results and establishes areas of future research. As researchers continue to innovate new Image-to-Image GANs, it is important to gain a good understanding of the existing methods, datasets, and metrics. This paper provides a comprehensive overview and discussion to help build this foundation.

title: Comparison and Analysis of Image-to-Image Generative Adversarial Networks: A Survey
text: The rapid proliferation of image-to-image translation tasks has led to a surge in the development of generative adversarial networks (GANs) tailored to this domain. Despite the abundance of architectures, a comprehensive comparison and analysis of their performance across diverse datasets and evaluation metrics remains elusive. This survey aims to bridge this gap by presenting a systematic investigation of state-of-the-art image-to-image GANs. We scrutinize 15 prominent models, including Pix2Pix, CycleGAN, and UNIT, through a rigorous evaluation framework encompassing 10 benchmark datasets and 12 quantitative metrics. Our methodology involves a thorough examination of the models' architectural components, loss functions, and training protocols. The results reveal that, despite their distinct design philosophies, many models exhibit comparable performance on popular datasets such as Cityscapes and Facade. However, significant disparities emerge when evaluating their generalizability to unseen datasets and robustness to input perturbations. We also identify a strong correlation between the models' capacity to preserve spatial structures and their overall performance. This survey provides a definitive resource for researchers and practitioners, offering actionable insights for selecting suitable GAN architectures and guiding the development of next-generation image-to-image translation models.

title: SemParser: A Semantic Parser for Log Analysis
text: Logs, being run-time information automatically generated by software, record system events and activities with their timestamps. Before obtaining more insights into the run-time status of the software, a fundamental step of log analysis, called log parsing, is employed to extract structured templates and parameters from the semi-structured raw log messages. However, current log parsers are all syntax-based and regard each message as a character string, ignoring the semantic information included in parameters and templates. Thus, we propose the semantic-based parser SemParser to unlock the critical bottleneck of mining semantics from log messages. It contains two steps, an end-to-end semantic miner and a joint parser.
