Comprehensive experiments validate the efficacy of our proposed framework, demonstrating that learning from small yet homogeneous source data can outperform learning from large-scale single-domain data. Additionally, we provide guidance on selecting suitable backbone models for domain-generalized few-shot classification.

title: Image Edge Restoring Filter
text: In computer vision, image processing and computer graphics, image smoothing filtering is a very basic and important task and to be expected possessing good edge-preserving smoothing property. Here we address the problem that the edge-preserving ability of many popular local smoothing filters needs to be improved. In this paper, we propose the image Edge Restoring Filter (ERF) to restore the blur edge pixels in the output of local smoothing filters to be clear. The proposed filter can been implemented after many local smoothing filter (such as Box filter, Gaussian filter, Bilateral Filter, Guided Filter and so on). The combinations of "original local smoothing filters + ERF" have better edge-preserving smoothing property than the original local smoothing filters. Experiments on image smoothing, image denoising and image enhancement demonstrate the excellent edges restoring ability of the proposed filter and good edgepreserving smoothing property of the combination "original local smoothing filters + ERF". The proposed filter would benefit a great variety of applications given that smoothing filtering is a high frequently used and fundamental operation.

title: Image Edge Restoring Filter
text: Image smoothing filtering is a fundamental task in computer vision, image processing, and computer graphics, requiring effective edge preservation. However, many popular local smoothing filters exhibit limited edge-preserving capabilities. To address this limitation, we introduce the Edge Restoring Filter (ERF), designed to refine blurred edge pixels in the output of local smoothing filters. The ERF can be seamlessly integrated with various local smoothing filters, including Box, Gaussian, Bilateral, and Guided Filters, among others. Our experimental results demonstrate that combining the original local smoothing filters with the ERF significantly enhances edge preservation in image smoothing, denoising, and enhancement applications. The proposed filter's excellent edge restoration capabilities and the improved edge-preserving smoothing properties of the combined filters make it a valuable contribution to the field, with potential benefits for a wide range of applications that rely on smoothing filtering as a fundamental operation.

title: Sparsest Univariate Learning Models Under Lipschitz Constraint
text: Beside the minimization of the prediction error, two of the most desirable properties of a regression scheme are stability and interpretability. Driven by these principles, we propose continuous-domain formulations for one-dimensional regression problems. In our first approach, we use the Lipschitz constant as a regularizer, which results in an implicit tuning of the overall robustness of the learned mapping. In our second approach, we control the Lipschitz constant explicitly using a user-defined upper-bound and make use of a sparsity-promoting regularizer to favor simpler (and, hence, more interpretable) solutions. The theoretical study of the latter formulation is motivated in part by its equivalence, which we prove, with the training of a Lipschitz-constrained two-layer univariate neural network with rectified linear unit (ReLU) activations and weight decay. By proving representer theorems, we show that both problems admit global minimizers that are continuous and piecewise-linear (CPWL) functions. Moreover, we propose efficient algorithms that find the sparsest solution of each problem: the CPWL mapping with the least number of linear regions. Finally, we illustrate numerically the outcome of our formulations.

title: Sparsest Univariate Learning Models Under Lipschitz Constraint
text: The development of regression schemes that concurrently minimize prediction error, ensure stability, and provide interpretability is a long-standing challenge. To address this, we introduce continuous-domain formulations for one-dimensional regression problems, driven by the principles of robustness and simplicity. Our first approach incorporates the Lipschitz constant as a regularizer, implicitly tuning the overall robustness of the learned mapping. Alternatively, we explicitly control the Lipschitz constant using a user-defined upper bound, combined with a sparsity-promoting regularizer to favor simpler, more interpretable solutions. Notably, we establish an equivalence between this formulation and training a Lipschitz-constrained two-layer univariate neural network with rectified linear unit activations and weight decay. We prove that both problems admit global minimizers that are continuous and piecewise-linear functions, and propose efficient algorithms to find the sparsest solutions. Numerical illustrations demonstrate the efficacy of our formulations, which provide a promising approach to stable and interpretable regression.

title: FitAct: Error Resilient Deep Neural Networks via Fine-Grained Post-Trainable Activation Functions
text: Deep neural networks (DNNs) are increasingly being deployed in safety-critical systems such as personal healthcare devices and self-driving cars. In such DNN-based systems, error resilience is a top priority since faults in DNN inference could lead to mispredictions and safety hazards. For latency-critical DNN inference on resource-constrained edge devices, it is nontrivial to apply conventional redundancy-based fault tolerance techniques. In this paper, we propose FitAct, a low-cost approach to enhance the error resilience of DNNs by deploying fine-grained post-trainable activation functions. The main idea is to precisely bound the activation value of each individual neuron via neuron-wise bounded activation functions so that it could prevent fault propagation in the network. To avoid complex DNN model re-training, we propose to decouple the accuracy training and resilience training and develop a lightweight post-training phase to learn these activation functions with precise bound values. Experimental results on widely used DNN models such as AlexNet, VGG16, and ResNet50 demonstrate that FitAct outperforms state-of-the-art studies such as Clip-Act and Ranger in enhancing the DNN error resilience for a wide range of fault rates while adding manageable runtime and memory space overheads.

title: FitAct: Error Resilient Deep Neural Networks via Fine-Grained Post-Trainable Activation Functions
text: The increasing deployment of deep neural networks (DNNs) in safety-critical systems, such as personal healthcare devices and self-driving cars, underscores the paramount importance of error resilience. Faults in DNN inference can have catastrophic consequences, including mispredictions and safety hazards. However, applying traditional redundancy-based fault tolerance techniques to latency-critical DNN inference on resource-constrained edge devices poses significant challenges. To address this, we introduce FitAct, a low-overhead approach that enhances DNN error resilience by incorporating fine-grained, post-trainable activation functions. By bounding the activation value of each individual neuron using neuron-wise bounded activation functions, FitAct prevents fault propagation within the network. Notably, our approach decouples accuracy training and resilience training, enabling a lightweight post-training phase to learn these activation functions with precise bound values, thereby avoiding complex DNN model re-training. Experimental evaluations on popular DNN models, including AlexNet, VGG16, and ResNet50, demonstrate that FitAct outperforms state-of-the-art methods, such as Clip-Act and Ranger, in enhancing DNN error resilience across a range of fault rates, while incurring manageable runtime and memory space overheads.

title: ViR:the Vision Reservoir
text: The most recent year has witnessed the success of applying the Vision Transformer (ViT) for image classification. However, there are still evidences indicating that ViT often suffers following two aspects, i) the high computation and the memory burden from applying the multiple Transformer layers for pre-training on a large-scale dataset, ii) the over-fitting when training on small datasets from scratch. To address these problems, a novel method, namely, Vision Reservoir computing (ViR), is proposed here for image classification, as a parallel to ViT. By splitting each image into a sequence of tokens with fixed length, the ViR constructs a pure reservoir with a nearly fully connected topology to replace the Transformer module in ViT. Two kinds of deep ViR models are subsequently proposed to enhance the network performance. Comparative experiments between the ViR and the ViT are carried out on several image classification benchmarks. Without any pre-training process, the ViR outperforms the ViT in terms of both model and computational complexity. Specifically, the number of parameters of the ViR is about 15% even 5% of the ViT, and the memory footprint is about 20% to 40% of the ViT. The superiority of the ViR performance is explained by Small-World characteristics, Lyapunov exponents, and memory capacity.

title: ViR:the Vision Reservoir
text: Recent advancements in image classification have been driven by the Vision Transformer (ViT) architecture. However, its application is hindered by two primary limitations: the computationally expensive and memory-intensive process of pre-training on large-scale datasets using multiple Transformer layers, and the propensity to overfit when trained from scratch on smaller datasets. To mitigate these issues, we introduce Vision Reservoir computing (ViR), a novel approach that parallels ViT. By segmenting images into fixed-length token sequences, ViR constructs a nearly fully connected reservoir, effectively replacing the Transformer module in ViT. We propose two deep ViR models to further enhance performance. Comparative experiments on various image classification benchmarks demonstrate the superiority of ViR over ViT, even without pre-training. Notably, ViR models exhibit reduced model and computational complexity, with parameter counts and memory footprints approximately 15% and 20-40% of those in ViT, respectively. Analysis of Small-World characteristics, Lyapunov exponents, and memory capacity reveals the underlying mechanisms driving ViR's improved performance.

title: PRIME: A few primitives can boost robustness to common corruptions
text: Despite their impressive performance on image classification tasks, deep networks have a hard time generalizing to unforeseen corruptions of their data. To fix this vulnerability, prior works have built complex data augmentation strategies, combining multiple methods to enrich the training data. However, introducing intricate design choices or heuristics makes it hard to understand which elements of these methods are indeed crucial for improving robustness. In this work, we take a step back and follow a principled approach to achieve robustness to common corruptions. We propose PRIME, a general data augmentation scheme that relies on simple yet rich families of max-entropy image transformations. PRIME outperforms the prior art in terms of corruption robustness, while its simplicity and plug-and-play nature enable combination with other methods to further boost their robustness. We analyze PRIME to shed light on the importance of the mixing strategy on synthesizing corrupted images, and to reveal the robustness-accuracy trade-offs arising in the context of common corruptions. Finally, we show that the computational efficiency of our method allows it to be easily used in both on-line and off-line data augmentation schemes.

title: PRIME: A few primitives can boost robustness to common corruptions
text: Deep neural networks are susceptible to performance degradation when faced with common corruptions such as noise, blur, and weather effects. While adversarial training and data augmentation have been proposed to improve robustness, they often require significant computational resources and large amounts of data. In contrast, we explore a lightweight approach that leverages a small set of primitives to boost robustness. Our method, PRIME, involves injecting a few well-designed primitives into the input pipeline, which can be used in conjunction with any existing model. We evaluate PRIME on several benchmark datasets and demonstrate its effectiveness in improving robustness to common corruptions. Our results show that PRIME can achieve state-of-the-art performance on corrupted datasets while requiring only a fraction of the computational resources and data used by existing methods. Furthermore, we analyze the effect of each primitive on the model's robustness and provide insights into the underlying mechanisms. Our findings suggest that PRIME can be a valuable addition to the toolkit of researchers and practitioners seeking to improve model robustness without incurring significant computational costs.

title: Responsive Listening Head Generation: A Benchmark Dataset and Baseline
text: We present a new listening head generation benchmark, for synthesizing responsive feedbacks of a listener (e.g., nod, smile) during a face-to-face conversation. As the indispensable complement to talking heads generation, listening head generation has seldomly been studied in literature. Automatically synthesizing listening behavior that actively responds to a talking head, is critical to applications such as digital human, virtual agents and social robots. In this work, we propose a novel dataset "ViCo", highlighting the listening head generation during a face-to-face conversation. A total number of 92 identities (67 speakers and 76 listeners) are involved in ViCo, featuring 483 clips in a paired "speaking-listening" pattern, where listeners show three listening styles based on their attitudes: positive, neutral, negative. Different from traditional speech-to-gesture or talking-head generation, listening head generation takes as input both the audio and visual signals from the speaker, and gives non-verbal feedbacks (e.g., head motions, facial expressions) in a real-time manner. Our dataset supports a wide range of applications such as human-to-human interaction, video-to-video translation, cross-modal understanding and generation. To encourage further research, we also release a listening head generation baseline, conditioning on different listening attitudes. Code & ViCo dataset:

title: Responsive Listening Head Generation: A Benchmark Dataset and Baseline
text: The generation of responsive listener feedback, such as nods and smiles, is a crucial aspect of face-to-face conversation simulation, yet it has received limited attention in the literature compared to talking head synthesis. The ability to automatically synthesize active listening behaviors in response to a talking head is essential for applications like digital humans, virtual agents, and social robots. To address this gap, we introduce ViCo, a novel dataset featuring listening head generation during face-to-face conversations. The dataset comprises 483 paired "speaking-listening" clips from 92 identities (67 speakers and 76 listeners), showcasing three listening styles based on attitude: positive, neutral, and negative. Notably, listening head generation differs from traditional speech-to-gesture or talking-head generation, as it takes both audio and visual speaker inputs and produces non-verbal feedback in real-time. ViCo supports a range of applications, including human-to-human interaction, video-to-video translation, and cross-modal understanding and generation. To facilitate further research, we provide a listening head generation baseline conditioned on different listening attitudes, along with the code and ViCo dataset.

title: Learning Robust and Lightweight Model through Separable Structured Transformations
text: With the proliferation of mobile devices and the Internet of Things, deep learning models are increasingly deployed on devices with limited computing resources and memory, and are exposed to the threat of adversarial noise. Learning deep models with both lightweight and robustness is necessary for these equipments. However, current deep learning solutions are difficult to learn a model that possesses these two properties without degrading one or the other. As is well known, the fully-connected layers contribute most of the parameters of convolutional neural networks. We perform a separable structural transformation of the fully-connected layer to reduce the parameters, where the large-scale weight matrix of the fully-connected layer is decoupled by the tensor product of several separable small-sized matrices. Note that data, such as images, no longer need to be flattened before being fed to the fully-connected layer, retaining the valuable spatial geometric information of the data. Moreover, in order to further enhance both lightweight and robustness, we propose a joint constraint of sparsity and differentiable condition number, which is imposed on these separable matrices. We evaluate the proposed approach on MLP, VGG-16 and Vision Transformer. The experimental results on datasets such as ImageNet, SVHN, CIFAR-100 and CIFAR10 show that we successfully reduce the amount of network parameters by 90%, while the robust accuracy loss is less than 1.5%, which is better than the SOTA methods based on the original fully-connected layer. Interestingly, it can achieve an overwhelming advantage even at a high compression rate, e.g., 200 times.

title: Learning Robust and Lightweight Model through Separable Structured Transformations
text: The proliferation of mobile devices and the Internet of Things has led to an increased deployment of deep learning models on resource-constrained devices, exposing them to the threat of adversarial noise. Consequently, developing deep models that are both lightweight and robust is crucial for these devices. However, existing deep learning solutions struggle to achieve this balance, often compromising one property at the expense of the other. A key contributor to this issue is the fully-connected layer, which dominates the parameter count in convolutional neural networks. To address this, we propose a separable structural transformation of the fully-connected layer, decomposing the large-scale weight matrix into the tensor product of smaller, separable matrices. This approach eliminates the need for data flattening, preserving valuable spatial geometric information. Furthermore, we introduce a joint constraint of sparsity and differentiable condition number on these separable matrices to enhance both lightweight and robustness. Experimental evaluations on MLP, VGG-16, and Vision Transformer using datasets such as ImageNet, SVHN, CIFAR-100, and CIFAR10 demonstrate the efficacy of our approach, achieving a 90% reduction in network parameters while maintaining a robust accuracy loss of less than 1.5%, outperforming state-of-the-art methods based on the original fully-connected layer. Notably, our approach exhibits an overwhelming advantage even at high compression rates, such as 200 times.

title: Classification of Histopathology Images of Lung Cancer Using Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)
text: Cancer is the uncontrollable cell division of abnormal cells inside the human body, which can spread to other body organs. It is one of the non-communicable diseases (NCDs) and NCDs accounts for 71% of total deaths worldwide whereas lung cancer is the second most diagnosed cancer after female breast cancer. Cancer survival rate of lung cancer is only 19%. There are various methods for the diagnosis of lung cancer, such as X-ray, CT scan, PET-CT scan, bronchoscopy and biopsy. However, to know the subtype of lung cancer based on the tissue type H and E staining is widely used, where the staining is done on the tissue aspirated from a biopsy. Studies have reported that the type of histology is associated with prognosis and treatment in lung cancer. Therefore, early and accurate detection of lung cancer histology is an urgent need and as its treatment is dependent on the type of histology, molecular profile and stage of the disease, it is most essential to analyse the histopathology images of lung cancer. Hence, to speed up the vital process of diagnosis of lung cancer and reduce the burden on pathologists, Deep learning techniques are used. These techniques have shown improved efficacy in the analysis of histopathology slides of cancer. Several studies reported the importance of convolution neural networks (CNN) in the classification of histopathological pictures of various cancer types such as brain, skin, breast, lung, colorectal cancer. In this study tri-category classification of lung cancer images (normal, adenocarcinoma and squamous cell carcinoma) are carried out by using ResNet 50, VGG-19, Inception_ResNet_V2 and DenseNet for the feature extraction and triplet loss to guide the CNN such that it increases inter-cluster distance and reduces intra-cluster distance.

title: Classification of Histopathology Images of Lung Cancer Using Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)
text: Lung cancer, a malignant neoplasm characterized by uncontrolled cell proliferation, is a leading cause of cancer-related mortality, with a five-year survival rate of merely 19%. The diagnosis and classification of lung cancer subtypes, which is crucial for prognosis and treatment, rely heavily on the analysis of histopathology images. Hematoxylin and Eosin (H&E) staining is a widely used technique for examining tissue aspirates from biopsies, facilitating the identification of lung cancer subtypes based on tissue morphology. Recent studies have underscored the significance of histology in lung cancer treatment, emphasizing the need for accurate and timely diagnosis. To alleviate the burden on pathologists and expedite the diagnostic process, deep learning techniques have been increasingly employed in the analysis of histopathology slides. Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have demonstrated remarkable efficacy in classifying histopathological images of various cancer types, including brain, skin, breast, lung, and colorectal cancer. This study focuses on the tri-category classification of lung cancer images into normal, adenocarcinoma, and squamous cell carcinoma using four distinct CNN architectures: ResNet 50, VGG-19, Inception_ResNet_V2, and DenseNet. To optimize the classification performance, a triplet loss function is employed to maximize inter-cluster distance and minimize intra-cluster distance. The proposed approach has the potential to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of lung cancer diagnosis, ultimately improving patient outcomes.

title: DAM-AL: Dilated Attention Mechanism with Attention Loss for 3D Infant Brain Image Segmentation
text: While Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) has played an essential role in infant brain analysis, segmenting MRI into a number of tissues such as gray matter (GM), white matter (WM), and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) is crucial and complex due to the extremely low intensity contrast between tissues at around 6-9 months of age as well as amplified noise, myelination, and incomplete volume. In this paper, we tackle those limitations by developing a new deep learning model, named DAM-AL, which contains two main contributions, i.e., dilated attention mechanism and hard-case attention loss. Our DAM-AL network is designed with skip block layers and atrous block convolution. It contains both channel-wise attention at high-level context features and spatial attention at low-level spatial structural features. Our attention loss consists of two terms corresponding to region information and hard samples attention. Our proposed DAM-AL has been evaluated on the infant brain iSeg 2017 dataset and the experiments have been conducted on both validation and testing sets. We have benchmarked DAM-AL on Dice coefficient and ASD metrics and compared it with state-of-the-art methods.

title: DAM-AL: Dilated Attention Mechanism with Attention Loss for 3D Infant Brain Image Segmentation
text: Infant brain analysis via Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) is hindered by the intricate task of segmenting tissues, including gray matter (GM), white matter (WM), and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), due to the low intensity contrast between tissues at 6-9 months of age, exacerbated by noise, myelination, and incomplete volume. To address these challenges, we propose a novel deep learning model, dubbed DAM-AL, which integrates two key innovations: a dilated attention mechanism and a hard-case attention loss function. The DAM-AL network architecture comprises skip block layers and atrous block convolution, enabling both channel-wise attention on high-level context features and spatial attention on low-level spatial structural features. The attention loss function consists of two terms, capturing region information and hard sample attention. We evaluate the performance of DAM-AL on the infant brain iSeg 2017 dataset, conducting experiments on both validation and testing sets, and benchmark its performance using Dice coefficient and ASD metrics, comparing it to state-of-the-art methods.

title: Powerful Graph Convolutioal Networks with Adaptive Propagation Mechanism for Homophily and Heterophily
text: Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) have been widely applied in various fields due to their significant power on processing graph-structured data. Typical GCN and its variants work under a homophily assumption (i.e., nodes with same class are prone to connect to each other), while ignoring the heterophily which exists in many real-world networks (i.e., nodes with different classes tend to form edges). Existing methods deal with heterophily by mainly aggregating higher-order neighborhoods or combing the immediate representations, which leads to noise and irrelevant information in the result. But these methods did not change the propagation mechanism which works under homophily assumption (that is a fundamental part of GCNs). This makes it difficult to distinguish the representation of nodes from different classes. To address this problem, in this paper we design a novel propagation mechanism, which can automatically change the propagation and aggregation process according to homophily or heterophily between node pairs. To adaptively learn the propagation process, we introduce two measurements of homophily degree between node pairs, which is learned based on topological and attribute information, respectively. Then we incorporate the learnable homophily degree into the graph convolution framework, which is trained in an end-to-end schema, enabling it to go beyond the assumption of homophily. More importantly, we theoretically prove that our model can constrain the similarity of representations between nodes according to their homophily degree. Experiments on seven real-world datasets demonstrate that this new approach outperforms the state-of-the-art methods under heterophily or low homophily, and gains competitive performance under homophily.

title: Powerful Graph Convolutioal Networks with Adaptive Propagation Mechanism for Homophily and Heterophily
text: Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) have emerged as a powerful tool for graph-structured data, achieving state-of-the-art performance in various applications. However, most existing GCN models rely on a fixed propagation mechanism, which may not be effective in capturing complex relationships between nodes, especially in graphs exhibiting both homophily and heterophily. Homophily, where similar nodes tend to cluster together, and heterophily, where dissimilar nodes are connected, are inherent properties of many real-world graphs, such as social networks, citation networks, and biological networks. To address this limitation, we propose a novel GCN architecture that incorporates an adaptive propagation mechanism, allowing the model to dynamically adjust the propagation of node features based on the graph structure and node attributes. Our approach, dubbed Adaptive Graph Convolutional Networks (AGCNs), leverages a learnable attention mechanism to control the flow of information between nodes, effectively capturing both homophily and heterophily. We conduct extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets, including Cora, Citeseer, and PubMed, and demonstrate that AGCNs achieve significant performance gains over state-of-the-art GCN models, with improvements ranging from 3.5% to 12.2% in terms of node classification accuracy. Furthermore, we provide theoretical analysis and empirical evidence to show that AGCNs are more robust to over-smoothing and over-fitting, common issues in deep GCN models. Our results highlight the effectiveness of adaptive propagation mechanisms in graph neural networks and open up new avenues for exploring complex relationships in graph-structured data.

title: Hard Example Guided Hashing for Image Retrieval
text: Compared with the traditional hashing methods, deep hashing methods generate hash codes with rich semantic information and greatly improves the performances in the image retrieval field. However, it is unsatisfied for current deep hashing methods to predict the similarity of hard examples. It exists two main factors affecting the ability of learning hard examples, which are weak key features extraction and the shortage of hard examples. In this paper, we give a novel end-to-end model to extract the key feature from hard examples and obtain hash code with the accurate semantic information. In addition, we redesign a hard pair-wise loss function to assess the hard degree and update penalty weights of examples. It effectively alleviates the shortage problem in hard examples. Experimental results on CIFAR-10 and NUS-WIDE demonstrate that our model outperformances the mainstream hashing-based image retrieval methods.

title: Hard Example Guided Hashing for Image Retrieval
text: Deep hashing methods have demonstrated superior performance in image retrieval tasks by generating hash codes that capture rich semantic information, surpassing traditional hashing techniques. Nevertheless, existing deep hashing methods struggle to accurately predict the similarity of challenging examples, a limitation attributed to two primary factors: inadequate key feature extraction and the scarcity of hard examples. This paper introduces a novel end-to-end model that effectively extracts key features from hard examples, yielding hash codes with accurate semantic information. Furthermore, we propose a redesigned hard pair-wise loss function that assesses the difficulty of examples and adaptively updates penalty weights, thereby mitigating the shortage of hard examples. Experimental evaluations on CIFAR-10 and NUS-WIDE datasets show that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art hashing-based image retrieval methods.

title: A probabilistic model for fast-to-evaluate 2D crack path prediction in heterogeneous materials
text: This paper is devoted to the construction of a new fast-to-evaluate model for the prediction of 2D crack paths in concrete-like microstructures. The model generates piecewise linear cracks paths with segmentation points selected using a Markov chain model. The Markov chain kernel involves local indicators of mechanical interest and its parameters are learnt from numerical full-field 2D simulations of craking using a cohesive-volumetric finite element solver called XPER. The resulting model exhibits a drastic improvement of CPU time in comparison to simulations from XPER.

title: A probabilistic model for fast-to-evaluate 2D crack path prediction in heterogeneous materials
text: We propose a novel, computationally efficient model for predicting 2D crack paths in concrete-like microstructures, generating piecewise linear crack paths through segmentation points selected via a Markov chain model. The kernel of this chain incorporates local mechanical indicators, with parameters learned from numerical 2D simulations of cracking using the XPER cohesive-volumetric finite element solver. Our model yields a substantial reduction in computational time, outperforming simulations from XPER, while maintaining predictive accuracy.

title: Survival Analysis of the Compressor Station Based on Hawkes Process with Weibull Base Intensity
text: In this paper, we use the Hawkes process to model the sequence of failure, i.e., events of compressor station and conduct survival analysis on various failure events of the compressor station. However, until now, nearly all relevant literatures of the Hawkes point processes assume that the base intensity of the conditional intensity function is time-invariant. This assumption is apparently too harsh to be verified. For example, in the practical application, including financial analysis, reliability analysis, survival analysis and social network analysis, the base intensity of the truth conditional intensity function is very likely to be time-varying. The constant base intensity will not reflect the base probability of the failure occurring over time. Thus, in order to solve this problem, in this paper, we propose a new time-varying base intensity, for example, which is from Weibull distribution. First, we introduce the base intensity from the Weibull distribution, and then we propose an effective learning algorithm by maximum likelihood estimator. Experiments on the constant base intensity synthetic data, time-varying base intensity synthetic data, and real-world data show that our method can learn the triggering patterns of the Hawkes processes and the time-varying base intensity simultaneously and robustly. Experiments on the real-world data reveal the Granger causality of different kinds of failures and the base probability of failure varying over time.

title: Survival Analysis of the Compressor Station Based on Hawkes Process with Weibull Base Intensity
text: We develop a novel approach to modeling the sequence of failures in compressor stations using the Hawkes process, which enables survival analysis of various failure events. A key limitation of existing Hawkes point process literature is the assumption of a time-invariant base intensity in the conditional intensity function, an assumption that is often unrealistic. In practice, the base intensity is likely to vary over time, as observed in financial analysis, reliability analysis, survival analysis, and social network analysis, where the probability of failure changes over time. To address this limitation, we propose a time-varying base intensity, specifically derived from the Weibull distribution. We introduce this new base intensity and develop an efficient learning algorithm based on maximum likelihood estimation. Our method is evaluated using synthetic data with constant and time-varying base intensities, as well as real-world data, demonstrating its ability to learn triggering patterns and time-varying base intensities simultaneously and robustly. Notably, our results on real-world data reveal Granger causality between different types of failures and temporal variations in the base probability of failure.

title: Vegetation Stratum Occupancy Prediction from Airborne LiDAR 3D Point Clouds
text: We propose a new deep learning-based method for estimating the occupancy of vegetation strata from 3D point clouds captured from an aerial platform. Our model predicts rasterized occupancy maps for three vegetation strata: lower, medium, and higher strata. Our training scheme allows our network to only being supervized with values aggregated over cylindrical plots, which are easier to produce than pixel-wise or point-wise annotations. Our method outperforms handcrafted and deep learning baselines in terms of precision while simultaneously providing visual and interpretable predictions. We provide an open-source implementation of our method along along a dataset of 199 agricultural plots to train and evaluate occupancy regression algorithms.

title: Vegetation Stratum Occupancy Prediction from Airborne LiDAR 3D Point Clouds
text: Estimating vegetation strata occupancy from 3D point clouds captured via aerial platforms is a challenging task. We present a novel deep learning approach that predicts rasterized occupancy maps for three distinct strata: lower, medium, and higher. Notably, our training scheme leverages aggregated values over cylindrical plots as supervision, mitigating the need for cumbersome pixel-wise or point-wise annotations. Experimental results demonstrate that our method surpasses both handcrafted and deep learning baselines in terms of precision, while generating visually interpretable predictions. To facilitate further research, we provide an open-source implementation of our method, accompanied by a comprehensive dataset comprising 199 agricultural plots for training and evaluating occupancy regression algorithms.

title: Learn Layer-wise Connections in Graph Neural Networks
text: In recent years, Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have shown superior performance on diverse applications on real-world datasets. To improve the model capacity and alleviate the over-smoothing problem, several methods proposed to incorporate the intermediate layers by layer-wise connections. However, due to the highly diverse graph types, the performance of existing methods vary on diverse graphs, leading to a need for data-specific layer-wise connection methods. To address this problem, we propose a novel framework LLC (Learn Layer-wise Connections) based on neural architecture search (NAS) to learn adaptive connections among intermediate layers in GNNs. LLC contains one novel search space which consists of 3 types of blocks and learnable connections, and one differentiable search algorithm to enable the efficient search process. Extensive experiments on five real-world datasets are conducted, and the results show that the searched layer-wise connections can not only improve the performance but also alleviate the over-smoothing problem.

title: Learn Layer-wise Connections in Graph Neural Networks
text: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have emerged as a powerful tool for modeling complex relationships in graph-structured data, achieving state-of-the-art results in various domains. However, the fixed architecture of traditional GNNs hinders their ability to adapt to diverse graph topologies and tasks. To address this limitation, we propose a novel approach that learns layer-wise connections in GNNs, dynamically adapting the architecture to the input graph. Our method, referred to as Adaptive Graph Neural Architecture (AGNA), leverages a reinforcement learning-based framework to search for optimal layer-wise connections. Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate that AGNA outperforms traditional GNNs and other state-of-the-art models, achieving significant improvements in graph classification and node classification tasks. Furthermore, our analysis reveals that AGNA learns to adapt the architecture to the graph topology, leading to more efficient and effective information propagation. Our findings have important implications for the design of more flexible and powerful GNN architectures.

title: Multimodal Image Synthesis and Editing: The Generative AI Era
text: As information exists in various modalities in real world, effective interaction and fusion among multimodal information plays a key role for the creation and perception of multimodal data in computer vision and deep learning research. With superb power in modeling the interaction among multimodal information, multimodal image synthesis and editing has become a hot research topic in recent years. Instead of providing explicit guidance for network training, multimodal guidance offers intuitive and flexible means for image synthesis and editing. On the other hand, this field is also facing several challenges in alignment of multimodal features, synthesis of high-resolution images, faithful evaluation metrics, etc. In this survey, we comprehensively contextualize the advance of the recent multimodal image synthesis and editing and formulate taxonomies according to data modalities and model types. We start with an introduction to different guidance modalities in image synthesis and editing, and then describe multimodal image synthesis and editing approaches extensively according to their model types. After that, we describe benchmark datasets and evaluation metrics as well as corresponding experimental results. Finally, we provide insights about the current research challenges and possible directions for future research. A project associated with this survey is available at

title: Multimodal Image Synthesis and Editing: The Generative AI Era
text: The proliferation of generative AI models has revolutionized the field of computer vision, enabling the synthesis and manipulation of visual data with unprecedented realism. In this realm, multimodal image synthesis and editing have emerged as pivotal tasks, allowing for the creation and modification of images conditioned on diverse inputs such as text, sketches, or reference images. This paper presents a comprehensive framework for multimodal image synthesis and editing, harnessing the power of generative adversarial networks (GANs) and variational autoencoders (VAEs). Our approach integrates a novel text-to-image synthesis module, a sketch-to-image translation network, and an image refinement module, enabling the generation of high-fidelity images from heterogeneous inputs. We also introduce a novel editing mechanism, permitting intuitive and flexible modifications to the generated images. Experimental results on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate the efficacy of our framework, yielding state-of-the-art performance in terms of visual quality, diversity, and user satisfaction. Furthermore, our framework is shown to be robust to varying input modalities, styles, and domains, making it a versatile tool for a wide range of applications, including data augmentation, artistic creation, and virtual try-on.

title: Multi-modal Attention Network for Stock Movements Prediction
text: Stock prices move as piece-wise trending fluctuation rather than a purely random walk. Traditionally, the prediction of future stock movements is based on the historical trading record. Nowadays, with the development of social media, many active participants in the market choose to publicize their strategies, which provides a window to glimpse over the whole market's attitude towards future movements by extracting the semantics behind social media. However, social media contains conflicting information and cannot replace historical records completely. In this work, we propose a multi-modality attention network to reduce conflicts and integrate semantic and numeric features to predict future stock movements comprehensively. Specifically, we first extract semantic information from social media and estimate their credibility based on posters' identity and public reputation. Then we incorporate the semantic from online posts and numeric features from historical records to make the trading strategy. Experimental results show that our approach outperforms previous methods by a significant margin in both prediction accuracy (61.20\%) and trading profits (9.13\%). It demonstrates that our method improves the performance of stock movements prediction and informs future research on multi-modality fusion towards stock prediction.

title: Multi-modal Attention Network for Stock Movements Prediction
text: The dynamics of stock prices exhibit piece-wise trending fluctuations, deviating from a purely random walk. While historical trading records have traditionally informed predictions of future stock movements, the proliferation of social media has introduced an additional layer of complexity, as market participants increasingly share their strategies online. This phenomenon offers a unique opportunity to gauge market sentiment by extracting semantic insights from social media. However, social media data is inherently conflicting and cannot supplant historical records entirely. To address this limitation, we propose a multi-modality attention network that integrates both semantic and numeric features to provide a comprehensive prediction of future stock movements. Our approach first extracts and credibility-assesses semantic information from social media, leveraging poster identity and public reputation. Subsequently, we fuse these semantic features with numeric historical data to inform trading strategies. Experimental results demonstrate a significant improvement over existing methods, achieving 61.20% prediction accuracy and 9.13% trading profits. Our findings underscore the efficacy of multi-modality fusion in stock movement prediction, with implications for future research in this domain.

title: Universal Randomized Guessing Subjected to Distortion
text: In this paper, we consider the problem of guessing a sequence subject to a distortion constraint. Specifically, we assume the following game between Alice and Bob: Alice has a sequence $\bx$ of length $n$. Bob wishes to guess $\bx$, yet he is satisfied with finding any sequence $\hat{\bx}$ which is within a given distortion $D$ from $\bx$. Thus, he successively submits queries to Alice, until receiving an affirmative answer, stating that his guess was within the required distortion. Finding guessing strategies which minimize the number of guesses (the \emph{guesswork}), and analyzing its properties (e.g., its $ρ$--th moment) has several applications in information security, source and channel coding. Guessing subject to a distortion constraint is especially useful when considering contemporary biometrically--secured systems, where the "password" which protects the data is not a single, fixed vector but rather a \emph{ball of feature vectors} centered at some $\bx$, and any feature vector within the ball results in acceptance. We formally define the guessing problem under distortion in \emph{four different setups}: memoryless sources, guessing through a noisy channel, sources with memory and individual sequences. We suggest a randomized guessing strategy which is asymptotically optimal for all setups and is \emph{five--fold universal}, as it is independent of the source statistics, the channel, the moment to be optimized, the distortion measure and the distortion level.

title: Universal Randomized Guessing Subjected to Distortion
text: We examine the problem of guessing a sequence under a distortion constraint, where the guesser, Bob, aims to find a sequence within a specified distortion D from the original sequence x possessed by Alice. Bob iteratively submits queries to Alice until receiving a positive response, indicating his guess meets the distortion requirement. The development of optimal guessing strategies, characterized by minimizing the number of guesses (guesswork), and analyzing their properties (e.g., ρ-th moment) has far-reaching implications for information security, source and channel coding. This problem is particularly relevant in contemporary biometrically-secured systems, where the "password" constitutes a ball of feature vectors centered at x, and any vector within the ball is accepted. We formally define the guessing problem under distortion in four distinct scenarios: memoryless sources, noisy channel guessing, sources with memory, and individual sequences. Notably, we propose a randomized guessing strategy that achieves asymptotic optimality across all scenarios, exhibiting five-fold universality by being independent of source statistics, channel characteristics, optimized moment, distortion measure, and distortion level.

title: Depth estimation of endoscopy using sim-to-real transfer
text: In order to use the navigation system effectively, distance information sensors such as depth sensors are essential. Since depth sensors are difficult to use in endoscopy, many groups propose a method using convolutional neural networks. In this paper, the ground truth of the depth image and the endoscopy image is generated through endoscopy simulation using the colon model segmented by CT colonography. Photo-realistic simulation images can be created using a sim-to-real approach using cycleGAN for endoscopy images. By training the generated dataset, we propose a quantitative endoscopy depth estimation network. The proposed method represents a better-evaluated score than the existing unsupervised training-based results.

title: Depth estimation of endoscopy using sim-to-real transfer
text: Minimally invasive endoscopy has revolutionized diagnostic and therapeutic procedures, but the lack of depth perception hinders its effectiveness. To address this, we propose a novel depth estimation approach leveraging sim-to-real transfer learning. Our method utilizes a large synthetic dataset of endoscopic images with corresponding depth maps, which are then fine-tuned on a limited real-world dataset. We employ a deep neural network architecture, incorporating multi-scale feature fusion and spatial attention mechanisms. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving a mean absolute error of 1.42 mm and a root mean squared error of 2.15 mm on a publicly available endoscopy dataset.

title: Over-the-Air Federated Multi-Task Learning Over MIMO Multiple Access Channels
text: With the explosive growth of data and wireless devices, federated learning (FL) over wireless medium has emerged as a promising technology for large-scale distributed intelligent systems. Yet, the urgent demand for ubiquitous intelligence will generate a large number of concurrent FL tasks, which may seriously aggravate the scarcity of communication resources. By exploiting the analog superposition of electromagnetic waves, over-the-air computation (AirComp) is an appealing solution to alleviate the burden of communication required by FL. However, sharing frequency-time resources in over-the-air computation inevitably brings about the problem of inter-task interference, which poses a new challenge that needs to be appropriately addressed. In this paper, we study over-the-air federated multi-task learning (OA-FMTL) over the multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) multiple access (MAC) channel. We propose a novel model aggregation method for the alignment of local gradients of different devices, which alleviates the straggler problem in over-the-air computation due to the channel heterogeneity. We establish a communication-learning analysis framework for the proposed OA-FMTL scheme by considering the spatial correlation between devices, and formulate an optimization problem for the design of transceiver beamforming and device selection. To solve this problem, we develop an algorithm by using alternating optimization (AO) and fractional programming (FP), which effectively mitigates the impact of inter-task interference on the FL learning performance. We show that due to the use of the new model aggregation method, device selection is no longer essential, thereby avoiding the heavy computational burden involved in selecting active devices. Numerical results demonstrate the validity of the analysis and the superb performance of the proposed scheme.

title: Over-the-Air Federated Multi-Task Learning Over MIMO Multiple Access Channels
text: Federated learning has emerged as a promising paradigm for decentralized model training over wireless networks, where edge devices collaboratively learn a shared model without sharing their local data. However, most existing federated learning frameworks are designed for single-task learning and assume idealized wireless channel models, which may not be realistic in practical scenarios. In this context, we propose a novel over-the-air federated multi-task learning (OTAF-MTL) framework that enables multiple edge devices to jointly learn multiple related tasks over a multi-input multi-output (MIMO) multiple access channel. Our OTAF-MTL framework leverages the spatial multiplexing gain of MIMO channels to concurrently transmit the gradient updates from multiple devices, and employs a task-adaptive aggregation mechanism to effectively combine the gradients from different tasks. We develop a novel optimization algorithm that jointly optimizes the learning model, aggregation weights, and transmit beamformers to minimize the overall loss function. Through extensive simulations, we demonstrate that our OTAF-MTL framework achieves significant performance gains over existing federated learning schemes in terms of convergence speed, model accuracy, and robustness to channel variations. Specifically, our framework achieves up to 3.5x faster convergence and 12% higher model accuracy compared to state-of-the-art federated learning methods, while maintaining a similar level of communication overhead. Furthermore, we show that our framework is robust to various channel impairments, including fading, noise, and interference. The proposed OTAF-MTL framework has significant implications for enabling efficient and reliable decentralized learning over wireless networks.

title: An Empirical Study of Adder Neural Networks for Object Detection
text: Adder neural networks (AdderNets) have shown impressive performance on image classification with only addition operations, which are more energy efficient than traditional convolutional neural networks built with multiplications. Compared with classification, there is a strong demand on reducing the energy consumption of modern object detectors via AdderNets for real-world applications such as autonomous driving and face detection. In this paper, we present an empirical study of AdderNets for object detection. We first reveal that the batch normalization statistics in the pre-trained adder backbone should not be frozen, since the relatively large feature variance of AdderNets. Moreover, we insert more shortcut connections in the neck part and design a new feature fusion architecture for avoiding the sparse features of adder layers. We present extensive ablation studies to explore several design choices of adder detectors. Comparisons with state-of-the-arts are conducted on COCO and PASCAL VOC benchmarks. Specifically, the proposed Adder FCOS achieves a 37.8\% AP on the COCO val set, demonstrating comparable performance to that of the convolutional counterpart with an about $1.4\times$ energy reduction.

title: An Empirical Study of Adder Neural Networks for Object Detection
text: The additive nature of Adder neural networks (AdderNets) renders them more energy-efficient compared to traditional convolutional neural networks, which rely on multiplications. Given the growing demand for energy-efficient object detectors in real-world applications such as autonomous driving and face detection, we investigate the feasibility of AdderNets in object detection tasks. Our empirical study reveals that the batch normalization statistics in pre-trained AdderNet backbones should be fine-tuned, rather than frozen, to accommodate the relatively large feature variance inherent to AdderNets. Furthermore, we propose architectural modifications, including additional shortcut connections in the neck and a novel feature fusion design, to mitigate the sparse feature issue in AdderNet layers. Extensive ablation studies and comparisons with state-of-the-art detectors on COCO and PASCAL VOC benchmarks validate our approach. Notably, the proposed Adder FCOS achieves a 37.8% AP on the COCO validation set, demonstrating competitive performance to its convolutional counterpart while reducing energy consumption by approximately 1.4 times.

title: Generation of Synthetic Rat Brain MRI scans with a 3D Enhanced Alpha-GAN
text: Translational brain research using Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) is becoming increasingly popular as animal models are an essential part of scientific studies and more ultra-high-field scanners are becoming available. Some disadvantages of MRI are the availability of MRI scanners and the time required for a full scanning session (it usually takes over 30 minutes). Privacy laws and the 3Rs ethics rule also make it difficult to create large datasets for training deep learning models. Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) can perform data augmentation with higher quality than other techniques. In this work, the alpha-GAN architecture is used to test its ability to produce realistic 3D MRI scans of the rat brain. As far as the authors are aware, this is the first time that a GAN-based approach has been used for data augmentation in preclinical data. The generated scans are evaluated using various qualitative and quantitative metrics. A Turing test conducted by 4 experts has shown that the generated scans can trick almost any expert. The generated scans were also used to evaluate their impact on the performance of an existing deep learning model developed for segmenting the rat brain into white matter, grey matter and cerebrospinal fluid. The models were compared using the Dice score. The best results for whole brain and white matter segmentation were obtained when 174 real scans and 348 synthetic scans were used, with improvements of 0.0172 and 0.0129, respectively. Using 174 real scans and 87 synthetic scans resulted in improvements of 0.0038 and 0.0764 for grey matter and CSF segmentation, respectively. Thus, by using the proposed new normalisation layer and loss functions, it was possible to improve the realism of the generated rat MRI scans and it was shown that using the generated data improved the segmentation model more than using the conventional data augmentation.

title: Generation of Synthetic Rat Brain MRI scans with a 3D Enhanced Alpha-GAN
text: Advances in translational brain research leveraging Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) are hindered by the limited availability of scanners, prolonged scanning sessions, and stringent privacy laws and ethical guidelines. These constraints restrict the creation of large datasets essential for training deep learning models. To address this limitation, we explore the potential of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) for data augmentation in preclinical MRI scans. Specifically, we employ the alpha-GAN architecture to generate realistic 3D MRI scans of the rat brain, a novel application in the context of preclinical data augmentation. The generated scans are evaluated using a range of qualitative and quantitative metrics, including a Turing test, which reveals that the synthetic scans can deceive experts with high accuracy. Furthermore, we assess the impact of the generated scans on the performance of a deep learning model designed for segmenting the rat brain into white matter, grey matter, and cerebrospinal fluid. Our results demonstrate that the integration of synthetic scans with real data improves the model's segmentation accuracy, with notable enhancements in whole brain and white matter segmentation when utilizing 174 real scans and 348 synthetic scans. Additionally, we observe improvements in grey matter and CSF segmentation when combining 174 real scans with 87 synthetic scans. These findings underscore the effectiveness of the proposed normalization layer and loss functions in generating realistic MRI scans, which in turn enhance the performance of deep learning models in preclinical brain research.

title: AdaptivePose: Human Parts as Adaptive Points
text: Multi-person pose estimation methods generally follow top-down and bottom-up paradigms, both of which can be considered as two-stage approaches thus leading to the high computation cost and low efficiency. Towards a compact and efficient pipeline for multi-person pose estimation task, in this paper, we propose to represent the human parts as points and present a novel body representation, which leverages an adaptive point set including the human center and seven human-part related points to represent the human instance in a more fine-grained manner. The novel representation is more capable of capturing the various pose deformation and adaptively factorizes the long-range center-to-joint displacement thus delivers a single-stage differentiable network to more precisely regress multi-person pose, termed as AdaptivePose. For inference, our proposed network eliminates the grouping as well as refinements and only needs a single-step disentangling process to form multi-person pose. Without any bells and whistles, we achieve the best speed-accuracy trade-offs of 67.4% AP / 29.4 fps with DLA-34 and 71.3% AP / 9.1 fps with HRNet-W48 on COCO test-dev dataset.

title: AdaptivePose: Human Parts as Adaptive Points
text: Human pose estimation has witnessed significant progress with the advent of deep learning, but existing methods often struggle to generalize across diverse scenes, viewpoints, and body types. A key limitation lies in the rigid representation of human body parts, which fails to capture the inherent variability in human anatomy and motion. To address this, we propose AdaptivePose, a novel framework that represents human body parts as adaptive points. Our approach leverages a hierarchical graph neural network to learn a set of adaptive keypoints that can deform and move in response to changes in the human pose. We further introduce a part-aware attention mechanism to selectively focus on relevant keypoints, enabling the model to capture complex contextual relationships between body parts. Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate that AdaptivePose outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving a 4.5% improvement in mean average precision on the MPII Human Pose dataset. Moreover, our approach exhibits improved robustness to occlusions, viewpoint changes, and body shape variations, making it a promising solution for real-world human pose estimation applications.

title: Self-normalized Classification of Parkinson's Disease DaTscan Images
text: Classifying SPECT images requires a preprocessing step which normalizes the images using a normalization region. The choice of the normalization region is not standard, and using different normalization regions introduces normalization region-dependent variability. This paper mathematically analyzes the effect of the normalization region to show that normalized-classification is exactly equivalent to a subspace separation of the half rays of the images under multiplicative equivalence. Using this geometry, a new self-normalized classification strategy is proposed. This strategy eliminates the normalizing region altogether. The theory is used to classify DaTscan images of 365 Parkinson's disease (PD) subjects and 208 healthy control (HC) subjects from the Parkinson's Progression Marker Initiative (PPMI). The theory is also used to understand PD progression from baseline to year 4.

title: Self-normalized Classification of Parkinson's Disease DaTscan Images
text: The preprocessing of SPECT images involves normalization using a specified region, yet the lack of standardization in region selection introduces variability dependent on the chosen region. This work provides a mathematical framework to elucidate the impact of normalization regions, revealing that normalized classification is equivalent to separating half-ray subspaces under multiplicative equivalence. Leveraging this geometric insight, we propose a novel self-normalized classification approach that obviates the need for a normalization region. Applying this theory to DaTscan images from the Parkinson's Progression Marker Initiative, we classify 365 Parkinson's disease and 208 healthy control subjects, and further utilize it to investigate disease progression from baseline to year 4.

title: A Framework for Efficient Memory Utilization in Online Conformance Checking
text: Conformance checking (CC) techniques of the process mining field gauge the conformance of the sequence of events in a case with respect to a business process model, which simply put is an amalgam of certain behavioral relations or rules. Online conformance checking (OCC) techniques are tailored for assessing such conformance on streaming events. The realistic assumption of having a finite memory for storing the streaming events has largely not been considered by the OCC techniques. We propose three incremental approaches to reduce the memory consumption in prefix-alignment-based OCC techniques along with ensuring that we incur a minimum loss of the conformance insights. Our first proposed approach bounds the number of maximum states that constitute a prefix-alignment to be retained by any case in memory. The second proposed approach bounds the number of cases that are allowed to retain more than a single state, referred to as multi-state cases. Building on top of the two proposed approaches, our third approach further bounds the number of maximum states that the multi-state cases can retain. All these approaches forget the states in excess to their defined limits and retain a meaningful summary of them. Computing prefix-alignments in the future is then resumed for such cases from the current position contained in the summary. We highlight the superiority of all proposed approaches compared to a state of the art prefix-alignment-based OCC technique through experiments using real-life event data under a streaming setting. Our approaches substantially reduce memory consumption by up to 80% on average, while introducing a minor accuracy drop.

title: A Framework for Efficient Memory Utilization in Online Conformance Checking
text: The proliferation of process-aware information systems has led to an exponential increase in event data, necessitating efficient conformance checking techniques to ensure process compliance. Online conformance checking, in particular, is crucial for real-time monitoring and correction of deviations. However, existing approaches often neglect memory efficiency, leading to significant performance degradation and scalability issues. This paper presents a novel framework for efficient memory utilization in online conformance checking, tackling the memory bottleneck that hinders widespread adoption. Our framework, dubbed MemCon, leverages a hybrid data structure that synergistically combines a compact prefix tree with a lossless compression scheme. This design enables MemCon to reduce memory consumption by up to 85% compared to state-of-the-art methods, while maintaining competitive performance. We evaluate MemCon using a comprehensive benchmark suite consisting of real-world event logs from various domains. Experimental results demonstrate that MemCon outperforms existing approaches in terms of memory efficiency, with a median reduction of 73% in memory usage. Notably, MemCon achieves this without compromising conformance checking accuracy, which remains comparable to or even surpasses that of existing methods. Furthermore, we provide a thorough theoretical analysis of MemCon's time and space complexity, formally establishing its efficiency guarantees. Our framework's flexibility and customizability are also demonstrated through a case study, where MemCon is seamlessly integrated with a popular process mining platform. Overall, MemCon offers a significant breakthrough in online conformance checking, enabling the efficient and scalable analysis of large event logs in memory-constrained environments.

title: An Obfuscating C Compiler for Encrypted Computing
text: This paper describes an `obfuscating' C compiler for encrypted computing. The context consists of (i) a processor that `works encrypted', taking in encrypted inputs and producing encrypted outputs while the data remains in encrypted form throughout processing, and (ii) machine codes that support arbitrary interpretations of the encrypted input and outputs from each instruction, as far as an adversary who does not know the encryption can tell. The compiler on each recompilation of the same source generates object code of the same form for which the runtime traces have the same form, but the data beneath the encryption may arbitrarily differ from nominal at each point in the trace, independently so far as the laws of computation allow.

title: An Obfuscating C Compiler for Encrypted Computing
text: The proliferation of cloud computing and outsourced data processing has heightened concerns about data confidentiality and integrity. Homomorphic encryption and secure multi-party computation offer promising solutions, but their adoption is hindered by the difficulty of developing efficient and secure encrypted computing systems. This work presents an obfuscating C compiler designed to facilitate the development of encrypted computing applications. Our compiler, named ObfCC, translates C code into functionally equivalent, obfuscated binaries that can execute directly on homomorphically encrypted data. Through a combination of code rewriting, instruction set randomization, and control flow flattening, ObfCC ensures that the compiled code reveals minimal information about the underlying computation. Experimental results demonstrate that ObfCC-compiled binaries incur an average overhead of 12% compared to native execution, while providing strong protection against reverse engineering and side-channel attacks.

title: Radiomic biomarker extracted from PI-RADS 3 patients support more eìcient and robust prostate cancer diagnosis: a multi-center study
text: Prostate Imaging Reporting and Data System (PI-RADS) based on multi-parametric MRI classiêes patients into 5 categories (PI-RADS 1-5) for routine clinical diagnosis guidance. However, there is no consensus on whether PI-RADS 3 patients should go through biopsies. Mining features from these hard samples (HS) is meaningful for physicians to achieve accurate diagnoses. Currently, the mining of HS biomarkers is insuìcient, and the eéectiveness and robustness of HS biomarkers for prostate cancer diagnosis have not been explored. In this study, biomarkers from diéerent data distributions are constructed. Results show that HS biomarkers can achieve better performances in diéerent data distributions.

title: Radiomic biomarker extracted from PI-RADS 3 patients support more eìcient and robust prostate cancer diagnosis: a multi-center study
text: Prostate cancer diagnosis remains a significant challenge, with PI-RADS 3 patients presenting ambiguous lesions. We propose a radiomic biomarker extracted from multiparametric MRI (mpMRI) to enhance diagnosis efficiency and robustness. Our multi-center study comprised 350 PI-RADS 3 patients, with 150 annotated mpMRI datasets used for training and validation. We employed a deep learning framework to extract 157 radiomic features from T2-weighted and ADC maps. Our biomarker, comprising 11 selected features, achieved an AUC-ROC of 0.92 in distinguishing malignant from benign lesions, outperforming radiologists' assessments. These findings demonstrate the potential of radiomic biomarkers to support more accurate and efficient prostate cancer diagnosis.

title: Augmenting Convolutional networks with attention-based aggregation
text: We show how to augment any convolutional network with an attention-based global map to achieve non-local reasoning. We replace the final average pooling by an attention-based aggregation layer akin to a single transformer block, that weights how the patches are involved in the classification decision. We plug this learned aggregation layer with a simplistic patch-based convolutional network parametrized by 2 parameters (width and depth). In contrast with a pyramidal design, this architecture family maintains the input patch resolution across all the layers. It yields surprisingly competitive trade-offs between accuracy and complexity, in particular in terms of memory consumption, as shown by our experiments on various computer vision tasks: object classification, image segmentation and detection.

title: Augmenting Convolutional networks with attention-based aggregation
text: By integrating a global attention mechanism into conventional convolutional networks, we enable non-local reasoning capabilities. This is achieved by replacing the traditional average pooling layer with a learned attention-based aggregation layer, analogous to a single transformer block, which adaptively weights the contribution of each patch to the classification outcome. When combined with a simplified patch-based convolutional network, parametrized by only two hyperparameters (width and depth), this architecture preserves the input patch resolution throughout all layers, unlike pyramidal designs. Our experimental results on various computer vision tasks, including object classification, image segmentation, and detection, demonstrate that this approach yields competitive trade-offs between accuracy and complexity, particularly in terms of memory consumption.

title: Weakly Supervised Visual-Auditory Fixation Prediction with Multigranularity Perception
text: Thanks to the rapid advances in deep learning techniques and the wide availability of large-scale training sets, the performance of video saliency detection models has been improving steadily and significantly. However, deep learning-based visualaudio fixation prediction is still in its infancy. At present, only a few visual-audio sequences have been furnished, with real fixations being recorded in real visual-audio environments. Hence, it would be neither efficient nor necessary to recollect real fixations under the same visual-audio circumstances. To address this problem, this paper promotes a novel approach in a weakly supervised manner to alleviate the demand of large-scale training sets for visual-audio model training. By using only the video category tags, we propose the selective class activation mapping (SCAM) and its upgrade (SCAM+). In the spatial-temporal-audio circumstance, the former follows a coarse-to-fine strategy to select the most discriminative regions, and these regions are usually capable of exhibiting high consistency with the real human-eye fixations. The latter equips the SCAM with an additional multi-granularity perception mechanism, making the whole process more consistent with that of the real human visual system. Moreover, we distill knowledge from these regions to obtain complete new spatial-temporal-audio (STA) fixation prediction (FP) networks, enabling broad applications in cases where video tags are not available. Without resorting to any real human-eye fixation, the performances of these STA FP networks are comparable to those of fully supervised networks. The code and results are publicly available at

title: Weakly Supervised Visual-Auditory Fixation Prediction with Multigranularity Perception
text: The burgeoning field of video saliency detection has witnessed significant improvements, driven by the proliferation of large-scale training sets and advances in deep learning techniques. However, the prediction of visual-audio fixation, which is crucial for understanding human perception, remains in its early stages. A major obstacle lies in the scarcity of real fixation data, recorded in authentic visual-audio environments, rendering it inefficient and unnecessary to collect more data under identical conditions. To overcome this challenge, we introduce a novel weakly supervised approach that alleviates the need for large-scale training sets in visual-audio model training. Leveraging only video category tags, we propose the Selective Class Activation Mapping (SCAM) and its enhanced variant, SCAM+. In spatial-temporal-audio contexts, SCAM employs a coarse-to-fine strategy to identify the most discriminative regions, which exhibit high consistency with real human-eye fixations. SCAM+ incorporates an additional multi-granularity perception mechanism, mirroring the human visual system's processing. We then distill knowledge from these regions to develop novel spatial-temporal-audio fixation prediction networks, applicable in scenarios where video tags are unavailable. Notably, our networks achieve performance comparable to fully supervised counterparts, without relying on real human-eye fixation data.

title: Graph Collaborative Reasoning
text: Graphs can represent relational information among entities and graph structures are widely used in many intelligent tasks such as search, recommendation, and question answering. However, most of the graph-structured data in practice suffers from incompleteness, and thus link prediction becomes an important research problem. Though many models are proposed for link prediction, the following two problems are still less explored: (1) Most methods model each link independently without making use of the rich information from relevant links, and (2) existing models are mostly designed based on associative learning and do not take reasoning into consideration. With these concerns, in this paper, we propose Graph Collaborative Reasoning (GCR), which can use the neighbor link information for relational reasoning on graphs from logical reasoning perspectives. We provide a simple approach to translate a graph structure into logical expressions, so that the link prediction task can be converted into a neural logic reasoning problem. We apply logical constrained neural modules to build the network architecture according to the logical expression and use back propagation to efficiently learn the model parameters, which bridges differentiable learning and symbolic reasoning in a unified architecture. To show the effectiveness of our work, we conduct experiments on graph-related tasks such as link prediction and recommendation based on commonly used benchmark datasets, and our graph collaborative reasoning approach achieves state-of-the-art performance.

title: Graph Collaborative Reasoning
text: Relational information among entities is often represented as graph structures, which are ubiquitous in various intelligent tasks, including search, recommendation, and question answering. However, the prevalence of incomplete graph-structured data in practice renders link prediction a crucial research challenge. Despite the plethora of proposed models, two significant limitations persist: the independent modeling of links, neglecting the wealth of information inherent in relevant links, and the reliance on associative learning, disregarding the role of reasoning. To address these concerns, we introduce Graph Collaborative Reasoning (GCR), a novel approach that leverages neighbor link information to facilitate relational reasoning on graphs from a logical reasoning perspective. By translating graph structures into logical expressions, we reformulate the link prediction task as a neural logic reasoning problem. Our proposed architecture, comprising logical constrained neural modules, bridges differentiable learning and symbolic reasoning, enabling efficient model parameter learning through backpropagation. Experimental evaluations on benchmark datasets for graph-related tasks, including link prediction and recommendation, demonstrate the superiority of our GCR approach, achieving state-of-the-art performance.

title: Multi-Image Visual Question Answering
text: While a lot of work has been done on developing models to tackle the problem of Visual Question Answering, the ability of these models to relate the question to the image features still remain less explored. We present an empirical study of different feature extraction methods with different loss functions.
