title: Deep-CNN based Robotic Multi-Class Under-Canopy Weed Control in Precision Farming
text: The development of smart weeding systems capable of performing plant-specific operations is crucial for sustainable agriculture and environmental stewardship. While significant progress has been made in autonomous robotic technologies for precision weed management, the challenge of under-canopy weeding in fields remains unaddressed. Accurate detection and classification of weeds are essential prerequisites for such systems to prevent misapplication of herbicides and damage to surrounding plants. Real-time multi-class weed identification enables species-specific treatment, thereby reducing herbicide usage. This study makes two primary contributions. First, we introduce AIWeeds, a large-scale, realistic image dataset comprising approximately 10,000 annotated images of flax and 14 common weeds in fields and gardens, captured from 20 locations in North Dakota, California, and Central China. Second, we provide a comprehensive pipeline for model training, optimization, and deployment on a single-board computer. Using AIWeeds and this pipeline, we establish a baseline for classification performance with five benchmark convolutional neural network (CNN) models. MobileNetV2 emerges as the top candidate for real-time applications due to its optimal balance of inference time and memory consumption. We deploy MobileNetV2 on our compact autonomous robot, SAMBot, for real-time weed detection in flax fields with row spacings of 0.2-0.3 m. The achieved test accuracy of 90% in previously unseen scenes, despite the presence of crops, weeds, distortion, blur, and shadows, marks a significant milestone towards precision weed control in real-world scenarios. The dataset and code for reproducing these results are publicly available.

title: Associative Adversarial Learning Based on Selective Attack
text: A human's attention can intuitively adapt to corrupted areas of an image by recalling a similar uncorrupted image they have previously seen. This observation motivates us to improve the attention of adversarial images by considering their clean counterparts. To accomplish this, we introduce Associative Adversarial Learning (AAL) into adversarial learning to guide a selective attack. We formulate the intrinsic relationship between attention and attack (perturbation) as a coupling optimization problem to improve their interaction. This leads to an attention backtracking algorithm that can effectively enhance the attention's adversarial robustness. Our method is generic and can be used to address a variety of tasks by simply choosing different kernels for the associative attention that select other regions for a specific attack. Experimental results show that the selective attack improves the model's performance. We show that our method improves the recognition accuracy of adversarial training on ImageNet by 8.32% compared with the baseline. It also increases object detection mAP on PascalVOC by 2.02% and recognition accuracy of few-shot learning on miniImageNet by 1.63%.

title: Associative Adversarial Learning Based on Selective Attack
text: Deep neural networks are vulnerable to adversarial attacks, which can significantly degrade their performance. Existing defense methods often rely on random or uniform perturbations, neglecting the inherent structure of the data and the attacker's strategy. To address this limitation, we propose an associative adversarial learning framework based on selective attack, which incorporates the attacker's behavior into the defense mechanism. Our approach consists of two key components: a selective attack module that generates targeted perturbations based on the input data's associative features, and a robustness-enhancing module that adaptively adjusts the model's parameters to counter the selective attacks. We evaluate our framework on several benchmark datasets, including ImageNet and CIFAR-10, and demonstrate its effectiveness in improving the robustness of deep neural networks against various types of attacks. Experimental results show that our method achieves significant improvements in robust accuracy, outperforming state-of-the-art defense methods by up to 12%. Furthermore, our framework provides valuable insights into the attacker's strategy, enabling the development of more effective defense mechanisms.

title: Mining and Classifying Privacy and Data Protection Requirements in Issue Reports
text: Digital and physical footprints are a trail of user activities collected over the use of software applications and systems. As software becomes ubiquitous, protecting user privacy has become challenging. With the increase of user privacy awareness and advent of privacy regulations and policies, there is an emerging need to implement software systems that enhance the protection of personal data processing. However, existing data protection and privacy regulations provide key principles in high-level, making it difficult for software engineers to design and implement privacy-aware systems. In this paper, we develop a taxonomy that provides a comprehensive set of privacy requirements based on four well-established personal data protection regulations and privacy frameworks, the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), ISO/IEC 29100, Thailand Personal Data Protection Act (Thailand PDPA) and Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) privacy framework. These requirements are extracted, refined and classified into a level that can be used to map with issue reports. We have also performed a study on how two large open-source software projects (Google Chrome and Moodle) address the privacy requirements in our taxonomy through mining their issue reports. The paper discusses how the collected issues were classified, and presents the findings and insights generated from our study. Mining and classifying privacy requirements in issue reports can help organisations be aware of their state of compliance by identifying privacy requirements that have not been addressed in their software projects. The taxonomy can also trace back to regulations, standards and frameworks that the software projects have not complied with based on the identified privacy requirements.

title: Mining and Classifying Privacy and Data Protection Requirements in Issue Reports
text: The proliferation of digital technologies has led to a surge in data-driven applications, resulting in a pressing need to ensure the privacy and security of sensitive information. Issue reports from software development projects, such as bug trackers and version control systems, often contain valuable insights into privacy and data protection concerns. However, the sheer volume and unstructured nature of these reports make it challenging to extract and categorize relevant requirements. To address this challenge, we present a novel approach for mining and classifying privacy and data protection requirements from issue reports. Our methodology involves a multi-step process, combining natural language processing techniques with machine learning algorithms. We first collect a large dataset of issue reports from open-source software projects and apply named entity recognition to identify relevant keywords related to privacy and data protection. We then employ topic modeling to uncover underlying themes and sentiments expressed in the reports. Subsequently, we train a supervised classification model to categorize the extracted requirements into predefined categories, such as data encryption, access control, and data anonymization. Our evaluation on a dataset of over 10,000 issue reports demonstrates the effectiveness of our approach, achieving an F1-score of 0.87 in classifying privacy and data protection requirements. We also conduct a qualitative analysis of the extracted requirements, revealing patterns and trends that can inform the development of more privacy-preserving software systems. Our findings have significant implications for software development teams, regulatory bodies, and organizations seeking to ensure compliance with data protection regulations such as GDPR. By automating the extraction and classification of privacy and data protection requirements, our approach can facilitate the development of more secure and privacy-aware software systems.

title: On Privacy Weaknesses and Vulnerabilities in Software Systems
text: In this digital era, our privacy is under constant threat as our personal data and traceable online/offline activities are frequently collected, processed and transferred by many software applications. Privacy attacks are often formed by exploiting vulnerabilities found in those software applications. The Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) and Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE) systems are currently the main sources that software engineers rely on for understanding and preventing publicly disclosed software vulnerabilities. However, our study on all 922 weaknesses in the CWE and 156,537 vulnerabilities registered in the CVE to date has found a very small coverage of privacy-related vulnerabilities in both systems, only 4.45\% in CWE and 0.1\% in CVE. These also cover only a small number of areas of privacy threats that have been raised in existing privacy software engineering research, privacy regulations and frameworks, and relevant reputable organisations. The actionable insights generated from our study led to the introduction of 11 new common privacy weaknesses to supplement the CWE system, making it become a source for both security and privacy vulnerabilities.

title: On Privacy Weaknesses and Vulnerabilities in Software Systems
text: The widespread adoption of software systems in various aspects of modern life has led to a substantial increase in the collection and processing of sensitive user data, rendering privacy a paramount concern. Despite the severity of privacy breaches, existing research has primarily focused on network and database-level vulnerabilities, overlooking the inherent weaknesses in software systems themselves. This study undertakes a comprehensive examination of privacy weaknesses and vulnerabilities in software systems, with a specific emphasis on design and implementation flaws. Our methodology involves a rigorous analysis of 30 popular open-source software systems, utilizing a combination of static code analysis, dynamic testing, and manual code review. Our findings reveal a disturbing prevalence of privacy vulnerabilities, with 23 out of 30 systems exhibiting at least one critical flaw. Notably, we identify a lack of secure defaults, inadequate encryption, and insufficient access control as the most common weaknesses. Furthermore, we demonstrate the feasibility of exploiting these vulnerabilities to compromise user privacy, highlighting the urgent need for software developers to prioritize privacy-centric design principles.

title: Pale Transformer: A General Vision Transformer Backbone with Pale-Shaped Attention
text: Recently, Transformers have shown promising performance in various vision tasks. To reduce the quadratic computation complexity caused by the global self-attention, various methods constrain the range of attention within a local region to improve its efficiency. Consequently, their receptive fields in a single attention layer are not large enough, resulting in insufficient context modeling. To address this issue, we propose a Pale-Shaped self-Attention (PS-Attention), which performs self-attention within a pale-shaped region. Compared to the global self-attention, PS-Attention can reduce the computation and memory costs significantly. Meanwhile, it can capture richer contextual information under the similar computation complexity with previous local self-attention mechanisms. Based on the PS-Attention, we develop a general Vision Transformer backbone with a hierarchical architecture, named Pale Transformer, which achieves 83.4%, 84.3%, and 84.9% Top-1 accuracy with the model size of 22M, 48M, and 85M respectively for 224 ImageNet-1K classification, outperforming the previous Vision Transformer backbones. For downstream tasks, our Pale Transformer backbone performs better than the recent state-of-the-art CSWin Transformer by a large margin on ADE20K semantic segmentation and COCO object detection & instance segmentation. title: Pale Transformer: A General Vision Transformer Backbone with Pale-Shaped Attention
text: The Transformer architecture has demonstrated remarkable success in various computer vision tasks, but its global self-attention mechanism incurs a quadratic computational complexity. To mitigate this issue, recent approaches have resorted to constraining attention within local regions, thereby sacrificing contextual modeling capabilities. We propose a novel Pale-Shaped self-Attention (PS-Attention) mechanism, which strikes a balance between computational efficiency and contextual information capture by performing self-attention within a pale-shaped region. Compared to global self-attention, PS-Attention significantly reduces computational and memory costs while capturing richer contextual information at a comparable computational complexity to previous local attention mechanisms. Building upon PS-Attention, we develop a hierarchical Vision Transformer backbone, dubbed Pale Transformer, which achieves state-of-the-art performance on ImageNet-1K classification, with Top-1 accuracies of 83.4%, 84.3%, and 84.9% for models of 22M, 48M, and 85M parameters, respectively. Furthermore, our Pale Transformer backbone outperforms the CSWin Transformer on ADE20K semantic segmentation and COCO object detection and instance segmentation tasks by a substantial margin.

title: Efficient Performance Bounds for Primal-Dual Reinforcement Learning from Demonstrations
text: We consider large-scale Markov decision processes with an unknown cost function and address the problem of learning a policy from a finite set of expert demonstrations. We assume that the learner is not allowed to interact with the expert and has no access to reinforcement signal of any kind. Existing inverse reinforcement learning methods come with strong theoretical guarantees, but are computationally expensive, while state-of-the-art policy optimization algorithms achieve significant empirical success, but are hampered by limited theoretical understanding. To bridge the gap between theory and practice, we introduce a novel bilinear saddle-point framework using Lagrangian duality. The proposed primal-dual viewpoint allows us to develop a model-free provably efficient algorithm through the lens of stochastic convex optimization. The method enjoys the advantages of simplicity of implementation, low memory requirements, and computational and sample complexities independent of the number of states. We further present an equivalent no-regret online-learning interpretation.

title: Efficient Performance Bounds for Primal-Dual Reinforcement Learning from Demonstrations
text: Reinforcement learning from demonstrations (RLfD) has gained popularity for its ability to leverage expert demonstrations to accelerate learning. However, existing RLfD methods often suffer from poor sample efficiency and lack of theoretical guarantees. In this context, primal-dual reinforcement learning (PDRL) has emerged as a promising approach, leveraging the power of Lagrangian duality to incorporate demonstrations into the learning process. Despite its empirical success, PDRL lacks rigorous performance bounds, hindering its widespread adoption. We bridge this gap by developing novel, efficient performance bounds for PDRL from demonstrations. Our bounds, derived using a novel primal-dual analysis, provide a tight characterization of the suboptimality gap between the PDRL solution and the optimal policy. We demonstrate the efficacy of our bounds through extensive experiments on benchmark domains, showcasing improved sample efficiency and robustness to demonstration quality. Our results have significant implications for the development of reliable and efficient RLfD algorithms in real-world settings.

title: Multi-Band Wi-Fi Sensing with Matched Feature Granularity
text: Complementary to the fine-grained channel state information (CSI) from the physical layer and coarse-grained received signal strength indicator (RSSI) measurements, the mid-grained spatial beam attributes (e.g., beam SNR) that are available at millimeter-wave (mmWave) bands during the mandatory beam training phase can be repurposed for Wi-Fi sensing applications. In this paper, we propose a multi-band Wi-Fi fusion method for Wi-Fi sensing that hierarchically fuses the features from both the fine-grained CSI at sub-6 GHz and the mid-grained beam SNR at 60 GHz in a granularity matching framework. The granularity matching is realized by pairing two feature maps from the CSI and beam SNR at different granularity levels and linearly combining all paired feature maps into a fused feature map with learnable weights. To further address the issue of limited labeled training data, we propose an autoencoder-based multi-band Wi-Fi fusion network that can be pre-trained in an unsupervised fashion. Once the autoencoder-based fusion network is pre-trained, we detach the decoders and append multi-task sensing heads to the fused feature map by fine-tuning the fusion block and re-training the multi-task heads from the scratch. The multi-band Wi-Fi fusion framework is thoroughly validated by in-house experimental Wi-Fi sensing datasets spanning three tasks: 1) pose recognition; 2) occupancy sensing; and 3) indoor localization. Comparison to four baseline methods (i.e., CSI-only, beam SNR-only, input fusion, and feature fusion) demonstrates the granularity matching improves the multi-task sensing performance. Quantitative performance is evaluated as a function of the number of labeled training data, latent space dimension, and fine-tuning learning rates.

title: Multi-Band Wi-Fi Sensing with Matched Feature Granularity
text: The proliferation of Wi-Fi enabled devices has created a ubiquitous infrastructure for device-free human sensing, enabling various applications such as gesture recognition, activity monitoring, and people counting. Despite its potential, existing Wi-Fi sensing systems suffer from limited robustness and accuracy, primarily due to the coarse granularity of Wi-Fi features extracted from Channel State Information (CSI). In this work, we propose a novel multi-band Wi-Fi sensing approach that leverages matched feature granularity to significantly enhance the performance of Wi-Fi sensing systems. Our approach exploits the diversity of Wi-Fi frequency bands to extract fine-grained features that are robust to environmental and hardware variations. Specifically, we design a hierarchical feature extraction framework that adaptively matches the granularity of CSI features to the specific sensing task, thereby minimizing the feature dimensionality while preserving discriminative information. We evaluate our approach on a comprehensive dataset comprising various human activities and gestures, collected using a custom-built multi-band Wi-Fi sensing platform. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach achieves an average improvement of 15.3% in activity recognition accuracy and 21.1% in gesture recognition accuracy, compared to state-of-the-art Wi-Fi sensing systems. Furthermore, our approach exhibits improved robustness to environmental changes, such as furniture rearrangement and multipath effects, and outperforms existing systems in scenarios with varying device and hardware configurations. The proposed approach has significant implications for the development of accurate and robust Wi-Fi sensing systems, enabling a wide range of applications in smart homes, healthcare, and surveillance.

title: To Supervise or Not: How to Effectively Learn Wireless Interference Management Models?
text: Machine learning has become successful in solving wireless interference management problems. Different kinds of deep neural networks (DNNs) have been trained to accomplish key tasks such as power control, beamforming and admission control. There are two popular training paradigms for such DNNs-based interference management models: supervised learning (i.e., fitting labels generated by an optimization algorithm) and unsupervised learning (i.e., directly optimizing some system performance measure). Although both of these paradigms have been extensively applied in practice, due to the lack of any theoretical understanding about these methods, it is not clear how to systematically understand and compare their performance. In this work, we conduct theoretical studies to provide some in-depth understanding about these two training paradigms. First, we show a somewhat surprising result, that for some special power control problem, the unsupervised learning can perform much worse than its supervised counterpart, because it is more likely to stuck at some low-quality local solutions. We then provide a series of theoretical results to further understand the properties of the two approaches. Generally speaking, we show that when high-quality labels are available, then the supervised learning is less likely to be stuck at a solution than its unsupervised counterpart. Additionally, we develop a semi-supervised learning approach which properly integrates these two training paradigms, and can effectively utilize limited number of labels to find high-quality solutions. To our knowledge, these are the first set of theoretical results trying to understand different training approaches in learning-based wireless communication system design.

title: To Supervise or Not: How to Effectively Learn Wireless Interference Management Models?
text: Wireless interference management is a crucial aspect of maintaining quality of service in modern wireless communication systems. The increasing density of wireless devices has led to a surge in interference, necessitating effective management strategies. Machine learning-based approaches have shown promise in this regard, but their success hinges on the availability of high-quality training data. In this context, the role of supervision in learning wireless interference management models remains unclear. We investigate the efficacy of supervised, semi-supervised, and unsupervised learning paradigms in modeling wireless interference. Our approach leverages a novel dataset of wireless channel measurements, collected from a large-scale indoor wireless network. We design and implement a range of machine learning models, including graph neural networks, random forests, and Gaussian processes, and evaluate their performance under varying levels of supervision. Our results reveal that, counterintuitively, unsupervised learning outperforms supervised and semi-supervised methods in modeling wireless interference. We attribute this to the ability of unsupervised models to capture complex, latent patterns in the data that are not explicitly labeled. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the incorporation of domain knowledge, in the form of physical layer models, significantly enhances the performance of unsupervised models. Our findings have important implications for the design of efficient wireless interference management systems, suggesting that unsupervised learning may be a more effective strategy than traditional supervised approaches. We provide insights into the optimal choice of learning paradigm, model architecture, and domain knowledge incorporation, thereby contributing to the development of more accurate and robust wireless interference management models.

title: Solving time dependent Fokker-Planck equations via temporal normalizing flow
text: In this work, we propose an adaptive learning approach based on temporal normalizing flows for solving time-dependent Fokker-Planck (TFP) equations. It is well known that solutions of such equations are probability density functions, and thus our approach relies on modelling the target solutions with the temporal normalizing flows. The temporal normalizing flow is then trained based on the TFP loss function, without requiring any labeled data. Being a machine learning scheme, the proposed approach is mesh-free and can be easily applied to high dimensional problems. We present a variety of test problems to show the effectiveness of the learning approach.

title: Solving time dependent Fokker-Planck equations via temporal normalizing flow
text: Time-dependent Fokker-Planck equations are ubiquitous in modeling complex systems, but their solution poses significant computational challenges. Recent advances in normalizing flows have shown promise in approximating complex distributions, yet their application to time-dependent problems remains largely unexplored. We propose a novel framework for solving time-dependent Fokker-Planck equations using temporal normalizing flows. By modeling the time-evolution of the probability density function as a sequence of invertible transformations, our approach enables efficient and accurate approximation of the solution. We demonstrate the efficacy of our method on a range of benchmark problems, achieving significant improvements in accuracy and computational efficiency compared to traditional numerical methods.

title: GuidedMix-Net: Semi-supervised Semantic Segmentation by Using Labeled Images as Reference
text: Semi-supervised learning is a challenging problem which aims to construct a model by learning from limited labeled examples. Numerous methods for this task focus on utilizing the predictions of unlabeled instances consistency alone to regularize networks. However, treating labeled and unlabeled data separately often leads to the discarding of mass prior knowledge learned from the labeled examples. %, and failure to mine the feature interaction between the labeled and unlabeled image pairs. In this paper, we propose a novel method for semi-supervised semantic segmentation named GuidedMix-Net, by leveraging labeled information to guide the learning of unlabeled instances. Specifically, GuidedMix-Net employs three operations: 1) interpolation of similar labeled-unlabeled image pairs; 2) transfer of mutual information; 3) generalization of pseudo masks. It enables segmentation models can learning the higher-quality pseudo masks of unlabeled data by transfer the knowledge from labeled samples to unlabeled data. Along with supervised learning for labeled data, the prediction of unlabeled data is jointly learned with the generated pseudo masks from the mixed data. Extensive experiments on PASCAL VOC 2012, and Cityscapes demonstrate the effectiveness of our GuidedMix-Net, which achieves competitive segmentation accuracy and significantly improves the mIoU by +7$\%$ compared to previous approaches.

title: GuidedMix-Net: Semi-supervised Semantic Segmentation by Using Labeled Images as Reference
text: Semi-supervised learning, a longstanding challenge in machine learning, seeks to construct models from limited labeled examples. While numerous approaches rely solely on consistency regularization using unlabeled instance predictions, this often results in the loss of valuable prior knowledge gleaned from labeled examples and neglects the exploration of feature interactions between labeled and unlabeled image pairs. We propose GuidedMix-Net, a novel semi-supervised semantic segmentation method that leverages labeled information to guide the learning of unlabeled instances. By integrating three key operations – interpolation of similar labeled-unlabeled image pairs, mutual information transfer, and pseudo mask generalization – GuidedMix-Net enables the generation of higher-quality pseudo masks for unlabeled data through knowledge transfer from labeled samples. Our approach jointly learns predictions from labeled data and unlabeled data with generated pseudo masks, leading to improved segmentation accuracy. Extensive experiments on PASCAL VOC 2012 and Cityscapes datasets demonstrate the efficacy of GuidedMix-Net, achieving a significant +7% improvement in mean intersection over union (mIoU) compared to existing approaches.

title: Recursive Least-Squares Estimator-Aided Online Learning for Visual Tracking
text: Tracking visual objects from a single initial exemplar in the testing phase has been broadly cast as a one-/few-shot problem, i.e., one-shot learning for initial adaptation and few-shot learning for online adaptation. The recent few-shot online adaptation methods incorporate the prior knowledge from large amounts of annotated training data via complex meta-learning optimization in the offline phase. This helps the online deep trackers to achieve fast adaptation and reduce overfitting risk in tracking. In this paper, we propose a simple yet effective recursive least-squares estimator-aided online learning approach for few-shot online adaptation without requiring offline training. It allows an in-built memory retention mechanism for the model to remember the knowledge about the object seen before, and thus the seen data can be safely removed from training. This also bears certain similarities to the emerging continual learning field in preventing catastrophic forgetting. This mechanism enables us to unveil the power of modern online deep trackers without incurring too much extra computational cost. We evaluate our approach based on two networks in the online learning families for tracking, i.e., multi-layer perceptrons in RT-MDNet and convolutional neural networks in DiMP. The consistent improvements on several challenging tracking benchmarks demonstrate its effectiveness and efficiency.

title: Recursive Least-Squares Estimator-Aided Online Learning for Visual Tracking
text: Visual object tracking is a fundamental task in computer vision, with numerous applications in surveillance, robotics, and autonomous driving. Despite significant advances, online learning-based trackers still struggle to adapt to dynamic scene changes, leading to performance degradation over time. To address this limitation, we propose a novel online learning framework that integrates a recursive least-squares (RLS) estimator with a visual tracker. Our approach leverages the RLS estimator to recursively update the tracker's parameters, enabling efficient adaptation to changing object appearances and scene conditions. We formulate the online learning problem as a sequential minimization of a quadratic objective function, which is solved using the RLS estimator. The resulting algorithm, dubbed RLS-T, exhibits robustness to noisy observations, partial occlusions, and sudden changes in object motion. Experimental evaluations on the OTB-2015 and VOT-2018 benchmarks demonstrate that RLS-T outperforms state-of-the-art trackers, achieving a gain of up to 15% in terms of tracking accuracy. Furthermore, our approach reduces the computational overhead by approximately 30% compared to existing methods, making it suitable for real-time applications. The proposed framework provides a new direction for online learning in visual tracking, with potential implications for various computer vision tasks.

title: Semi-supervised Salient Object Detection with Effective Confidence Estimation
text: The success of existing salient object detection models relies on a large pixel-wise labeled training dataset, which is time-consuming and expensive to obtain. We study semi-supervised salient object detection, with access to a small number of labeled samples and a large number of unlabeled samples. Specifically, we present a pseudo label based learn-ing framework with a Conditional Energy-based Model. We model the stochastic nature of human saliency labels using the stochastic latent variable of the Conditional Energy-based Model. It further enables generation of a high-quality pixel-wise uncertainty map, highlighting the reliability of corresponding pseudo label generated for the unlabeled sample. This minimises the contribution of low-certainty pseudo labels in optimising the model, preventing the error propagation. Experimental results show that the proposed strategy can effectively explore the contribution of unlabeled data. With only 1/16 labeled samples, our model achieves competitive performance compared with state-of-the-art fully-supervised models.

title: Semi-supervised Salient Object Detection with Effective Confidence Estimation
text: Salient object detection has garnered significant attention in computer vision due to its diverse applications in image and video processing. While fully supervised approaches have achieved state-of-the-art performance, they often rely on large amounts of annotated data, which can be expensive and time-consuming to obtain. To alleviate this limitation, we propose a semi-supervised salient object detection framework that leverages both labeled and unlabeled data. Our approach integrates a confidence estimation module to evaluate the reliability of the predicted saliency maps, allowing the model to adaptively select the most informative samples for self-training. Experimental results on five benchmark datasets demonstrate that our method outperforms existing semi-supervised and weakly supervised approaches, achieving comparable performance to fully supervised methods. Moreover, our confidence estimation module improves the model's robustness to noisy labels and enables the detection of salient objects in challenging scenarios.

title: Multilayer Graph Contrastive Clustering Network
text: Multilayer graph has garnered plenty of research attention in many areas due to their high utility in modeling interdependent systems. However, clustering of multilayer graph, which aims at dividing the graph nodes into categories or communities, is still at a nascent stage. Existing methods are often limited to exploiting the multiview attributes or multiple networks and ignoring more complex and richer network frameworks. To this end, we propose a generic and effective autoencoder framework for multilayer graph clustering named Multilayer Graph Contrastive Clustering Network (MGCCN). MGCCN consists of three modules: (1)Attention mechanism is applied to better capture the relevance between nodes and neighbors for better node embeddings. (2)To better explore the consistent information in different networks, a contrastive fusion strategy is introduced. (3)MGCCN employs a self-supervised component that iteratively strengthens the node embedding and clustering. Extensive experiments on different types of real-world graph data indicate that our proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art techniques.

title: Multilayer Graph Contrastive Clustering Network
text: The proliferation of multilayer graph-structured data has sparked interest in developing effective clustering algorithms that can capture complex relationships across different layers. Existing methods often overlook the inherent heterogeneity and non-linearity in such data, leading to subpar performance. We propose the Multilayer Graph Contrastive Clustering Network (MGCCN), a novel deep learning framework that jointly learns node representations and clusters in a multilayer graph. MGCCN leverages contrastive learning to align node representations across layers, while a clustering module identifies densely connected communities. Our approach iteratively refines node representations and cluster assignments, enabling the discovery of more accurate and robust clusters. Experimental results on real-world datasets demonstrate that MGCCN outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving an average improvement of 12.4% in clustering accuracy and 9.2% in normalized mutual information. Additionally, MGCCN exhibits superior robustness to noise and varying layer importance, making it a promising solution for multilayer graph clustering tasks.

title: Towards Low Light Enhancement with RAW Images
text: In this paper, we make the first benchmark effort to elaborate on the superiority of using RAW images in the low light enhancement and develop a novel alternative route to utilize RAW images in a more flexible and practical way. Inspired by a full consideration on the typical image processing pipeline, we are inspired to develop a new evaluation framework, Factorized Enhancement Model (FEM), which decomposes the properties of RAW images into measurable factors and provides a tool for exploring how properties of RAW images affect the enhancement performance empirically. The empirical benchmark results show that the Linearity of data and Exposure Time recorded in meta-data play the most critical role, which brings distinct performance gains in various measures over the approaches taking the sRGB images as input. With the insights obtained from the benchmark results in mind, a RAW-guiding Exposure Enhancement Network (REENet) is developed, which makes trade-offs between the advantages and inaccessibility of RAW images in real applications in a way of using RAW images only in the training phase. REENet projects sRGB images into linear RAW domains to apply constraints with corresponding RAW images to reduce the difficulty of modeling training. After that, in the testing phase, our REENet does not rely on RAW images. Experimental results demonstrate not only the superiority of REENet to state-of-the-art sRGB-based methods and but also the effectiveness of the RAW guidance and all components.

title: Towards Low Light Enhancement with RAW Images
text: Low-light image enhancement is a longstanding challenge in computer vision, as it severely degrades the performance of various applications, including object detection, segmentation, and recognition. Conventional approaches rely on sRGB images, which are limited by the lossy compression and nonlinear transformations applied during the camera's image signal processing pipeline. In contrast, RAW images preserve the original sensor data, offering a more faithful representation of the scene. This work explores the potential of RAW images in low-light enhancement, proposing a novel framework that leverages the unique properties of RAW data. Our approach, called RAW-LLE, consists of two stages: noise modeling and image enhancement. We first develop a noise model that characterizes the sensor-specific noise patterns in RAW images, which is learned through a large-scale dataset of paired noisy and clean images. The learned model is then integrated into a deep neural network that enhances the input RAW image, refining the noise modeling and enhancement stages through a joint optimization process. Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate the superiority of RAW-LLE over state-of-the-art methods, achieving an average improvement of 2.45 dB in PSNR and 0.035 in SSIM. Notably, our approach excels in extreme low-light conditions, where the noise level is high and the input images are severely degraded. The proposed framework opens up new opportunities for low-light image enhancement, enabling applications such as surveillance, autonomous driving, and microscopy to operate effectively in challenging environments.

title: The Devil is in the Task: Exploiting Reciprocal Appearance-Localization Features for Monocular 3D Object Detection
text: Low-cost monocular 3D object detection plays a fundamental role in autonomous driving, whereas its accuracy is still far from satisfactory. In this paper, we dig into the 3D object detection task and reformulate it as the sub-tasks of object localization and appearance perception, which benefits to a deep excavation of reciprocal information underlying the entire task. We introduce a Dynamic Feature Reflecting Network, named DFR-Net, which contains two novel standalone modules: (i) the Appearance-Localization Feature Reflecting module (ALFR) that first separates taskspecific features and then self-mutually reflects the reciprocal features; (ii) the Dynamic Intra-Trading module (DIT) that adaptively realigns the training processes of various sub-tasks via a self-learning manner. Extensive experiments on the challenging KITTI dataset demonstrate the effectiveness and generalization of DFR-Net. We rank 1st among all the monocular 3D object detectors in the KITTI test set (till March 16th, 2021). The proposed method is also easy to be plug-and-play in many cutting-edge 3D detection frameworks at negligible cost to boost performance. The code will be made publicly available.

title: The Devil is in the Task: Exploiting Reciprocal Appearance-Localization Features for Monocular 3D Object Detection
text: The accuracy of low-cost monocular 3D object detection remains a significant bottleneck in autonomous driving applications. To address this limitation, we reframe the detection task as the interdependent sub-problems of object localization and appearance perception, enabling a deeper exploration of the underlying reciprocal information. Our proposed Dynamic Feature Reflecting Network (DFR-Net) comprises two novel modules: the Appearance-Localization Feature Reflecting (ALFR) module, which separates task-specific features and then reflects them self-mutually, and the Dynamic Intra-Trading (DIT) module, which adaptively realigns the training processes of various sub-tasks through self-learning. Comprehensive experiments on the challenging KITTI dataset demonstrate the efficacy and generalizability of DFR-Net, achieving a top-ranked performance among all monocular 3D object detectors in the KITTI test set as of March 16th, 2021. Notably, our approach can be seamlessly integrated into various state-of-the-art 3D detection frameworks with minimal overhead, yielding significant performance gains. The corresponding code will be made publicly available.

title: Delving into Probabilistic Uncertainty for Unsupervised Domain Adaptive Person Re-Identification
text: Clustering-based unsupervised domain adaptive (UDA) person re-identification (ReID) reduces exhaustive annotations. However, owing to unsatisfactory feature embedding and imperfect clustering, pseudo labels for target domain data inherently contain an unknown proportion of wrong ones, which would mislead feature learning. In this paper, we propose an approach named probabilistic uncertainty guided progressive label refinery (P$^2$LR) for domain adaptive person re-identification. First, we propose to model the labeling uncertainty with the probabilistic distance along with ideal single-peak distributions. A quantitative criterion is established to measure the uncertainty of pseudo labels and facilitate the network training. Second, we explore a progressive strategy for refining pseudo labels. With the uncertainty-guided alternative optimization, we balance between the exploration of target domain data and the negative effects of noisy labeling. On top of a strong baseline, we obtain significant improvements and achieve the state-of-the-art performance on four UDA ReID benchmarks. Specifically, our method outperforms the baseline by 6.5% mAP on the Duke2Market task, while surpassing the state-of-the-art method by 2.5% mAP on the Market2MSMT task.

title: Delving into Probabilistic Uncertainty for Unsupervised Domain Adaptive Person Re-Identification
text: Unsupervised domain adaptive person re-identification (UDAPR) remains a challenging problem in computer vision, where the goal is to adapt a model trained on a labeled source domain to an unlabeled target domain with a different distribution. Existing methods often rely on adversarial training or pseudo-labeling, but neglect the inherent uncertainty in the target domain. We propose a novel probabilistic approach to UDAPR, which explicitly models the uncertainty in the target domain using Bayesian neural networks. Our method, termed ProbUDAPR, consists of a variational inference module that estimates the posterior distribution of the model parameters, and a domain adaptation module that aligns the feature distributions across domains. Experimental results on four benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of ProbUDAPR, achieving state-of-the-art performance on three datasets and competitive results on the fourth. Notably, our method outperforms existing approaches by a significant margin when the target domain contains a large proportion of uncertain samples. We further analyze the uncertainty estimates produced by ProbUDAPR, providing insights into the model's confidence in its predictions and the adaptation process.

title: SECP-Net: SE-Connection Pyramid Network of Organ At Risk Segmentation for Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma
text: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) is a kind of malignant tumor. Accurate and automatic segmentation of organs at risk (OAR) of computed tomography (CT) images is clinically significant. In recent years, deep learning models represented by U-Net have been widely applied in medical image segmentation tasks, which can help doctors with reduction of workload and get accurate results more quickly. In OAR segmentation of NPC, the sizes of OAR are variable, especially, some of them are small. Traditional deep neural networks underperform during segmentation due to the lack use of global and multi-size information. This paper proposes a new SE-Connection Pyramid Network (SECP-Net). SECP-Net extracts global and multi-size information flow with se connection (SEC) modules and a pyramid structure of network for improving the segmentation performance, especially that of small organs. SECP-Net also designs an auto-context cascaded network to further improve the segmentation performance. Comparative experiments are conducted between SECP-Net and other recently methods on a dataset with CT images of head and neck. Five-fold cross validation is used to evaluate the performance based on two metrics, i.e., Dice and Jaccard similarity. Experimental results show that SECP-Net can achieve SOTA performance in this challenging task.

title: SECP-Net: SE-Connection Pyramid Network of Organ At Risk Segmentation for Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma
text: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) is a prevalent and aggressive head and neck cancer, with accurate segmentation of organs at risk (OARs) being crucial for effective treatment planning. Despite recent advancements in deep learning-based segmentation methods, OAR segmentation in NPC remains a challenging task due to the complex anatomy and variability in tumor shapes and sizes. To address this challenge, we propose SECP-Net, a novel SE-connection pyramid network that leverages spatial and channel attention mechanisms to improve OAR segmentation accuracy. SECP-Net consists of a pyramid encoder that extracts multi-scale features, followed by a decoder that refines features using spatial and channel attention. We evaluate SECP-Net on a dataset of 150 NPC patients, with manual annotations of six OARs. Experimental results show that SECP-Net outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving a mean Dice similarity coefficient of 0.854 and a Hausdorff distance of 2.31 mm. Furthermore, SECP-Net demonstrates improved robustness to tumor variability and shape irregularities. Our method has the potential to improve the accuracy and efficiency of OAR segmentation in NPC treatment planning, ultimately enhancing patient outcomes.

title: Bipartite Graph Matching Algorithms for Clean-Clean Entity Resolution: An Empirical Evaluation
text: Entity Resolution (ER) is the task of finding records that refer to the same real-world entities. A common scenario is when entities across two clean sources need to be resolved, which we refer to as Clean-Clean ER. In this paper, we perform an extensive empirical evaluation of 8 bipartite graph matching algorithms that take in as input a bipartite similarity graph and provide as output a set of matched entities. We consider a wide range of matching algorithms, including algorithms that have not previously been applied to ER, or have been evaluated only in other ER settings. We assess the relative performance of the algorithms with respect to accuracy and time efficiency over 10 established, real datasets, from which we extract >700 different similarity graphs. Our results provide insights into the relative performance of these algorithms and guidelines for choosing the best one, depending on the data at hand.

title: Bipartite Graph Matching Algorithms for Clean-Clean Entity Resolution: An Empirical Evaluation
text: Entity resolution, the process of identifying duplicate references to real-world entities, is a fundamental task in data integration and data cleaning. Clean-clean entity resolution, a variant of this problem, occurs when both input datasets are free of errors, but still require matching to establish correspondences. Bipartite graph matching algorithms have been proposed as a solution to this problem, but their empirical performance on real-world datasets remains understudied. This paper presents a comprehensive evaluation of six state-of-the-art bipartite graph matching algorithms on five large-scale datasets from diverse domains. Our experiments reveal that the algorithms' performance varies significantly across datasets, with no single algorithm dominating across all metrics. Notably, we find that the recently proposed DeepIso algorithm outperforms traditional methods on datasets with complex entity relationships, while the scalable GBPH algorithm excels on large datasets. Our findings provide valuable insights for practitioners and researchers seeking to deploy entity resolution systems in real-world applications.

title: Deep neural networks for solving forward and inverse problems of (2+1)-dimensional nonlinear wave equations with rational solitons
text: In this paper, we investigate the forward problems on the data-driven rational solitons for the (2+1)-dimensional KP-I equation and spin-nonlinear Schrödinger (spin-NLS) equation via the deep neural networks leaning. Moreover, the inverse problems of the (2+1)-dimensional KP-I equation and spin-NLS equation are studied via deep learning. The main idea of the data-driven forward and inverse problems is to use the deep neural networks with the activation function to approximate the solutions of the considered (2+1)-dimensional nonlinear wave equations by optimizing the chosen loss functions related to the considered nonlinear wave equations.

title: Deep neural networks for solving forward and inverse problems of (2+1)-dimensional nonlinear wave equations with rational solitons
text: We explore the application of deep neural networks to solve forward and inverse problems associated with the (2+1)-dimensional KP-I equation and spin-nonlinear Schrödinger equation, leveraging the data-driven rational soliton approach. By optimizing tailored loss functions related to these nonlinear wave equations, we utilize deep neural networks with activation functions to approximate solutions. Our methodology effectively tackles both forward and inverse problems, yielding a powerful framework for understanding these complex equations.

title: DetarNet: Decoupling Translation and Rotation by Siamese Network for Point Cloud Registration
text: Point cloud registration is a fundamental step for many tasks. In this paper, we propose a neural network named DetarNet to decouple the translation $t$ and rotation $R$, so as to overcome the performance degradation due to their mutual interference in point cloud registration. First, a Siamese Network based Progressive and Coherent Feature Drift (PCFD) module is proposed to align the source and target points in high-dimensional feature space, and accurately recover translation from the alignment process. Then we propose a Consensus Encoding Unit (CEU) to construct more distinguishable features for a set of putative correspondences. After that, a Spatial and Channel Attention (SCA) block is adopted to build a classification network for finding good correspondences. Finally, the rotation is obtained by Singular Value Decomposition (SVD). In this way, the proposed network decouples the estimation of translation and rotation, resulting in better performance for both of them. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed DetarNet improves registration performance on both indoor and outdoor scenes. Our code will be available in \url{

title: DetarNet: Decoupling Translation and Rotation by Siamese Network for Point Cloud Registration
text: Decoupling translation and rotation estimation is crucial for accurate point cloud registration, as their mutual interference can significantly degrade performance. We introduce DetarNet, a neural network that addresses this challenge by disentangling the estimation of translation t and rotation R. Our approach begins with a Siamese Network-based Progressive and Coherent Feature Drift (PCFD) module, which aligns source and target points in high-dimensional feature space, yielding accurate translation recovery. Next, a Consensus Encoding Unit (CEU) is employed to construct distinctive features for putative correspondences. A Spatial and Channel Attention (SCA) block is then used to build a classification network for identifying reliable correspondences. Finally, rotation is obtained via Singular Value Decomposition (SVD). By decoupling translation and rotation estimation, DetarNet achieves improved performance for both components. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in registering point clouds from both indoor and outdoor scenes, outperforming existing methods.

title: Investigating Shifts in GAN Output-Distributions
text: A fundamental and still largely unsolved question in the context of Generative Adversarial Networks is whether they are truly able to capture the real data distribution and, consequently, to sample from it. In particular, the multidimensional nature of image distributions leads to a complex evaluation of the diversity of GAN distributions. Existing approaches provide only a partial understanding of this issue, leaving the question unanswered. In this work, we introduce a loop-training scheme for the systematic investigation of observable shifts between the distributions of real training data and GAN generated data. Additionally, we introduce several bounded measures for distribution shifts, which are both easy to compute and to interpret. Overall, the combination of these methods allows an explorative investigation of innate limitations of current GAN algorithms. Our experiments on different data-sets and multiple state-of-the-art GAN architectures show large shifts between input and output distributions, showing that existing theoretical guarantees towards the convergence of output distributions appear not to be holding in practice.

title: Investigating Shifts in GAN Output-Distributions
text: The remarkable success of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) in modeling complex distributions has been tempered by concerns regarding their reliability and robustness. A particularly vexing issue is the phenomenon of output-distribution shifts, wherein a GAN's generated samples drift away from the target distribution over time. This shift can have disastrous consequences in applications where accuracy and consistency are paramount. To better understand this phenomenon, we conduct a systematic investigation of output-distribution shifts in GANs. We propose a novel metric, dubbed "Distributional Drift Coefficient" (DDC), which quantifies the degree of shift in a GAN's output distribution. Through an extensive suite of experiments involving multiple GAN architectures and benchmark datasets, we uncover several key factors contributing to output-distribution shifts, including mode collapse, overfitting, and parameter updates. Our findings suggest that careful tuning of hyperparameters, particularly learning rates and batch sizes, can mitigate distributional drift. Furthermore, we demonstrate that incorporating DDC as a regularization term in the GAN loss function can effectively stabilize the output distribution.

title: Financial Vision Based Differential Privacy Applications
text: The importance of deep learning data privacy has gained significant attention in recent years. It is probably to suffer data breaches when applying deep learning to cryptocurrency that lacks supervision of financial regulatory agencies. However, there is little relative research in the financial area to our best knowledge. We apply two representative deep learning privacy-privacy frameworks proposed by Google to financial trading data. We designed the experiments with several different parameters suggested from the original studies. In addition, we refer the degree of privacy to Google and Apple companies to estimate the results more reasonably. The results show that DP-SGD performs better than the PATE framework in financial trading data. The tradeoff between privacy and accuracy is low in DP-SGD. The degree of privacy also is in line with the actual case. Therefore, we can obtain a strong privacy guarantee with precision to avoid potential financial loss.

title: Financial Vision Based Differential Privacy Applications
text: The increasing significance of privacy-preserving deep learning has become a pressing concern, particularly in the realm of cryptocurrency where the absence of regulatory oversight renders it vulnerable to data breaches. Despite its importance, there is a dearth of research focusing on the financial sector. This study addresses this gap by applying two prominent deep learning privacy frameworks, proposed by Google, to financial trading data. A series of experiments were designed, incorporating various parameters suggested by the original studies. To contextualize the results, the degree of privacy was benchmarked against the standards employed by Google and Apple. The findings indicate that DP-SGD outperforms the PATE framework in financial trading data, with a favorable tradeoff between privacy and accuracy. Furthermore, the estimated degree of privacy aligns with real-world scenarios, enabling the attainment of robust privacy guarantees while maintaining precision, thereby mitigating potential financial losses.

title: Blockchain Meets AI for Resilient and Intelligent Internet of Vehicles
text: The Internet of Vehicles (IoV) is flourishing and offers various applications relating to road safety, traffic and fuel efficiency, and infotainment. Dealing with security and privacy threats and managing the trust (detecting malicious and misbehaving peers) in IoV remains the most significant concern. Artificial Intelligence is one of the most revolutionizing technologies, and the predictive power of its machine learning models can help detect intrusions and misbehaviors. Similarly, empowering the state-of-the-art IoV security framework with blockchain can make it secure and resilient. This article discusses joint AI and blockchain for security, privacy and trust-related risks in IoV. This paper also presents problems, challenges, requirements and solutions using ML and blockchain to address aforementioned issues in IoV.

title: Blockchain Meets AI for Resilient and Intelligent Internet of Vehicles
text: The proliferation of Internet of Vehicles (IoV) has introduced unprecedented cybersecurity risks, compromising the safety and reliability of autonomous systems. To address this challenge, we propose a novel framework that synergistically integrates blockchain and Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies. Our approach leverages blockchain's immutability and transparency to ensure secure data sharing and tamper-evident logs, while AI algorithms are employed to detect and respond to potential threats in real-time. We implement a decentralized, consortium blockchain architecture and develop a machine learning-based intrusion detection system, trained on a dataset of simulated IoV attacks. Experimental results demonstrate a 35% increase in detection accuracy and a 40% reduction in response time compared to traditional, centralized approaches, highlighting the potential of our framework to enhance the resilience and intelligence of IoV ecosystems.

title: Embodied Learning for Lifelong Visual Perception
text: We study lifelong visual perception in an embodied setup, where we develop new models and compare various agents that navigate in buildings and occasionally request annotations which, in turn, are used to refine their visual perception capabilities. The purpose of the agents is to recognize objects and other semantic classes in the whole building at the end of a process that combines exploration and active visual learning. As we study this task in a lifelong learning context, the agents should use knowledge gained in earlier visited environments in order to guide their exploration and active learning strategy in successively visited buildings. We use the semantic segmentation performance as a proxy for general visual perception and study this novel task for several exploration and annotation methods, ranging from frontier exploration baselines which use heuristic active learning, to a fully learnable approach. For the latter, we introduce a deep reinforcement learning (RL) based agent which jointly learns both navigation and active learning. A point goal navigation formulation, coupled with a global planner which supplies goals, is integrated into the RL model in order to provide further incentives for systematic exploration of novel scenes. By performing extensive experiments on the Matterport3D dataset, we show how the proposed agents can utilize knowledge from previously explored scenes when exploring new ones, e.g. through less granular exploration and less frequent requests for annotations. The results also suggest that a learning-based agent is able to use its prior visual knowledge more effectively than heuristic alternatives.

title: Embodied Learning for Lifelong Visual Perception
text: Lifelong visual perception in embodied agents is a complex task that requires efficient exploration and active learning strategies to recognize objects and semantic classes in novel environments. We investigate this problem in the context of embodied agents navigating through buildings, where they request annotations to refine their visual perception capabilities. The key challenge lies in leveraging knowledge gained from earlier explored environments to guide exploration and active learning in subsequent buildings. We employ semantic segmentation performance as a proxy for general visual perception and evaluate various exploration and annotation methods, including frontier exploration baselines with heuristic active learning and a fully learnable approach. The latter involves a deep reinforcement learning (RL) agent that jointly learns navigation and active learning, incorporating a point goal navigation formulation and a global planner to promote systematic exploration of novel scenes. Our extensive experiments on the Matterport3D dataset demonstrate that the proposed agents can effectively utilize prior knowledge to adapt their exploration strategy in new environments, resulting in more efficient exploration and reduced annotation requests. Moreover, our results suggest that learning-based agents outperform heuristic alternatives in leveraging prior visual knowledge to improve visual perception capabilities.

title: APRIL: Finding the Achilles' Heel on Privacy for Vision Transformers
text: Federated learning frameworks typically require collaborators to share their local gradient updates of a common model instead of sharing training data to preserve privacy. However, prior works on Gradient Leakage Attacks showed that private training data can be revealed from gradients. So far almost all relevant works base their attacks on fully-connected or convolutional neural networks. Given the recent overwhelmingly rising trend of adapting Transformers to solve multifarious vision tasks, it is highly valuable to investigate the privacy risk of vision transformers. In this paper, we analyse the gradient leakage risk of self-attention based mechanism in both theoretical and practical manners. Particularly, we propose APRIL - Attention PRIvacy Leakage, which poses a strong threat to self-attention inspired models such as ViT. Showing how vision Transformers are at the risk of privacy leakage via gradients, we urge the significance of designing privacy-safer Transformer models and defending schemes.

title: APRIL: Finding the Achilles' Heel on Privacy for Vision Transformers
text: Vision transformers have revolutionized the field of computer vision, achieving state-of-the-art performance in various tasks. However, their increasing adoption has raised concerns about their privacy vulnerabilities. Recent studies have demonstrated the susceptibility of vision models to membership inference attacks, which can compromise user privacy. In this context, we propose APRIL, a novel framework for identifying the Achilles' heel of privacy in vision transformers. APRIL leverages a generative approach to craft synthetic images that maximize the likelihood of membership inference attacks. Our methodology involves training a generator network to produce images that are indistinguishable from real data, yet exhibit heightened privacy risks. Through extensive experiments on popular vision transformers, we demonstrate that APRIL can identify critical vulnerabilities, achieving an average precision of 0.92 in detecting private data. Our findings highlight the need for proactive privacy auditing in vision transformers and provide a valuable tool for developers to strengthen their models against membership inference attacks.

title: Synchronized Audio-Visual Frames with Fractional Positional Encoding for Transformers in Video-to-Text Translation
text: Video-to-Text (VTT) is the task of automatically generating descriptions for short audio-visual video clips, which can support visually impaired people to understand scenes of a YouTube video for instance. Transformer architectures have shown great performance in both machine translation and image captioning, lacking a straightforward and reproducible application for VTT. However, there is no comprehensive study on different strategies and advice for video description generation including exploiting the accompanying audio with fully self-attentive networks. Thus, we explore promising approaches from image captioning and video processing and apply them to VTT by developing a straightforward Transformer architecture. Additionally, we present a novel way of synchronizing audio and video features in Transformers which we call Fractional Positional Encoding (FPE). We run multiple experiments on the VATEX dataset to determine a configuration applicable to unseen datasets that helps describe short video clips in natural language and improved the CIDEr and BLEU-4 scores by 37.13 and 12.83 points compared to a vanilla Transformer network and achieve state-of-the-art results on the MSR-VTT and MSVD datasets. Also, FPE helps increase the CIDEr score by a relative factor of 8.6%.

title: Synchronized Audio-Visual Frames with Fractional Positional Encoding for Transformers in Video-to-Text Translation
text: The proliferation of video content on the internet has spurred significant interest in developing efficient video-to-text translation systems. Existing approaches rely on extracting features from individual modalities, neglecting the nuanced temporal relationships between audio and visual components. We propose a novel framework that synchronizes audio-visual frames using fractional positional encoding, enabling transformers to effectively capture multimodal interactions. Our method, dubbed SyncAVF, incorporates a hierarchical attention mechanism to selectively focus on relevant audio-visual frames and their relative positions. Experimental results on the popular How2 and MSVD datasets demonstrate that SyncAVF achieves state-of-the-art performance, outperforming existing multimodal fusion techniques by 12.4% and 8.7% in terms of BLEU-4 and METEOR scores, respectively. Furthermore, our ablation studies reveal that the fractional positional encoding scheme is instrumental in capturing subtle temporal dependencies, leading to a 5.2% improvement over traditional positional encoding. We envision SyncAVF facilitating a wide range of applications, from automated video captioning to multimedia content analysis and beyond.

title: Extended Self-Critical Pipeline for Transforming Videos to Text (TRECVID-VTT Task 2021) -- Team: MMCUniAugsburg
text: The Multimedia and Computer Vision Lab of the University of Augsburg participated in the VTT task only. We use the VATEX and TRECVID-VTT datasets for training our VTT models. We base our model on the Transformer approach for both of our submitted runs. For our second model, we adapt the X-Linear Attention Networks for Image Captioning which does not yield the desired bump in scores. For both models, we train on the complete VATEX dataset and 90% of the TRECVID-VTT dataset for pretraining while using the remaining 10% for validation. We finetune both models with self-critical sequence training, which boosts the validation performance significantly. Overall, we find that training a Video-to-Text system on traditional Image Captioning pipelines delivers very poor performance. When switching to a Transformer-based architecture our results greatly improve and the generated captions match better with the corresponding video.

title: Extended Self-Critical Pipeline for Transforming Videos to Text (TRECVID-VTT Task 2021) -- Team: MMCUniAugsburg
text: The TRECVID-VTT task 2021 challenges participants to develop models capable of generating accurate and informative descriptions for videos. This paper presents the approach of Team MMCUniAugsburg, which leverages an extended self-critical pipeline to tackle this task. We propose a novel architecture that integrates a video encoder, a text decoder, and a self-critical module. The video encoder employs a 3D convolutional neural network to extract spatiotemporal features, while the text decoder uses a transformer-based model to generate descriptions. The self-critical module is designed to refine the generated descriptions by iteratively assessing their quality and guiding the decoder to produce more accurate and relevant outputs. Experimental results on the TRECVID-VTT 2021 dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, achieving a METEOR score of 34.5, outperforming several state-of-the-art methods. Ablation studies further validate the contribution of each component in our pipeline, showcasing the potential of our method for video-to-text tasks.

title: Fostering the Robustness of White-Box Deep Neural Network Watermarks by Neuron Alignment
text: The wide application of deep learning techniques is boosting the regulation of deep learning models, especially deep neural networks (DNN), as commercial products. A necessary prerequisite for such regulations is identifying the owner of deep neural networks, which is usually done through the watermark. Current DNN watermarking schemes, particularly white-box ones, are uniformly fragile against a family of functionality equivalence attacks, especially the neuron permutation. This operation can effortlessly invalidate the ownership proof and escape copyright regulations. To enhance the robustness of white-box DNN watermarking schemes, this paper presents a procedure that aligns neurons into the same order as when the watermark is embedded, so the watermark can be correctly recognized. This neuron alignment process significantly facilitates the functionality of established deep neural network watermarking schemes.

title: Fostering the Robustness of White-Box Deep Neural Network Watermarks by Neuron Alignment
text: Deep neural network watermarks have emerged as a promising approach to protect intellectual property in machine learning models. However, existing white-box watermarking schemes are vulnerable to robustness attacks, which can compromise the watermark's integrity. To address this limitation, we propose a novel neuron alignment strategy that enhances the robustness of white-box deep neural network watermarks. Our approach leverages the idea that aligned neurons in the watermark and host models can improve the resilience of the watermark against adversarial attacks. We conduct extensive experiments on various benchmark datasets and demonstrate that our neuron alignment strategy significantly improves the robustness of white-box watermarks, achieving an average increase of 23.4% in detection accuracy under robustness attacks. Our findings have important implications for the development of reliable watermarking schemes in deep learning.

title: State Compression and Quantitative Assessment Model for Assessing Security Risks in the Oil and Gas Transmission Systems
text: The SCADA system is the foundation of the large-scale industrial control system. It is widely used in industries of petrochemistry, electric power, pipeline, etc. The natural gas SCADA system is among the critical infrastructure systems that have security issues related to trusted communications in transactions at the control system layer, and lack quantitative risk assessment and mitigation models. However, to guarantee the security of the Oil and Gas Transmission SCADA systems (OGTSS), there should be a holistic security system that considers the nature of these SCADA systems. In this paper, we augment our Security Awareness Framework with two new contributions, (i) a Data Quantization and State Compression Approach (DQSCA) that improves the classification accuracy, speeds up the detection algorithm, and reduces the computational resource consumption. DQSCA reduces the size of processed data while preserving original key events and patterns within the datasets. (ii) A quantitative risk assessment model that carries out regular system information security evaluation and assessment on the SCADA system using a deductive process. Our experiments denote that DQSCA has a low negative impact on the reduction of the detection accuracy (2.45% and 4.45%) while it reduces the detection time much (27.74% and 42.06%) for the Turnipseed and Gao datasets respectively. Furthermore, the mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) rate for the proposed risk assessment model is lower than the intrusion response system (Suricata) for the DOS, Response Injection, and Command Injection attacks by 59.80%, 73.72%, and 66.96% respectively.

title: State Compression and Quantitative Assessment Model for Assessing Security Risks in the Oil and Gas Transmission Systems
text: The reliability of large-scale industrial control systems hinges on the security of their SCADA systems, which are ubiquitously employed in industries such as petrochemistry, electric power, and pipeline transmission. Notably, natural gas SCADA systems, as critical infrastructure, are susceptible to security breaches due to trusted communication vulnerabilities at the control system layer and the lack of quantitative risk assessment and mitigation models. To ensure the security of Oil and Gas Transmission SCADA systems (OGTSS), a comprehensive security framework that acknowledges the inherent characteristics of these systems is essential. This paper extends our Security Awareness Framework by introducing two novel contributions. Firstly, a Data Quantization and State Compression Approach (DQSCA) is proposed, which enhances classification accuracy, accelerates detection algorithms, and minimizes computational resource consumption by reducing data size while preserving key events and patterns. Secondly, a quantitative risk assessment model is developed, which conducts regular system information security evaluations and assessments on the SCADA system using a deductive process. Experimental results demonstrate that DQSCA yields a negligible impact on detection accuracy (2.45% and 4.45% reduction) while significantly reducing detection time (27.74% and 42.06% reduction) for the Turnipseed and Gao datasets, respectively. Moreover, the proposed risk assessment model outperforms the intrusion response system (Suricata) in terms of mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) rates for DOS, Response Injection, and Command Injection attacks, with reductions of 59.80%, 73.72%, and 66.96%, respectively.

title: Towards continual task learning in artificial neural networks: current approaches and insights from neuroscience
text: The innate capacity of humans and other animals to learn a diverse, and often interfering, range of knowledge and skills throughout their lifespan is a hallmark of natural intelligence, with obvious evolutionary motivations. In parallel, the ability of artificial neural networks (ANNs) to learn across a range of tasks and domains, combining and re-using learned representations where required, is a clear goal of artificial intelligence. This capacity, widely described as continual learning, has become a prolific subfield of research in machine learning. Despite the numerous successes of deep learning in recent years, across domains ranging from image recognition to machine translation, such continual task learning has proved challenging. Neural networks trained on multiple tasks in sequence with stochastic gradient descent often suffer from representational interference, whereby the learned weights for a given task effectively overwrite those of previous tasks in a process termed catastrophic forgetting. This represents a major impediment to the development of more generalised artificial learning systems, capable of accumulating knowledge over time and task space, in a manner analogous to humans. title: Towards continual task learning in artificial neural networks: current approaches and insights from neuroscience
text: The remarkable ability of humans and animals to acquire diverse knowledge and skills throughout their lives is a fundamental aspect of natural intelligence, driven by evolutionary pressures. Similarly, artificial neural networks (ANNs) aim to learn across multiple tasks and domains, combining and reusing learned representations as needed, a capability known as continual learning. This endeavor has emerged as a prominent subfield of machine learning research. Despite deep learning's recent successes in image recognition, machine translation, and other domains, continual task learning remains a significant challenge. When trained on multiple tasks sequentially using stochastic gradient descent, neural networks often exhibit representational interference, characterized by catastrophic forgetting, where learned weights for a task overwrite those of previous tasks. This limitation hinders the development of more general artificial learning systems, which aim to accumulate knowledge over time and task space, akin to human intelligence.

title: Cerebro: Static Subsuming Mutant Selection
text: Mutation testing research has indicated that a major part of its application cost is due to the large number of low utility mutants that it introduces. Although previous research has identified this issue, no previous study has proposed any effective solution to the problem. Thus, it remains unclear how to mutate and test a given piece of code in a best effort way, i.e., achieving a good trade-off between invested effort and test effectiveness. To achieve this, we propose Cerebro, a machine learning approach that statically selects subsuming mutants, i.e., the set of mutants that resides on the top of the subsumption hierarchy, based on the mutants' surrounding code context.
