Such causality allows us to observe and analyze the whole learning process in the visible low dimensional space. Technically, we propose four spatial and temporal properties and design our visualization solution to satisfy them. These properties preserve the most important information when inverse-)projecting input samples between the visible low-dimensional and the invisible high-dimensional space, for causal analyses. Our extensive experiments show that, comparing to baseline approaches, we achieve the best visualization performance regarding the spatial/temporal properties and visualization efficiency. Moreover, our case study shows that our visual solution can well reflect the characteristics of various training scenarios, showing good potential of DVI as a debugging tool for analyzing deep learning training processes.

title: DeepVisualInsight: Time-Travelling Visualization for Spatio-Temporal Causality of Deep Classification Training
text: Deep neural networks have revolutionized the field of image classification, yet their training dynamics remain poorly understood. The lack of transparency in these complex systems hinders the development of more efficient and accurate models. Existing visualization techniques focus on static representations of the model's state, neglecting the crucial temporal dimension. To address this limitation, we introduce DeepVisualInsight, a novel time-travelling visualization framework for spatio-temporal causality analysis of deep classification training. By preserving the temporal relationships between model parameters, activations, and gradients, our approach enables the identification of causal patterns and correlations that are otherwise obscured. We leverage a combination of dimensionality reduction techniques and graph-based visualization to create a compact, yet informative, representation of the training process. Our framework is capable of handling high-dimensional data and scales to large models and datasets. Experimental results on various image classification benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness of DeepVisualInsight in revealing insights into the training dynamics, such as the emergence of feature detectors, the evolution of class boundaries, and the impact of hyperparameter tuning. Furthermore, our approach facilitates the discovery of novel training strategies, including a new gradient-based regularization technique that yields significant improvements in model accuracy.

title: Neural Myerson Auction for Truthful and Energy-Efficient Autonomous Aerial Data Delivery
text: A successful deployment of drones provides an ideal solution for surveillance systems. Using drones for surveillance can provide access to areas that may be difficult or impossible to reach by humans or in-land vehicles gathering images or video recordings of a specific target in their coverage. Therefore, we introduces a data delivery drone to transfer collected surveillance data in harsh communication conditions. This paper proposes a Myerson auction-based asynchronous data delivery in an aerial distributed data platform in surveillance systems taking battery limitation and long flight constraints into account. In this paper, multiple delivery drones compete to offer data transfer to a single fixed-location surveillance drone. Our proposed Myerson auction-based algorithm, which uses the truthful second-price auction (SPA) as a baseline, is to maximize the seller's revenue while meeting several desirable properties, i.e., individual rationality and incentive compatibility while pursuing truthful operations. On top of these SPA-based operations, a deep learning-based framework is additionally designed for delivery performance improvements.

title: Neural Myerson Auction for Truthful and Energy-Efficient Autonomous Aerial Data Delivery
text: In surveillance systems, drones offer a viable solution for accessing remote or hard-to-reach areas, providing valuable visual data through image and video capture. However, transmitting this data in harsh communication environments poses a significant challenge. To address this, we present a data delivery drone designed to facilitate secure data transfer in such conditions. This paper proposes an asynchronous data delivery mechanism for aerial distributed data platforms, incorporating a Myerson auction-based approach that considers battery limitations and long flight constraints. In this framework, multiple delivery drones compete to provide data transfer services to a fixed-location surveillance drone, with the goal of maximizing revenue while ensuring individual rationality, incentive compatibility, and truthful operations. Building upon the truthful second-price auction baseline, we further introduce a deep learning-based framework to enhance delivery performance, thereby optimizing data transmission in surveillance systems.

title: Towards Fair Recommendation in Two-Sided Platforms
text: Many online platforms today (such as Amazon, Netflix, Spotify, LinkedIn, and AirBnB) can be thought of as two-sided markets with producers and customers of goods and services. Traditionally, recommendation services in these platforms have focused on maximizing customer satisfaction by tailoring the results according to the personalized preferences of individual customers. However, our investigation reinforces the fact that such customer-centric design of these services may lead to unfair distribution of exposure to the producers, which may adversely impact their well-being. On the other hand, a pure producer-centric design might become unfair to the customers. As more and more people are depending on such platforms to earn a living, it is important to ensure fairness to both producers and customers. In this work, by mapping a fair personalized recommendation problem to a constrained version of the problem of fairly allocating indivisible goods, we propose to provide fairness guarantees for both sides. Formally, our proposed {\em FairRec} algorithm guarantees Maxi-Min Share ($α$-MMS) of exposure for the producers, and Envy-Free up to One Item (EF1) fairness for the customers. Extensive evaluations over multiple real-world datasets show the effectiveness of {\em FairRec} in ensuring two-sided fairness while incurring a marginal loss in overall recommendation quality. Finally, we present a modification of FairRec (named as FairRecPlus) that at the cost of additional computation time, improves the recommendation performance for the customers, while maintaining the same fairness guarantees.

title: Towards Fair Recommendation in Two-Sided Platforms
text: Two-sided platforms, where multiple stakeholders interact and exchange value, have become ubiquitous in modern economies. Recommendation systems play a crucial role in these platforms, as they influence user behavior and shape market outcomes. However, existing recommendation algorithms often prioritize platform-centric objectives, such as maximizing engagement or revenue, over fairness considerations. This can lead to biased outcomes, perpetuating existing social and economic inequalities. We propose a novel framework for fair recommendation in two-sided platforms, which incorporates multi-stakeholder fairness constraints into the recommendation process. Our approach leverages a multi-objective optimization formulation, where we jointly optimize platform-centric objectives alongside fairness metrics that promote equal opportunities and outcomes for all stakeholders. We develop a novel fairness-aware neural network architecture, FairRec, which integrates a fairness regularizer into the learning process. This regularizer is designed to mitigate bias in the recommendation space, ensuring that the algorithm is fair and unbiased towards all stakeholders. Through a comprehensive evaluation on real-world datasets from ride-hailing and e-commerce platforms, we demonstrate that FairRec significantly improves fairness metrics, such as demographic parity and equalized odds, while maintaining competitive performance on platform-centric objectives. Our results show that FairRec reduces bias in recommendation outcomes by up to 35% compared to state-of-the-art recommendation algorithms, while improving overall platform satisfaction by up to 12%. Our work contributes to the development of socially responsible AI systems, enabling fair and inclusive two-sided platforms that benefit all stakeholders.

title: Automated 3D reconstruction of LoD2 and LoD1 models for all 10 million buildings of the Netherlands
text: In this paper we present our workflow to automatically reconstruct 3D building models based on 2D building polygons and a LiDAR point cloud. The workflow generates models at different levels of detail (LoDs) to support data requirements of different applications from one consistent source. Specific attention has been paid to make the workflow robust to quickly run a new iteration in case of improvements in an algorithm or in case new input data become available. The quality of the reconstructed data highly depends on the quality of the input data and is monitored in several steps of the process. A 3D viewer has been developed to view and download the openly available 3D data at different LoDs in different formats. The workflow has been applied to all 10 million buildings of The Netherlands. The 3D service will be updated after new input data becomes available.

title: Automated 3D reconstruction of LoD2 and LoD1 models for all 10 million buildings of the Netherlands
text: The creation of detailed 3D city models is a crucial task in various fields, including urban planning, architecture, and computer-aided design. However, manually reconstructing 3D models for large-scale urban areas is a labor-intensive and time-consuming process. In this context, the Netherlands, with its dense urban landscape and rich cultural heritage, presents a unique challenge. We propose a novel, fully automated pipeline for reconstructing 3D models of buildings at Level of Detail 2 (LoD2) and Level of Detail 1 (LoD1) for all 10 million buildings in the Netherlands. Our approach leverages a combination of publicly available 2D maps, aerial imagery, and building footprints to generate accurate 3D models. Experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves a mean absolute error of 0.55 meters for LoD2 models and 1.23 meters for LoD1 models, outperforming existing state-of-the-art approaches. The reconstructed models are available as open data, enabling various applications such as urban planning, disaster response, and virtual tourism.

title: Software and Security Engineering in Digital Transformation
text: Digital transformation is a hot topic in the current global environment as a large number of organizations have been working to adopt digital solutions. Software engineering has also emerged to be a more important role as a large number of systems, either traditional or smart, are dependent on the software that collects, store, and process data. The role of software engineers has also become crucial in digital transformation. In this regard, this paper aims to examine the trends of software engineering and the role of software engineers in digital transformation. In addition to this, this paper also examines the importance of secure software development in digital transformation. It can be concluded that software engineering is an integral part of digital transformation as all digital systems make use of software to perform their functions efficiently. Software act as a bridge between digital systems and humans to use the systems interactively and efficiently.

title: Software and Security Engineering in Digital Transformation
text: The rapid pace of digital transformation has led to a surge in the development of software-intensive systems, exacerbating the already pressing need for effective software and security engineering practices. This study investigates the interplay between software engineering and security engineering in the context of digital transformation, with a focus on identifying key challenges, opportunities, and trade-offs. We conducted a mixed-methods study, combining a systematic literature review with a survey of 150 industry professionals and 20 in-depth interviews with experts from various domains. Our analysis reveals that the integration of security engineering into software development lifecycles is hindered by inadequate risk assessment, insufficient training, and misaligned priorities. We also identify opportunities for improvement, including the adoption of DevSecOps practices, threat modeling, and continuous monitoring. Our findings have significant implications for the development of secure software systems, highlighting the need for a more holistic approach to software and security engineering in digital transformation initiatives.

title: Deep learning for location based beamforming with NLOS channels
text: Massive MIMO systems are highly efficient but critically rely on accurate channel state information (CSI) at the base station in order to determine appropriate precoders. CSI acquisition requires sending pilot symbols which induce an important overhead. In this paper, a method whose objective is to determine an appropriate precoder from the knowledge of the user's location only is proposed. Such a way to determine precoders is known as location based beamforming. It allows to reduce or even eliminate the need for pilot symbols, depending on how the location is obtained. the proposed method learns a direct mapping from location to precoder in a supervised way. It involves a neural network with a specific structure based on random Fourier features allowing to learn functions containing high spatial frequencies. It is assessed empirically and yields promising results on realistic synthetic channels. As opposed to previously proposed methods, it allows to handle both line-of-sight (LOS) and non-line-of-sight (NLOS) channels.

title: Deep learning for location based beamforming with NLOS channels
text: The proliferation of millimeter wave (mmWave) and massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems has underscored the importance of beamforming in 5G and beyond wireless networks. However, the presence of non-line-of-sight (NLOS) channels poses significant challenges to conventional beamforming techniques, which rely on precise channel state information (CSI). In this context, we explore the efficacy of deep learning (DL) in location-based beamforming, where the beamformer is optimized based on the user's location rather than CSI. We propose a novel DL architecture that integrates a convolutional neural network (CNN) with a spatial attention mechanism to learn the beam patterns from a dataset of user locations and corresponding channel responses. Our simulation results, based on a realistic 3D ray-tracing channel model, demonstrate that the proposed DL-based beamformer achieves significant gains in terms of spectral efficiency and beamforming accuracy compared to traditional model-based approaches, particularly in NLOS scenarios. The results also highlight the robustness of the DL-based approach to varying user densities and environmental conditions.

title: End-to-End Autoencoder Communications with Optimized Interference Suppression
text: An end-to-end communications system based on Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) is modeled as an autoencoder (AE) for which the transmitter (coding and modulation) and receiver (demodulation and decoding) are represented as deep neural networks (DNNs) of the encoder and decoder, respectively. This AE communications approach is shown to outperform conventional communications in terms of bit error rate (BER) under practical scenarios regarding channel and interference effects as well as training data and embedded implementation constraints. A generative adversarial network (GAN) is trained to augment the training data when there is not enough training data available. Also, the performance is evaluated in terms of the DNN model quantization and the corresponding memory requirements for embedded implementation. Then, interference training and randomized smoothing are introduced to train the AE communications to operate under unknown and dynamic interference (jamming) effects on potentially multiple OFDM symbols. Relative to conventional communications, up to 36 dB interference suppression for a channel reuse of four can be achieved by the AE communications with interference training and randomized smoothing. AE communications is also extended to the multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) case and its BER performance gain with and without interference effects is demonstrated compared to conventional MIMO communications.

title: End-to-End Autoencoder Communications with Optimized Interference Suppression
text: Deep learning has recently emerged as a promising paradigm for wireless communication systems, offering a potential solution to the long-standing problem of interference-limited transmission. In this context, we explore the application of end-to-end autoencoder communications to suppress interference in multi-user scenarios. Our approach leverages a novel optimization framework that integrates deep neural networks with traditional signal processing techniques to mitigate interference. Specifically, we design an autoencoder-based transmitter and receiver architecture, where the encoder learns to map information bits to transmission symbols, and the decoder recovers the original information from the received signals. To optimize interference suppression, we propose a joint optimization algorithm that iteratively refines the autoencoder parameters and the interference covariance matrix. Our simulations demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves significant gains in terms of symbol error rate and spectral efficiency compared to traditional interference suppression methods in various multi-user scenarios. Furthermore, we show that our optimized autoencoder architecture can adapt to changing interference environments, maintaining robust performance even when the interference statistics are unknown or time-varying. These results have important implications for the design of next-generation wireless communication systems, where machine learning-based approaches can be integrated with traditional signal processing techniques to achieve reliable and efficient communication in complex interference environments.

title: Semantic Communications: Principles and Challenges
text: Semantic communication, regarded as the breakthrough beyond the Shannon paradigm, aims at the successful transmission of semantic information conveyed by the source rather than the accurate reception of each single symbol or bit regardless of its meaning. This article provides an overview on semantic communications. After a brief review of Shannon information theory, we discuss semantic communications with theory, framework, and system design enabled by deep learning. Different from the symbol/bit error rate used for measuring conventional communication systems, performance metrics for semantic communications are also discussed. The article concludes with several open questions in semantic communications.

title: Semantic Communications: Principles and Challenges
text: Beyond the Shannon paradigm, semantic communication seeks to convey meaningful information from the source, transcending the traditional focus on accurate symbol or bit reception. This article furnishes a comprehensive examination of semantic communication, commencing with a succinct review of Shannon's information theory. We then delve into the theoretical foundations, framework, and system design of semantic communication, highlighting the pivotal role of deep learning in enabling its implementation. The article also explores novel performance metrics, distinct from conventional symbol/bit error rates, to assess semantic communication systems. Finally, it identifies several open research questions in this emerging field.

title: Repairing Adversarial Texts through Perturbation
text: It is known that neural networks are subject to attacks through adversarial perturbations, i.e., inputs which are maliciously crafted through perturbations to induce wrong predictions. Furthermore, such attacks are impossible to eliminate, i.e., the adversarial perturbation is still possible after applying mitigation methods such as adversarial training. Multiple approaches have been developed to detect and reject such adversarial inputs, mostly in the image domain. Rejecting suspicious inputs however may not be always feasible or ideal. First, normal inputs may be rejected due to false alarms generated by the detection algorithm. Second, denial-of-service attacks may be conducted by feeding such systems with adversarial inputs. To address the gap, in this work, we propose an approach to automatically repair adversarial texts at runtime. Given a text which is suspected to be adversarial, we novelly apply multiple adversarial perturbation methods in a positive way to identify a repair, i.e., a slightly mutated but semantically equivalent text that the neural network correctly classifies. Our approach has been experimented with multiple models trained for natural language processing tasks and the results show that our approach is effective, i.e., it successfully repairs about 80\% of the adversarial texts. Furthermore, depending on the applied perturbation method, an adversarial text could be repaired in as short as one second on average.

title: Repairing Adversarial Texts through Perturbation
text: The proliferation of machine learning models has led to a surge in adversarial attacks, which can manipulate input data to deceive models. In the realm of natural language processing, adversarial texts pose a significant threat to the reliability of AI systems. Existing approaches to mitigate these attacks focus on either detecting perturbations or training robust models, but neglect the crucial aspect of repairing corrupted texts. This paper bridges this gap by proposing a novel framework, termed PerturbRepair, which leverages perturbation techniques to repair adversarial texts. Our approach involves generating a set of plausible candidate repairs for a given adversarial input, followed by a ranking mechanism that selects the most coherent and fluent repair. We evaluate PerturbRepair on three benchmark datasets, showcasing its effectiveness in restoring the original semantics of corrupted texts. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of repair quality, with a 23.4% increase in BLEU score and a 17.6% improvement in ROUGE-L F1 score. Furthermore, we conduct a thorough analysis of the robustness of PerturbRepair against various types of adversarial attacks, including character-level, word-level, and sentence-level perturbations. Our findings underscore the potential of PerturbRepair as a promising defense mechanism against adversarial texts, paving the way for more reliable NLP systems in real-world applications.

title: A Deep Learning Approach to Integrate Human-Level Understanding in a Chatbot
text: In recent times, a large number of people have been involved in establishing their own businesses. Unlike humans, chatbots can serve multiple customers at a time, are available 24/7 and reply in less than a fraction of a second. Though chatbots perform well in task-oriented activities, in most cases they fail to understand personalized opinions, statements or even queries which later impact the organization for poor service management. Lack of understanding capabilities in bots disinterest humans to continue conversations with them. Usually, chatbots give absurd responses when they are unable to interpret a user's text accurately. Extracting the client reviews from conversations by using chatbots, organizations can reduce the major gap of understanding between the users and the chatbot and improve their quality of products and services.Thus, in our research we incorporated all the key elements that are necessary for a chatbot to analyse and understand an input text precisely and accurately. We performed sentiment analysis, emotion detection, intent classification and named-entity recognition using deep learning to develop chatbots with humanistic understanding and intelligence. The efficiency of our approach can be demonstrated accordingly by the detailed analysis.

title: A Deep Learning Approach to Integrate Human-Level Understanding in a Chatbot
text: Human-computer interaction has witnessed a surge in chatbot-based systems, yet, these systems often struggle to comprehend user intent, leading to frustrating experiences. To bridge this gap, we propose a novel deep learning approach that integrates human-level understanding in a chatbot. Our methodology revolves around a multi-task learning framework, where a single neural network is trained to perform both intent detection and response generation. We leverage a large-scale dataset of human-human conversations to learn a rich contextual representation of language, enabling the chatbot to capture subtle nuances in user queries. The intent detection module utilizes a hierarchical attention mechanism to focus on relevant parts of the input, while the response generation module employs a conditional variational autoencoder to produce coherent and context-specific responses. Experimental results on a benchmark dataset demonstrate significant improvements over state-of-the-art chatbot systems, with an average increase of 23.4% in intent detection accuracy and 17.1% in response relevance. Human evaluation further reveals that our chatbot is perceived as more empathetic and engaging, with 85.6% of users reporting a satisfactory experience. Our approach has far-reaching implications for developing more effective and human-centric conversational systems.

title: Cognitive Computing to Optimize IT Services
text: In this paper, the challenges of maintaining a healthy IT operational environment have been addressed by proactively analyzing IT Service Desk tickets, customer satisfaction surveys, and social media data. A Cognitive solution goes beyond the traditional structured data analysis by deep analyses of both structured and unstructured text. The salient features of the proposed platform include language identification, translation, hierarchical extraction of the most frequently occurring topics, entities and their relationships, text summarization, sentiments, and knowledge extraction from the unstructured text using Natural Language Processing techniques. Moreover, the insights from unstructured text combined with structured data allow the development of various classification, segmentation, and time-series forecasting use-cases on the incident, problem, and change datasets. Further, the text and predictive insights together with raw data are used for visualization and exploration of actionable insights on a rich and interactive dashboard. However, it is hard not only to find these insights using traditional structured data analysis but it might also take a very long time to discover them, especially while dealing with a massive amount of unstructured data. By taking action on these insights, organizations can benefit from a significant reduction of ticket volume, reduced operational costs, and increased customer satisfaction. In various experiments, on average, upto 18-25% of yearly ticket volume has been reduced using the proposed approach.

title: Cognitive Computing to Optimize IT Services
text: Proactive maintenance of a healthy IT operational environment is a formidable challenge, necessitating the integration of structured and unstructured data analysis. Our proposed Cognitive solution leverages Natural Language Processing techniques to extract valuable insights from IT Service Desk tickets, customer satisfaction surveys, and social media data. This platform boasts a range of features, including language identification, translation, topic modeling, entity relationship extraction, text summarization, sentiment analysis, and knowledge extraction. By combining these insights with structured data, we can develop various classification, segmentation, and time-series forecasting models for incident, problem, and change datasets. A rich, interactive dashboard facilitates the visualization and exploration of actionable insights, enabling data-driven decision-making. Traditional structured data analysis often falls short in uncovering these insights, particularly when dealing with large volumes of unstructured data. By acting on these insights, organizations can reap significant benefits, including reduced ticket volumes, operational costs, and enhanced customer satisfaction. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach can lead to a substantial reduction of up to 18-25% in yearly ticket volume, underscoring its potential for driving operational efficiencies.

title: Brain Signals Analysis Based Deep Learning Methods: Recent advances in the study of non-invasive brain signals
text: Brain signals constitute the information that are processed by millions of brain neurons (nerve cells and brain cells). These brain signals can be recorded and analyzed using various of non-invasive techniques such as the Electroencephalograph (EEG), Magneto-encephalograph (MEG) as well as brain-imaging techniques such as Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI), Computed Tomography (CT) and others, which will be discussed briefly in this paper. This paper discusses about the currently emerging techniques such as the usage of different Deep Learning (DL) algorithms for the analysis of these brain signals and how these algorithms will be helpful in determining the neurological status of a person by applying the signal decoding strategy.

title: Brain Signals Analysis Based Deep Learning Methods: Recent advances in the study of non-invasive brain signals
text: The analysis of non-invasive brain signals has garnered significant attention in recent years, driven by advancements in electroencephalography (EEG) and functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) technologies. This paper provides a comprehensive review of deep learning methods applied to brain signals analysis, highlighting their potential in decoding cognitive states, diagnosing neurological disorders, and developing brain-computer interfaces. We survey recent studies that leverage convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and recurrent neural networks (RNNs) to extract meaningful representations from EEG and fNIRS data, and discuss their performance gains compared to traditional machine learning approaches. Furthermore, we identify key challenges and future research directions in this rapidly evolving field.

title: Malware Classification Using Static Disassembly and Machine Learning
text: Network and system security are incredibly critical issues now. Due to the rapid proliferation of malware, traditional analysis methods struggle with enormous samples. In this paper, we propose four easy-to-extract and small-scale features, including sizes and permissions of Windows PE sections, content complexity, and import libraries, to classify malware families, and use automatic machine learning to search for the best model and hyper-parameters for each feature and their combinations. Compared with detailed behavior-related features like API sequences, proposed features provide macroscopic information about malware. The analysis is based on static disassembly scripts and hexadecimal machine code. Unlike dynamic behavior analysis, static analysis is resource-efficient and offers complete code coverage, but is vulnerable to code obfuscation and encryption. The results demonstrate that features which work well in dynamic analysis are not necessarily effective when applied to static analysis. For instance, API 4-grams only achieve 57.96% accuracy and involve a relatively high dimensional feature set (5000 dimensions). In contrast, the novel proposed features together with a classical machine learning algorithm (Random Forest) presents very good accuracy at 99.40% and the feature vector is of much smaller dimension (40 dimensions). We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through integration in IDA Pro, which also facilitates the collection of new training samples and subsequent model retraining.

title: Malware Classification Using Static Disassembly and Machine Learning
text: The proliferation of malware has necessitated the development of efficient and effective classification techniques to combat the growing threat to cybersecurity. Traditional signature-based approaches are often inadequate, as they rely on prior knowledge of malware patterns. In response, machine learning-based methods have gained traction, leveraging static and dynamic analysis to identify malicious code. However, these approaches often suffer from high computational overhead and limited generalizability. This study proposes a novel malware classification framework that integrates static disassembly with machine learning. Our approach extracts a rich set of features from disassembled malware binaries, including opcode frequencies, control flow graph characteristics, and API call patterns. These features are then fed into a hybrid machine learning model, combining the strengths of random forests and gradient boosting machines. Evaluating our approach on a curated dataset of 10,000 malware samples, we achieve an accuracy of 97.4% and a false positive rate of 2.1%, outperforming state-of-the-art techniques. Notably, our framework demonstrates improved robustness against code obfuscation and packing, common evasion techniques employed by malware authors. Furthermore, our feature importance analysis reveals that opcode frequencies and control flow graph metrics are highly discriminative, providing valuable insights for future research. Our results have significant implications for the development of practical and effective malware detection systems, and our framework is readily adaptable for real-world deployment.

title: Enhancing CryptoGuards Deployability for Continuous Software Security Scanning
text: The increasing development speed via Agile may introduce overlooked security steps in the process, with an example being the Iowa Caucus application. Verifying the protection of confidential information such as social security numbers requires security at all levels, providing protection through any connected applications. CryptoGuard is a static code analyzer for Java. This program verifies that developers do not leave vulnerabilities in their applications. The program aids the developer by identifying cryptographic misuses such as hard-coded keys, weak program hashes, and using insecure protocols. In my Master's thesis work, I made several important contributions to improving the deployability, accessibility, and usability of CryptoGuard. I extended CryptoGuard to scan source and compiled code, created live documentation, and supported a dual cloud and local tool-suite. I also created build tool plugins and a program aid for CryptoGuard. In addition, I also analyzed several Java-related surveys encompassing more than 50,000 developers and reported interesting current practices of real-world software developers.

title: Enhancing CryptoGuards Deployability for Continuous Software Security Scanning
text: The proliferation of DevOps practices has necessitated continuous software security scanning to ensure the integrity of modern software systems. CryptoGuards, a prominent static analysis tool, has been instrumental in identifying vulnerabilities in cryptographic implementations. However, its deployability remains a significant concern, hindering its widespread adoption in continuous integration and delivery pipelines. This paper presents a systematic approach to enhance CryptoGuards' deployability, focusing on reducing its computational overhead and improving its scalability. We propose a novel, parallelizable architecture that leverages GPU acceleration and optimized data structures to reduce the analysis time by an average of 73%. Our evaluation on a dataset of 150 open-source projects demonstrates a significant reduction in false positives, with a precision of 92.5% and recall of 95.2%. Furthermore, our approach enables real-time scanning of large codebases, making it suitable for continuous integration environments. The enhanced CryptoGuards framework has been successfully integrated into a popular CI/CD platform, ensuring seamless security auditing and compliance monitoring.

title: Exploring Spreadsheet Use and Practices in a Technologically Constrained Setting
text: This paper explores the impacts of spreadsheets on business operations in a water utility parastatal in Malawi, Sub-Saharan Africa. The organisation is a typical example of a semi-government body operating in a technologically underdeveloped country. The study focused on spreadsheet scope of use and life cycle as well as organisational policy and governance. The results will help define future spreadsheet usage by influencing new approaches for managing potential risks associated with spreadsheets in the organization. Generally, findings indicate that the proliferation of spreadsheets in the organization has provided an enabling environment for business automation. The paper also highlights management, technological and human factor issues contributing to high risks associated with the pervasive spreadsheet use. The conclusions drawn from the research confirms that there is ample room for improvement in many areas such as implementation of comprehensive policies and regulations governing spreadsheet development processes and adoption.

title: Exploring Spreadsheet Use and Practices in a Technologically Constrained Setting
text: In the context of a water utility parastatal in Malawi, Sub-Saharan Africa, this study examines the implications of spreadsheet utilization on business operations. As a semi-governmental entity operating in a technologically underdeveloped country, the organization presents a paradigmatic case. Our investigation delves into the scope and lifecycle of spreadsheet use, as well as organizational policy and governance. The findings of this research are poised to inform future spreadsheet adoption strategies, mitigating potential risks associated with their use. Notably, the widespread adoption of spreadsheets has fostered an environment conducive to business automation. However, our analysis also reveals managerial, technological, and human factor concerns that contribute to elevated risks. Ultimately, our conclusions underscore the need for comprehensive policies and regulations governing spreadsheet development and implementation, highlighting avenues for improvement in this regard.

title: Demand-Driven Asset Reutilization Analytics
text: Manufacturers have long benefited from reusing returned products and parts. This benevolent approach can minimize cost and help the manufacturer to play a role in sustaining the environment, something which is of utmost importance these days because of growing environment concerns. Reuse of returned parts and products aids environment sustainability because doing so helps reduce the use of raw materials, eliminate energy use to produce new parts, and minimize waste materials. However, handling returns effectively and efficiently can be difficult if the processes do not provide the visibility that is necessary to track, manage, and re-use the returns. This paper applies advanced analytics on procurement data to increase reutilization in new build by optimizing Equal-to-New (ETN) parts return. This will reduce 'the spend' on new buy parts for building new product units. The process involves forecasting and matching returns supply to demand for new build. Complexity in the process is the forecasting and matching while making sure a reutilization engineering process is available. Also, this will identify high demand/value/yield parts for development engineering to focus. Analytics has been applied on different levels to enhance the optimization process including forecast of upgraded parts. Machine Learning algorithms are used to build an automated infrastructure that can support the transformation of ETN parts utilization in the procurement parts planning process. This system incorporate returns forecast in the planning cycle to reduce suppliers liability from 9 weeks to 12 months planning cycle, e.g., reduce 5% of 10 million US dollars liability.

title: Demand-Driven Asset Reutilization Analytics
text: Environmental sustainability has become a pressing concern, and manufacturers can contribute to this effort by reusing returned products and parts, thereby minimizing raw material consumption, energy expenditure, and waste generation. Effective reuse, however, hinges on the ability to track, manage, and optimize the returns process. This research applies advanced analytics to procurement data to enhance the reutilization of Equal-to-New (ETN) parts in new build, thereby reducing expenditures on new parts. The proposed approach involves forecasting and matching returns supply with demand for new build, while ensuring the availability of a reutilization engineering process. Additionally, this framework identifies high-demand, high-value, and high-yield parts for development engineering to focus on. To enhance optimization, analytics are applied at multiple levels, including forecasting upgraded parts. Machine Learning algorithms are employed to create an automated infrastructure that supports the integration of ETN parts utilization into the procurement parts planning process. By incorporating returns forecasting into the planning cycle, this system reduces suppliers' liability from 9 weeks to 12 months, resulting in a significant reduction of 5% of a $10 million liability. This research demonstrates a data-driven approach to optimizing returns management, ultimately contributing to a more sustainable and cost-effective manufacturing process.

title: Software Engineering Meets Network Engineering: Conceptual Model for Events Monitoring and Logging
text: Abstraction applied in computer networking hides network details behind a well-defined representation by building a model that captures an essential aspect of the network system. Two current methods of representation are available, one based on graph theory, where a network node is reduced to a point in a graph, and the other the use of non-methodological iconic depictions such as human heads, walls, towers or computer racks. In this paper, we adopt an abstract representation methodology, the thinging machine (TM), proposed in software engineering to model computer networks. TM defines a single coherent network architecture and topology that is constituted from only five generic actions with two types of arrows. Without loss of generality, this paper applies TM to model the area of network monitoring in packet-mode transmission. Complex network documents are difficult to maintain and are not guaranteed to mirror actual situations. Network monitoring is constant monitoring for and alerting of malfunctions, failures, stoppages or suspicious activities in a network system. Current monitoring systems are built on ad hoc descriptions that lack systemization. The TM model of monitoring presents a theoretical foundation integrated with events and behavior descriptions. To investigate TM modeling s feasibility, we apply it to an existing computer network in a Kuwaiti enterprise to create an integrated network system that includes hardware, software and communication facilities. The final specifications point to TM modeling s viability in the computer networking field.

title: Software Engineering Meets Network Engineering: Conceptual Model for Events Monitoring and Logging
text: Abstract representation in computer networking enables the concealment of intricate network details behind a well-defined interface, thereby facilitating the development of a model that captures the essence of the network system. Existing representation methods can be broadly categorized into two approaches: graph theory-based models, which reduce network nodes to graph points, and non-methodological iconic representations, which employ metaphors such as human heads, walls, towers, or computer racks. This paper explores the application of the "thinging machine" (TM) methodology, originally proposed in software engineering, to model computer networks. The TM paradigm defines a unified network architecture and topology comprising five generic actions and two types of arrows, ensuring a coherent representation without loss of generality. We instantiate TM in the context of packet-mode transmission network monitoring, which involves continuous surveillance for malfunctions, failures, and suspicious activities. Current monitoring systems often rely on ad hoc descriptions, lacking systematization. In contrast, the TM model of monitoring provides a theoretical foundation that integrates event and behavior descriptions. To validate the feasibility of TM modeling, we apply it to an existing computer network in a Kuwaiti enterprise, yielding a comprehensive network system encompassing hardware, software, and communication facilities. The results demonstrate the viability of TM modeling in the computer networking domain.

title: Predicting Succinylation Sites in Proteins with Improved Deep Learning Architecture
text: Post-translational modifications (PTMs) in proteins occur after the process of translation. PTMs account for many cellular processes such as deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) repair, cell signaling and cell death. One of the recent PTMs is succinylation. Succinylation modifies lysine residue from $-1$ to $+1$. Locating succinylation sites using experimental methods, such as mass spectrometry is very laborious. Hence, computational methods are favored using machine learning techniques. This paper proposes a deep learning architecture to predict succinylation sites. The performance of the proposed architecture is compared to the state-of-the-art deep learning architecture and other traditional machine learning techniques for succinylation. It is shown from the performance metrics that the proposed architecture provides a good trade-off between speed of computation and classification accuracy.

title: Predicting Succinylation Sites in Proteins with Improved Deep Learning Architecture
text: Succinylation, a crucial post-translational modification, plays a vital role in regulating various cellular processes. Despite its importance, identifying succinylation sites in proteins remains a challenging task. Existing machine learning approaches suffer from limited accuracy, largely due to the lack of robust feature representations and inadequate modeling of complex patterns. We propose a novel deep learning architecture that integrates convolutional and recurrent neural networks to capture both local and global protein sequence information. Our approach leverages a large-scale dataset of experimentally validated succinylation sites and achieves a significant improvement in prediction accuracy, outperforming state-of-the-art methods by 12.5% in terms of F1-score. Moreover, our model provides insights into the underlying mechanisms of succinylation, revealing novel sequence motifs and functional associations.
